jobs.title: Tupande Health, Safety, Security, and Transport (HSST) Coordinator
jobs.description:
## Job Description

Seeking a strategic leaders to lead Transport, OSH, and Security operations. You will manage a team, drive efficiency and compliance, and optimize budgets to ensure a safe, cost-effective environment for Tupande staff and partners.

## Job Level

JL 5

## Location

Kakamega, Kenya

## Expected Manager

Ignetius Mukokho

## Will this position be managing others?

Yes, One Transport and Dispatch Senior Supervisor JL4 and three Senior Transport Officers JL2

## Key Job Responsibilities

Manage the Transport workstream.

- Oversee transport workstream daily operations to maintain high-quality standards and exceptional service provision.
- Implement and audit transport workstream management systems to maintain expected performance standards.
- Manage the transport workstream assets through their life cycle for adequate work resourcing.
- Manage large and minor transport workstream projects, ensuring timely completion and customer satisfaction.
- Act as the primary decision-maker for day-to-day transport operational roadblocks, resolving driver or vehicle issues that the supervisors cannot handle.
- Enforce transport policies and maintenance schedules, ensuring the supervisors keep vehicles compliant, clean, and roadworthy.

Support the Occupational Safety and Health workstream

- Engage with relevant internal and external stakeholders to plan, implement, and complete annual OSH audits and related training.
- Organize all audit reports and training certificates for ease of sharing with relevant stakeholders
- Support in overseeing the OSH compliance for all relevant Tupande locations across all our regions of operation.
- Coordinate the implementation of all OSH audit recommendations to ensure 100% implementation rate across all audited locations.

Support Security Operations

- Act as the primary daily contact for the Vendor Security Manager regarding routine deployment updates, ad-hoc requests, and immediate operational issues.
- Validate the daily/weekly reports submitted by the security service provider against the internal observations to ensure "ghost guards" or missed shifts are flagged before invoicing.
- Follow up with the vendor's technical team on maintenance and track their turnaround time to ensure they meet the maintenance Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
- Collaborate with the Security service provider during initial incident responses; ensure the vendor’s Incident Reports capture the full internal context and accuracy required.
- Track recurring performance issues to provide data and talking points for the HSST lead during the monthly stakeholder sync-ups.
- Coordinate with the security vendor to ensure access control protocols are being enforced on the ground as per Tupande’s policy across all locations.

Budget and Cost Management

- Collate and track expenditure data for Transport, OSH, and Security to assist in budget analysis.
- Analyse HSST workstream expenditure to develop strategies to manage or reduce recurring expenses while maintaining quality.
- Support in preparation of monthly BvA reports for leadership review.
- Monitor budget levels to curb overspends and achieve 10% budget savings annually.
- Review vendor invoices against LPOs to ensure accurate vendor payments

People Management

- Recruit the right team members to fill any personnel gaps.
- Identify and facilitate opportunities for professional growth and development.
- Develop and train the team on HSST workstream performance metrics so they know what success in their roles looks like.
- Track, audit, and report on HSST workstream performance metrics to ensure the team achieves performance expectations.
- Identify potential future leaders within the team and develop their skills to prepare them for leadership roles.
- Foster a collaborative and inclusive workplace culture, implementing initiatives to boost team morale and motivation.

## Top Skills and Qualifications

Technical skills:

- Google Suite applications, i.e., Google Sheets and Google Docs.
- Proficiency in software and systems that manage and track transport operations.
- Experience with tools used for raising PRs and managing vendor payments.

Knowledge:

- Knowledge of fleet management and logistics principles, including route efficiency, scheduling maintenance, conducting safety checks, and ensuring proper vehicle performance.
- Familiarity with safety regulations and compliance standards in the transport industry.
- Knowledge of applicable safety regulations and transport industry-specific compliance requirements.
- Knowledge of OSHA and safety regulations in Kenya.
- Ability to conduct a Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment to assist the HSST Lead.
- Knowledge of fire suppression systems and evacuation drill protocols.
- Understanding of security and basic access controls, technology and regulation
- SLA management and understanding of how to hold private security firms accountable to Guard Force Instructions (GFIs).

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Sponsor International Candidates

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

12 November 2026. Applications after this date will be accepted on a rolling basis.

*For more information reach out to ignetius.mukokho@oneacrefund.org*

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Grants Coordinator
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

The IRC is implementing programs in the West Bank and Gaza working closely with partners and implementing directly in health, protection, WASH, early childhood development, and cash programming to meet the most critical humanitarian needs.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Grants Coordinator is responsible for the timely and effective management of a multi-donor grant portfolio. This position manages all functions of the grants unit at IRC oPt, inclusive of proposal development, reporting, donor compliance, and other administration.

The Grants Coordinator reports to the Deputy Director for Programs (DDP) The position will work closely with the MEAL Coordinator, Partnerships Coordinator, finance department, and program sector leads.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Proposal Development**

- In collaboration with the DDP and HQ colleagues, proactively identify new funding opportunities by monitoring and analyzing donor strategies and funding trends.
- Support the DDP and program sector leads in the development of new program design.
- Prepare for and lead Go/No Go meetings for funding opportunities as required.
- Assist in ensuring that Go/No Go discussions and program design are consistent with the SAP partnership ambition and program approach.
- In coordination with the Partnerships Coordinator, proactively engage partners in program development efforts.
- Ensure robust and effective representation and resourcing of IRC’s partnership strategy, approach and management in donor proposals and reports.
- Oversee the development of all concept notes and proposals, acting as or delegating responsibility for lead writer or editor. Develop efficient process management tools for proposal development.
- Outline and communicate clear roles and responsibilities and timelines for each department. Facilitate effective cross-departmental coordination.
- Thoroughly review all proposal documents to ensure coherence throughout narratives, logframes, and budgets.
- Act as focal point with HQ during proposal review, editing, and submission.
- Ensure all proposal outputs are accurate, complete, of high quality, and submitted on time.

**Grants Management**

- Act as focal point for communications with HQ on all grants administration functions.
- Review donor agreements and coordinate their review and signature with relevant HQ offices. Coordinate the approval of pre-award spending as required.
- Coordinate with the Partnership Lead to obtain any necessary donor approvals relating to partnerships.
- Lead and/or support all project revisions, amendments, and budget realignments.
- In close coordination with Finance team, facilitate BvAs to bring teams together to ensure sound financial management
- Serve as the country program expert on the facilitation of Project Cycle Meetings (PCM), including project design, opening, implementation, closing, and learning meetings.
- Actively promote full partner participation in program delivery in the context of PCM.
- Maintain and disseminate a regularly updated grants tracker.
- Ensure all departmental communication with IRC colleagues and donors is constructive, clear, and organized.
- Maintain a well-organized and comprehensive information management and grants filing system.
- Ensure IRC’s internal Opportunity Tracking Information System (OTIS) is updated and maintained throughout the awards lifecycle
- Participate in due diligence processes and collaborative partnership risk management as appropriate.
- Strengthen the capacity of IRC and partner staff in grants management functions by facilitating trainings and providing targeted support as required.

**Donor Compliance**

- Provide programs and operations teams with routine technical guidance to ensure that all grants are implemented in compliance with IRC and donor regulations.
- Coordinate with HQ on specialized compliance matters as required.
- Proactively raise potential compliance issues to senior management; work closely with HQ compliance colleagues to resolve any related concerns.
- Disseminate existing resources on donor compliance, liaise with regional counterparts for the development and updating of compliance cheat sheets for all grants.
- In coordination with the DDP and Advocacy Coordinator, assist in ensuring appropriate and effective IRC and donor visibility in program sites and materials.

**Reporting**

- Oversee the development and delivery of all internal and external reports in collaboration with the programs, finance, and MEAL departments.
- Maintain a comprehensive reports tracker and regularly communicate with all relevant team members about upcoming deadlines and specific report requirements.
- Lead the production of high-quality and well-written reports which meet donor and IRC requirements.
- Thoroughly review and confirm that all reports and supplementary documents are complete and accurate.
- Coordinate HQ and technical unit reviews and approvals prior to donor submission.
- Ensure strict compliance with internal and donor deadlines.

**Departmental Leadership and Staff Management**

- Lead the grants unit and provide professional development opportunities for staff as needed.
- Ensure clear delineation of roles and responsibilities and logical portfolio allocation for all team members.
- Coordinate performance management within the department and ensure a culture of high performance through staff engagement and accountability.
- Identify and support capacity building of grants team and as requested other team members to understand IRC’s Grants processes
- Oversee recruitment of new staff as required. Ensure comprehensive onboarding and training for new hires.

**Other**

Other relevant duties as assigned by supervisor to further IRC programs.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- Between five - six years of experience in humanitarian grants management in a multi-donor, multi-sector working environment.
- Demonstrated experience in an inter-departmental coordination role and the ability to communicate with and balance the priorities of a range of stakeholders.
- Extensive experience leading the development of large multi-sector funding proposals.
- Advanced skills in donor report drafting and compilation, including the coordination of inputs and development of complex documents across different departments.
- In-depth knowledge of institutional donor compliance required. Knowledge of ECHO, SIDA, GFFO, BMZ and Gulf donor requirements a particular advantage.
- Exceptional English writing and editing skills required. Able to draft and edit detailed documents for donor submission with minimal oversight.
- Previous experience in a conflict-affected or protracted crisis setting preferred.
- Exceptional advance planning and organizational skills. Able to effectively prioritize and follow multiple activities and deadlines simultaneously.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated positive attitude that can positively and constructively engage across programmatic and support departments

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances

**IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer.** IRC considerall applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: SOUTH SUDAN -HUMAN RESSOURCES HEAD OF DEPARTMENT - JUBA
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/02/2026**
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**
**Location: Juba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context.

\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement, this year El Nino), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.

\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.

\- South Sudan has also been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. As of October 2026, more than 1,400,000 people have entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).

\- In 2025 internal tensions increased at government level and have led to wide spread conflicts within the country. Elections at the end of 2026 may raise further division and tensions.

\- An Ebola outbreak is currently at its doors in DRC and Uganda.

As a result, 10 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2026.

SI sectors of intervention:

\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors. SI has also been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Recent fundings have allowed increasing significantly the FSL component on the mission

Areas of operation:

SI is present:

\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Renk, Malakal and Ulang (since 2025). The response has focused on cholera, response to acute food insecurity and drought while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.

\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team (ERRM) based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.

Size of operations:

In 2026, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 8 million, and 140 employees following an ongoing scale up since 2025.

The mission is currently funded by ECHO (3 grants), CDCS, FIFSAN, SSHF, Norway MoFA, FCDO.

'The mission is currently in the last step of a scale up phase with approx 120 staffs, aiming at reaching 140 staffs. Coordination team will soon be around 30 staffs

The HR team is 1/ HR Coordinator+ 1 Deputy Human Resource Coordinator and one HR Assistant

## About the job

**General objective:**

The HR Head of Department oversees the implementation of Solidarités International’s (SI) Human Resources framework and policies within the Country Team, ensures the smooth administrative running of the Country Office and that all staff comply with SI procedures, donor procedures and the laws of the country concerned. They regularly visit field offices to ensure the harmonisation and application of these procedures across the entire Country Office.

They are the point of contact within the Country Office for all matters relating to human resources, and acts as the liaison between headquarters and the Country Office on these matters.

**The main challenges:**

- Manage a team that needs support
- Complex and demandind labor aurhorities with different specificities depending on the location
- Growing teams in all bases that need follow up on HR procedures
- Creation of Policies on missing procedures
- Communication with other NGOs in the country
- Strong collaboration with other departments for various issues
- Follow up with a high number of expats on their documentation and off-boardings when needed

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

- Stabilize the Private Insurance payments and follow ups
- Stabilize the Shared Cost processes to be on time
- Follow up on revised DW Policy, updated function grid & salary grid
- Visit the bases and introduce himself/herself to the teams and to authorities

**Security constraints:**

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates.

The situation in South Sudan is volatile, please document yourself before applying. SI is adapting the set up in real time as context evolves

There is one driver available on evenings and 2 on weekends for movements out of office hours.

Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).

In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are limited

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : BA in Psychology, Business Administration or similar, MA in HR preferable

Experience in the humanitarian sector : More than 5 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. HOMERE user and familiarity with SI HR tools preferable
2. Good and comfortable to use Excel
3. HR Policies: Applying them consistently, be rigorous on identifying needs for new policies and create them
4. Able to handle sensitive cases with outmost professionalism and confidentiality

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Clear, effective, sensitive communication
2. Build positive relations
3. Confidentiality and Discretion
4. Cultural Awareness within the country
5. Rigor and attention to details

**LANGUAGES**

1. English necessary
2. Arabic is a bonus

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The HR Head of Department will be living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs. With the scale up, different options are being considered and

some staffs may also be hosted at another NGO nearby.

Individual room in the guesthouse, with electricity 24/7 and generator during specific time. NB: During field visits, living conditions are much more basic.

Juba, as the capital of South Sudan offers a good variety of markets, supermarkets, restaurants, and bars.

jobs.title: Chef(fe) de base – Consolidation de la paix, à Birao (République centrafricaine)
Responsable Logistique CTE - Nord Kivu- RDC
jobs.description:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA**

**L’ESPRIT ALIMA :** La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées surla proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de l’éthique médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients et aux patientes, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.

**LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :**

- Le patient et la patiente d’abord
- Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire
- Responsabilité et liberté
- Améliorer la qualité de nos actions
- Faire confiance
- L’intelligence collective
- La responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposés ou avérés. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

- Respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude ;
- Signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents cadre et procédure à une supérieure, un supérieur, une référente, un référent.

**SOIGNER - INNOVER - ENSEMBLE :** Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a touché plus de 18 millions de bénéficiaires dans 15 pays, principalement en Afrique. En 2024, nous avons développé 59 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté. L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers les structures de santé (dont hôpitaux et centres de santé). Notre action découle d’une adaptation constante aux réalités du terrain et aux progrès de la médecine. En 2024, ALIMA a atteint 5,9 millions de bénéficiaires. Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients et patientes bénéficient de l’expertise là où elle se trouve, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques notamment dans le domaine de la lutte contre la malnutrition et les fièvres virales hémorragiques.

**L'ÉQUIPE ALIMA :** plus de 2000 personnes œuvrent actuellement pour ALIMA. Les équipes terrain, au plus proche des patients, reçoivent leur support des équipes de coordination généralement basées en capitale des pays d’intervention. Celles-ci reçoivent le support des 4 équipes desk et de l’équipe du service urgences et ouvertures basées au siège opérationnel de Dakar, Sénégal. Les équipes de Paris et New-York travaillent activement à la collecte de fonds ainsi qu’à la représentation d’ALIMA. Le reste de la Galaxie ALIMA comprend des individus et des équipes partenaires qui travaillent pour le compte d’autres organisations telles que les ONGs médicales BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, les organismes de recherche PACCI, INSERM, INRB, les Universités de Bordeaux ou de Copenhague, l’ONG Solidarités International et bien d’autres.

**NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET :** Malnutrition, Santé sexuelle et reproductive incluant les violences basées sur le genre, Santé Primaire et secondaire, la chirurgie, les soins pédiatriques, les maladies tueuses tel que Paludisme, IRA, Diarrhée, Épidémies (Fièvres hémorragiques, méningite, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue, Covid-19).

**NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS :** Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Ethiopie, Haïti, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Guinée, Soudan du Sud, Sénégal, Mauritanie et Soudan.

**ALIMA**

ALIMA dispose d’une présence opérationnelle en Ituri depuis 2022, notamment dans les Zones de Santé de Bunia et de Rwampara, et bénéficie d’une bonne connaissance du contexte et des acteurs sanitaires locaux. Dès la déclaration de l’épidémie d’Ebola, ALIMA a activé son dispositif d’urgence, mobilisé ses équipes et ses stocks prépositionnés, et obtenu l’accréditation de l’Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) pour participer officiellement à la riposte. ALIMA possède une expertise reconnue dans la gestion des épidémies de fièvres hémorragiques virales en RDC et à l’international. L’organisation a joué un rôle majeur lors de plusieurs flambées d’Ebola en RDC (11e à 16e épidémies) ainsi qu’en Guinée, en Ouganda, en Guinée Équatoriale et au Rwanda, à travers la prise en charge des cas, la surveillance, la prévention et contrôle des infections (PCI) et le renforcement des capacités des personnels de santé.

Depuis 2020, ALIMA s’appuie sur un plan national de préparation et de réponse aux fièvres hémorragiques virales lui permettant de déployer rapidement du personnel qualifié et des ressources médicales et WASH. L’organisation est également à l’origine du concept CUBE (Chambre d’Urgence Bio Sécurisée pour Épidémies), une innovation reconnue internationalement pour la prise en charge sécurisée des patients atteints de maladies hautement infectieuses. Plus récemment, ALIMA a participé à la réponse à la précédente épidémie d’Ebola à Bulape ainsi qu’à la riposte contre l’épidémie de Mpox en RDC en 2024–2025, confirmant sa capacité à intervenir rapidement et efficacement dans les urgences sanitaires majeures.

**LIEU DE MISSION :** Nord Kivu avec déplacement

**PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ**

**Niveau 3 :** Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et à être en contact avec des enfants et/ou des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

**LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES**

Il·Elle rend compte au Coordo Projet Urgence (responsable hiérarchique) et Coordo Logistique (responsable technique)

Il collabore avec tous les autres membres de la mission

**MISSIONS ET ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

**1. Suivi de l’activité et définition des objectifs**

- Décrit et analyse son activité dans son environnement : mission explo, besoin en construction, circuit patient - staff - déchet, besoin en fleet, base, stock, etc…
- Compile les données quantitatives logistiques (consommations, stocks, distributions) et les analyse avant transmission au coordinateur logistique,
- Rédige la partie logistique des rapports pour son activité (sitrep mensuel),
- Identifie les acteurs locaux faisant partie de son environnement de travail : autorités locales, ONG, prestataires de services, fournisseurs. Création ou maintien des relations favorables de travail avec ces interlocuteurs.
- Avec les responsables d’activité médicaux et le coordinateur de projet, détermine les besoins pour les structures appuyées du projet en eau, hygiène et assainissement, et biens de première nécessité.
- Avec les responsables d’activité médicaux et le coordinateur de projet, détermine les besoins nouveaux, de maintenance ou d’approvisionnement pour les infrastructures médicales (énergie, éclairage, matériel, consommables) et pour les logements et bureaux de l’équipe .
- Participe à d’éventuelles missions exploratoires ou d’évaluation.
- Participe aux discussions sur la conduite du projet et la définition des objectifs.
- Est responsable de la mise en place et respect des procédures et règles sécuritaires

**2. Mise en œuvre des programmes**

**2.1. Secours non médicaux :**

- Supervise la chaîne de traitement des déchets (collecte, tri, destruction, décharge) dans les structures soutenues en collaboration avec le responsable log WASH.
- S’assure du respect des mesures bio-sécurités mises en places
- Supervise l’approvisionnement en biens de première nécessité (kits) en collaboration avec le Responsable Approvisionnement.
- Veille à la mise en sécurité des installations et des bâtiments (présence d’extincteurs, mise à la terre des installations électriques, etc…) en collaboration avec le coordinateur logistique et le district sanitaire.

***(Ces responsabilités comprennent les étapes de planification, mise en œuvre et supervision)***

**2.2. Secours médicaux :**

- Sur la base des besoins définis pour les structures médicales, propose à la coordination des solutions, évalue les moyens à mettre en œuvre, établit des devis détaillés et propose un plan d’action.
- Organiser et superviser les travaux décidés.
- Organiser et superviser la maintenance et l’entretien des infrastructures et du matériel .

**3. Gestion des ressources humaines**

**3.1. Composition des équipes :**

- Organiser le recrutement du personnel dans son activité (avec l’appui du Coordinateur RH et le coordinateur Logistique).
- Organiser avec les superviseurs le remplacement du personnel absent.

**3.2. Encadrement des équipes :**

- Organiser et superviser le travail des membres de son équipe.

**CONDITIONS**

**Prise de poste :**

**Salaire :** SALAIRE TRÈS COMPÉTITIF + EXPÉRIENCE + PER DIEM

jobs.title: PIR Caseworker
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. The role works closely with clients, internal teams, and external partners to develop and implement individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients to appropriate financial, medical, social, vocational, and community resources in alignment with program requirements, eligibility guidelines, and IRC standards.

**Major Responsibilities:**
**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure clients have access to housing, food, medical care, transportation, and community orientation.
- Conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery and public transportation orientation, and other field-based services to address immediate client needs.
- Purchase and transport program-related items; lift, move, and deliver materials necessary for service delivery.
- Conduct client intake assessments and develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with clients.
- Provide ongoing case management through direct services, referrals, advocacy, and coordination with internal and external service providers.
- Monitor client progress toward established goals, identify barriers, and adjust service plans as needed.
- Document all client interactions accurately and in compliance with program requirements; enter and maintain client data in required databases and tracking tools.
- Support Preferred Communities programming and intensive case management services, as assigned.
- Collaborate with colleagues across programs and grants to ensure clients access all eligible services.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and service providers.
- Participate in program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with grant requirements.
- Use a personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation to travel within the service delivery area as needed.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required.
- Experience providing casework, pre-arrival, or intensive case management services preferred.
- Demonstrated experience navigating program eligibility requirements and ensuring accurate service documentation.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, diplomacy, and networking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to use digital tools for data entry, research, and reporting.
- Ability to lift and carry items weighing 50+ pounds, including furniture and household goods.
- Ability to drive a large van or passenger vehicle, as required for program delivery.

**Working Environment**

**This position operates in a hybrid environment that includes office-based work, remote work, and fieldwork within the service delivery area. Typically, the role is based in the office four days per week and remotely one day per week, with field responsibilities possible on all workdays. Schedule flexibility is required, including occasional evenings and weekends for activities such as airport pick-ups.**

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $120 per month, dental starting at $7 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Compensation:( 20.97$/hourly**): Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Needs Assessment Consultant - Venezuela
jobs.description:
Relief International (RI) is seeking an experienced consultant or consulting firm to conduct a comprehensive needs assessment following the recent earthquake in Venezuela. The assessment will inform RI's decision on whether and how to establish a rehabilitation-focused programme and longer-term presence in the country.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities affected by conflict, climate change, and disasters to save lives, strengthen resilience, and support long-term health and wellbeing. RI works across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, delivering programmes in Health, Nutrition, WASH, Education, and Livelihoods.

**The Opportunity**

Following an earthquake that has impacted communities and health services in Venezuela, RI is exploring potential humanitarian interventions focused on physical rehabilitation and assistive technology. We are seeking a consultant or firm to lead an evidence-based assessment that will identify priority needs, evaluate existing services and referral pathways, assess market and supply-chain feasibility for assistive technologies, and provide practical recommendations for future programming.

The consultancy will include desk review, service mapping, primary data collection, analysis, stakeholder engagement, and final reporting.

**Scope of the Assessment**

The assessment will focus on:

- Rehabilitation needs of earthquake-affected populations.
- People with pre-existing disabilities whose access to care has been disrupted.
- Individuals with newly acquired impairments resulting from earthquake-related injuries.
- Access to physical rehabilitation services, prosthetics and orthotics (P&O), assistive technology, and relevant mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services.
- Existing service capacity, referral pathways, and partnership opportunities.
- Market availability and feasibility of assistive technologies, including spectacles, hearing aids, and other priority devices.

**Key Responsibilities**

The successful consultant or firm will:

- Design and implement the assessment methodology.
- Conduct secondary data review and stakeholder mapping.
- Lead qualitative primary data collection, including key informant interviews and focus group discussions.
- Assess rehabilitation service availability, accessibility, and continuity of care.
- Evaluate assistive technology markets, suppliers, and supply chains.
- Analyze findings and identify priority needs and service gaps.
- Develop feasible programme options and recommendations for RI.
- Facilitate a validation workshop with RI stakeholders.
- Produce high-quality reports and decision-making materials.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

Essential

- Significant experience conducting humanitarian needs assessments, health assessments, disability inclusion assessments, or similar assignments.
- Strong technical expertise in physical rehabilitation and continuity of care.
- Knowledge of prosthetics and orthotics (P&O) services and assistive technology provision.
- Experience assessing health systems, referral pathways, service gaps, and partnership opportunities.
- Proven qualitative research and analytical skills.
- Demonstrated ability to develop practical programme recommendations and indicative costings.
- Excellent report-writing skills.
- Ability to work independently and manage assessment activities within tight deadlines.

Desirable

- Experience in Venezuela or comparable contexts in Latin America.
- Professional proficiency in Spanish and English.
- Experience working with rehabilitation providers, Ministries of Health, OPDs, or humanitarian coordination mechanisms.
- Experience assessing assistive technology markets and procurement pathways.
- Familiarity with HD-NEST, Washington Group Questions, or other disability-inclusive assessment tools.
- Experience supporting organizations entering new geographic contexts.

**Consultancy Details**

**Location:** Venezuela (assessment locations to be proposed and agreed with RI)
**Duration:** Approximately 7-8 weeks from contract signature
**Expected Period:** November to December 2026

**Job Title:** Driver - Odesa (Ukrainian Nationals Only)

**Line Management Responsibility:** None

**Position Type:** Full-time

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organization. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**OVERVIEW:**

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014/2015 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022. NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The driver is a member of the Operations Team responsible for providing transport and logistics assistance to the mission under the direction of the Operations Manager and fleet officer. This includes transporting team members to meetings and other activities and care and management of maintenance of NP vehicles. It also involves assisting with the procurement and delivery of goods for the team of NP as well as any other activities relevant to the role. NP will offer armored vehicle training and safe driver training.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Transport:**

- Follow NP safety and security guidelines for drivers.
- Keep passengers and pedestrians safe.
- Treat vehicle properly and avoid damage caused by reckless driving.
- Keep vehicle in good condition, including regular cleaning.
- Not to authorise any passenger to travel in the vehicle who is unrelated to the work.
- Maintain fuel levels in the vehicle in line with SOPs.
- Perform daily service and weekly vehicle inspections and report any problems immediately.

**Procurement and logistics:**

- Assist the Logistics Officer, Field Programme Officer and Caretaking staff with procuring supplies and undertaking collection/delivery as directed
- Assist in general maintenance activities around the office

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

**Education, Knowledge and Experience:**

- Strong commitment to safety and security
- Commitment to humanitarian principles (humanity, non-partisanship, impartiality and independence) and the work of Nonviolent Peaceforce in Ukraine
- Experience as a driver, knowledge of basic vehicle maintenance

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES:**

**Independent Judgment/Analytical:**

- Ability to manage information with discretion and confidentiality
- Ability to set priorities, solve problems and devise practical solutions

**Interpersonal:**

- Flexible, energetic and adaptable
- Ability to work in a multicultural environment
- Proven ability to build relationships

**Vehicle Maintenance**:

- Basic emergency field repairs
- Basic maintenance under direction from the fleet officer
- Basic fault finding

**Language:**

- The ability to interact confidently with colleagues in **English and Ukrainian language** is a significant advantage

**Other Specialized Requirements:**

- Driving license **category C1** is preferable, **category B** is the minimum requirement

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector.NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [Inter](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/) [Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE**

**We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted** [**here**](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/) **on our website.**

jobs.description:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

MSI needs an experienced and ambitious strategic partnerships leader to establish our new Global Strategic Partnerships team. Building on significant success with our existing strategic funder partners, they will deepen those partnerships and add at least 1-2 additional strategic funding partnerships by 2030. They will play a key role in advancing MSI’s brand and reputation through the lens of our high impact relationships – positioning MSI as one of the lead go-to INGOs for partners looking for audacious, bold, sector - shaping innovators and acting as a public advocate on the reasons why MSI is highly valued in this way.

MSI’s high-performing team has successfully grown relationships and funding portfolios with 2-3 large, impact-focused foundation funders, who collectively contribute £50m+/year to MSI’s donor funding and view MSI as their SRHR partner of choice. We are looking for a dynamic leader with a deep understanding of impact-focused funding, extensive connections across the social impact landscape and a track record of growing strategic funding partnerships with large, complex and highly engaged funders at the £10m+/year level, who can take MSI’s strategic funding partnerships to the next level, positioning MSI for growth and mission impact in a rapidly evolving funding landscape. Aligned with MSI’s ownblended social business delivery model, new strategic partners may come from a range of sectors including foundations, corporates, donor advised funds or public-private initiatives.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- Deep understanding of social impact funder priorities and ways of working, especially those focused on maximising impact at scale.
- Proven ability to network, engage and co-create new high impact global partnerships at the highest level.
- Ability to work confidently across teams to accelerate delivery of priority, cross-cutting initiatives that meet the needs of strategic funders/corporate partners.
- Excellent communication skills - excellent verbal and written English communication skills and ability to organize and present information in a compelling way for a social impact leadership audience
- Strategic thinker with evidenced ability to influence funder future direction and maximise the alignment of funder and MSI strategies
- Strong coaching and capacity building skills

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- Experience of securing and leading durable strategic funder partnerships at the £10m+ level
- Extensive network amongst international social impact funders and implementers
- Experience of leading and motivating high-performing teams
- Experience of working for or in partnership with a service delivery social impact organisation (the successful candidate may have worked on the funder side or implementer side)
- Excellent communication skills, including significant flair in written communication and a strong understanding of visual modelling and graphical representation of ideas. You will demonstrate the ability to shape responses to technically complex problems and ideas, whilst also being able to simply summarize the core concept/s.

**Formal education/qualification**

- No formal educational requirement, qualification through experience is sufficient for the role

Please see the job description [here](https://www.msichoices.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Director-of-Global-Strategic-Partnerships-2026.pdf)

**Location:** London, UK (minimum of 2 days per week in the office), or any country where MSI operates

**Full-time:** 35 hours a week, Monday to Friday for UK based candidates

**Contract type:** Permanent

**Salary**: £80,700 - £100,000 per annum commensurate with experience + bonus + benefits for UK based candidates.

**For candidates based in a different MSI country, the salary will be banded within the local national context.**

**Salary band: BG 12**

**Closing date: 18th November 2026 (midnight GMT).** Interviews may take place before this date for exceptional candidates.

jobs.title: GBV/VAW Specialist Trainer - Consultancy
jobs.description:
**1. Background**

MiCT is implementing “Words That Protect” project that supports gender-responsive journalism and more responsible media coverage of violence against women in Iraq.

to strengthen collaborative journalism and gender-responsive reporting on violence against women (VAW) in Iraq. Component 2 combines media monitoring and baseline research, capacity building for Iraqi journalists, supported story production, and reflection on reporting practices.

The research examines how Iraqi media cover gender-based violence (GBV) and VAW, including terminology, framing, source selection, contextualisation, and the representation of survivors. Its findings will inform capacity-building activities and provide a reference for assessing reporting produced through the project.

MiCT seeks a GBV/VAW Expert and trainer to support the interpretation of research findings, review terminology and thematic accuracy, and deliver one day within the capacity-building workshop.

**2. Objective of the Assignment**

To strengthen the conceptual accuracy and survivor-centred approach of the project’s research interpretation and training, and improve participating journalists’ understanding of gender, GBV/VAW, and the social dynamics that shape violence against women in Iraq.

**3. Scope of Work**

The expert will undertake the following tasks in coordination with the Project Lead, research team, and lead trainer.

**A. Research interpretation and technical review — two working days**

Review the research findings with the research team to verify gender and GBV/VAW terminology, strengthen conceptual accuracy and interpretation in the Iraqi context, and identify key messages for training. Provide consolidated written feedback with recommended revisions.

**B. Training delivery — one working day**

Deliver 1 day training within the Component 2 workshop covering gender and power relations, forms and root causes of VAW, harmful norms and misconceptions, and survivor-centred principles, including consent, confidentiality, and avoiding secondary harm.

**C. Preparation and reporting — two working days**

Coordinate with the research team and lead trainer, prepare the session plan and supporting materials, and submit a concise report summarising the contribution, key observations, and recommendations.

The allocation of these two days between preparation and reporting will be agreed in the consultancy workplan.

**4. Deliverables**

Deliverables will be submitted to MiCT for review and acceptance in coordination with the Project Lead. Exact submission dates will be agreed in the consultancy workplan.

- **Research review feedback:** Consolidated comments on terminology, conceptual accuracy, and interpretation, with recommended revisions and key messages for training.
- **Training plan and materials:** A session plan, presentation, and practical exercises for the agreed training day.
- **Delivery of one training day:** Facilitation of the agreed gender and GBV/VAW sessions within the capacity-building workshop.
- **Final assignment report:** A concise summary of support delivered, key observations, and recommendations.

**6. Coordination and Responsibilities**

The expert will work under the supervision of the Project Lead and coordinate closely with the research team and lead trainer. MiCT will provide relevant research materials, the workshop framework, participant information, and project templates.

**7. Required Qualifications and Experience**

- Relevant academic qualification in gender studies, social sciences, human rights, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Demonstrated expertise in gender equality, GBV/VAW, and survivor-centred approaches.
- Strong understanding of the Iraqi context, including social norms and barriers faced by survivors.
- Experience reviewing research findings and translating complex concepts into accessible learning materials.
- Experience designing and delivering participatory training for adult audiences.
- Excellent spoken and written Arabic.
- Ability to coordinate with the project team and review relevant materials in English.

Previous work with journalists or media development programmes is an advantage. Journalism expertise is not required.

**8. Confidentiality and Ethical Standards**

The expert must maintain the confidentiality of unpublished research, project documents, and participant information. All contributions must uphold survivor dignity, privacy, informed consent, and the Do No Harm principle. Training examples must avoid disclosing identifying or sensitive information about survivors.

jobs.title: Logistics Officer (Ukrainian Nationals only)
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Logistics Officer

**Department:** Operations

**Division:** Logistics & Procurement

**Duty Station:** Odesa, Ukraine

**Line Manager:** Logistics Coordinator

**Technical Line Manager:** Senior Logistics Officer

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Full-time

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**OVERVIEW:**

The role is within the Nonviolent Peaceforce - Ukraine Country office (CO) to provide a central support service to multiple departments. We are looking for someone with a passion for organisation and accuracy looking to use their skills in complex administration, multi-tasking and problem-solving to make an impact on NP’s administrative and operational duties.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Logistics Officer provides operational and administrative support to the Country Office and all field offices, focusing on procurement, rental and lease agreements, logistics-related payments, cost tracking, and documentation. The role ensures accurate and timely processing of procurement and payment requests, compliance with organizational procedures and donor requirements, and effective communication with field teams, Finance, suppliers, and service providers.

This varied role, will require a high-level of organisational, communication and IT skills to provide a key central support function to various teams: HR, Finance and the Field teams, in particular the Field Programme Officers (FPO).

The role supports the Country Office and all field offices with administrative and operational duties. This includes performing a variety of administrative tasks, including management of office and accommodation contracts, management of the office administration.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

1\. **Commitment to NP Principles:**

- Demonstrate a commitment to NP’s mandate and principles.
- Maintain a positive image of the organisation full-time while communicating with external actors, staff or operating in the field.

2\. **Support to Logistics:**

- Process procurement of goods and services valued below USD 10,000 for the Country Office and all field offices, including simple procurement and procedures requiring BID analysis.
- Research the market, collect and compare supplier quotations, and update the vendor list to support purchasing decisions.
- Arrange procurement for office facilities and premises-related needs, compare options for value for money, and prepare the required contractual documentation.
- Check facility-related contracts and service providers, follow up on service quality and delivery issues, and report any non-compliance with agreed terms.
- Prepare and follow up on monthly payments for utilities, facility services, consumables, and office supplies required by the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Prepare vehicle lease agreements for the Country Office and all NP field offices, follow up on negotiations and signatures, and track renewals and contract implementation.
- Follow up on payments under fuel supply agreements for vehicle refuelling across the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Arrange and track payments for vehicle servicing, maintenance, and repairs for the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Prepare and follow up on monthly payments for rented premises, including offices, hubs, and guesthouses, across the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Check that payment processing and supporting documents comply with NP policies, procurement procedures, delegated approval limits, contractual terms, and donor requirements where applicable.
- Prepare monthly requests and supporting documents for office-related costs, including rent, utilities, telephone services, and other recurring charges, and check them for completeness and compliance with organizational procedures.
- Support monthly cost planning and forecasting by collecting and consolidating information on rent, utilities, facility services, fuel, vehicle maintenance, and other recurring logistics expenses across the Country Office and field offices.
- Track submitted, pending, overdue, and completed payments; follow up on delays with Finance and suppliers; and update the relevant trackers and stakeholders.
- Check invoices and payment requests against the relevant contract, purchase order, delivery or service confirmation, approved budget, and payment terms; clarify discrepancies before submission.
- File payment and procurement records in the relevant SharePoint folders and provide required hard copies to Finance, including BID analyses and payment tracking documents.
- Compile and verify procurement records and update the Purchase Request (PR) tracker with the latest status.
- File logistics documents in the relevant SharePoint folders and arrange for required hard copies to be retained by Finance, including BID analyses, payment documents, and payment trackers.
- Maintain a consolidated payment calendar for recurring and contractual costs, track due dates, and notify relevant colleagues of upcoming deadlines or missing documents.
- Carry out other logistics duties assigned by the Senior Logistics Officer or Logistics Coordinator\*\*.\*\*

3\. **Support to Administration:**

- Update tracking tools and databases for recurring monthly costs, procurement progress, lease agreements, and other operational records.
- Serve as the contact point for office and accommodation lease agreements and related technical services, and assist with drafting and reviewing rental contracts.
- Check contract balances, advance payments, deposits, and outstanding liabilities for assigned services and premises, and flag discrepancies and upcoming renewals or expiries in good time.
- Collect and consolidate monthly payment requests from field offices, check submissions for completeness and consistency, and return incomplete or unclear requests to the relevant focal points for correction.
- Keep in regular contact with Field Team Leaders and FPOs to identify upcoming operational needs, confirm expected costs, resolve documentation issues, and support the timely submission of payment requests.
- Inform Field Team Leaders, FPOs, and relevant budget holders about payment delays, contract or supplier issues, missing approvals, and actions required from them.
- Send documents to the relevant teams and follow up to ensure they reach the appropriate staff for review, approval, and filing.
- Prepare complete and accurate payment packages for Finance, checking that supporting documents are available, approvals are in place, and payment details are correct.
- Liaise with Finance and budget holders to check budget availability, budget codes and donor allocations, required approvals, and the status of submitted payments.
- Provide administrative assistance to the Logistics team as required.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

- High school diploma.
- Good knowledge and understanding of the conflict context in Ukraine expected.
- Highly proficient in the use of Microsoft applications, in particular Word & Excel, other applications an asset. High level of computer literacy, knowledge of Salesforce a significant benefit.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

- Experience working in NP or similar organisation.
- Familiarity with INGO logistics and administration structure and function with preferred experience within NP.

**KEY CHALLENGES:**

- Building and sustaining collaborative partnerships, negotiating, and resolving contentious issues and conflicts of interest while managing and balancing varied, diverse stakeholder priorities across a geographically dispersed region.

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES:**

- Experience in I/NGO administration, office management, procurement and/or logistics.
- Good knowledge and understanding of the conflict context in Ukraine expected.
- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal in English and Ukrainian.
- Excellent problem-solving and analytical abilities.
- Ability to work effectively in a team and independently.
- Ability to manage information with discretion.
- Independent Judgment/Analytical: Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data.

**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

- This country office position includes travel to field locations (Kramatorsk, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv and Kherson) and may include challenging living conditions, limited access to amenities, and potentially unstable and changeable security situations.
- You must be prepared to live in basic accommodation, which may include shared housing during travel and field site support tasks.
- Demonstrated ability to adhere to strict security protocols and maintain high level of discipline.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector. NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [Inter](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/) [Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE**

**We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted** [**here**](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/) **on our website.**

jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

The Accounting & Payments Coordinator supports One Acre Fund DRC’s operations by ensuring timely, accurate and properly authorized payments, complete expense documentation, and reliable financial records across all program sites.

## **Responsibilities**

Payment Processing

- Review payment requests submitted by departments to verify their completeness, accuracy, supporting documentation and required approvals, in accordance with internal policies.
- Determine the appropriate payment method—bank transfer, cheque, cash or an approved mobile money channel—based on internal procedures, transaction requirements, security considerations and available funds.
- Prepare bank transfers, cheques and other payment instructions for authorized approval and release;
- Monitor payments through to confirmation, investigate failed or delayed transactions, and retain proof of payment.
- Support Procurement in assessing supplier payment arrangements, including payment methods, advances and payment upon delivery
- Keep requesting departments informed of payment status, missing requirements and anticipated delays, including changes affecting agreed service timelines.

Expense Documentation and Advance Reconciliation

- Maintain a tracker of staff and supplier advances, including responsible parties, supporting documentation requirements, reconciliation deadlines and outstanding balances.
- Collect and review advance reconciliations and expense reports to confirm that expenditure is supported by a complete, valid and consistent documentation package.
- Follow up with suppliers on outstanding invoices, billing discrepancies and requests for clarification, coordinating with Procurement and requesting departments as needed.
- Escalate overdue reconciliations, unresolved discrepancies and recurring documentation gaps to the manager.
- Maintain an organized and accessible archive of payment and expense records, linking requests, approvals, invoices, receipts, reconciliation forms and proof of payment in accordance with document retention requirements.

Cash Management

- Act as custodian of the Kinshasa office cashbox, ensuring secure custody of funds, disbursement against approved documentation, timely recording of transactions and daily cash balancing.

Account Reconciliation

- Perform weekly reconciliations of sales collections received through mobile money, where applicable, against transaction records and related settlements.
- Maintain accurate accounting trackers, including the lease repository, fixed asset register, register of non-capitalized equipment, etc.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- SYCEBNL knowledge and application
- Excel / Google Sheets proficiency

- Attention to detail and financial control judgment

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, paid time off

## **Contract Duration**

1 year

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Democratic Republic of Congo.

28 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.
