**Contract type:** Consultancy contract (100%)

**Contract duration:** 1.1.2027 – 31.12.2027

**Reporting to:** Humanitarian Desk, Solidar Suisse Headquarters, Switzerland

**Eligibility:** Open to Venezuelan nationals and other applicants who are legally authorised to work in Venezuela and are currently residing in the country (no relocation support)

**Background**

Solidar Suisse is a Swiss non-governmental organisation founded in 1936, formerly known as Swiss Labour Assistance. The organisation is committed to promoting social justice, decent work and equal opportunities and implements humanitarian and development programmes across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe.

Following the earthquake that struck Venezuela in June 2026, Solidar Suisse launched an initial humanitarian response to support affected communities. Building on this first intervention, Solidar Suisse is now preparing a new humanitarian project focusing on WASH and Protection in Caracas and La Guaira.

In line with Solidar Suisse’s commitment to locally led humanitarian action, the project will be implemented in close partnership with two Venezuelan organisations with strong expertise in WASH and Protection respectively. Each partner will lead implementation in its core sector, while contributing complementary expertise to the overall response. Solidar Suisse will retain overall responsibility for the project and provide oversight, coordination and quality assurance through a lean in-country structure.

**Position Purpose**

Solidar Suisse is seeking a qualified and adaptable Project Manager and Technical Advisor for Protection to oversee the effective implementation of its humanitarian project in Venezuela.

The position is responsible for the overall management, coordination, monitoring and quality assurance of the project, as well as for providing technical guidance on Protection. The position holder will supervise two Solidar Suisse project staff and will work closely with both local partner organisations, supporting them in planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, compliance and organisational coordination.

The successful applicant must be comfortable working across different areas of responsibility and responding flexibly to changing project needs. The position requires a hands-on professional who can combine project management, partner accompaniment, technical guidance, team supervision, external coordination and field-level problem-solving.

**Main Responsibilities**

**Project Management and Implementation**

- Lead and oversee the overall implementation of the humanitarian project in accordance with the approved proposal, budget, workplan and partnership agreements.
- Ensure that project activities are implemented on time, within budget and in accordance with agreed objectives, indicators and quality standards.
- Coordinate implementation across the Protection and WASH components of the project.
- Maintain a comprehensive overview of project progress, challenges, risks, expenditure and required follow-up.
- Identify implementation gaps or delays and work with the partner organisations and Solidar Suisse Headquarters to develop practical solutions.
- Ensure that project implementation complies with donor requirements, Solidar Suisse policies, humanitarian principles and applicable standards.
- Coordinate project revisions and adjustments when required.
- Ensure that appropriate project documentation and records are maintained.

**Partner Coordination and Support**

- Serve as the principal operational focal point for the two local implementing partners.
- Maintain regular communication and coordination with partner management and project teams.
- Guide and support the partners throughout project planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting.
- Review partner workplans, activity plans, reports and other project documentation.
- Support partners in meeting agreed programme, financial, safeguarding, accountability and compliance requirements.
- Facilitate joint planning, reflection and problem-solving processes.
- Identify partner support and capacity-strengthening needs and coordinate appropriate follow-up.
- Promote a respectful, transparent and collaborative partnership approach.
- Ensure that roles, responsibilities, expectations and communication channels between Solidar Suisse and the partners remain clear throughout implementation.

**Technical Guidance on Protection**

- Provide technical guidance and oversight for the project’s Protection component.
- Support the Protection partner in developing and adapting technically sound implementation approaches.
- Review Protection activities, tools and project documentation and provide practical recommendations for improvement.
- Ensure that Protection activities are implemented in line with humanitarian principles, relevant Protection standards, safeguarding requirements and the do-no-harm approach.
- Support the integration of protection principles across the wider project, including the WASH component.
- Promote safe, inclusive and accessible programming for different population groups.
- Support appropriate accountability, participation, confidentiality and referral practices.
- Identify technical quality concerns and work with the partner to establish and monitor corrective actions.

**Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Reporting**

- Monitor project performance against the approved results framework, indicators, targets, workplan and budget.
- Conduct regular monitoring visits to project locations and partner activities.
- Assess the quality and relevance of implementation and agree on follow-up actions with the respective partner.
- Support the collection, verification and analysis of project monitoring information.
- Ensure that monitoring processes consider programme quality, accountability, safeguarding and protection-related risks.
- Review narrative reports and supporting documentation submitted by the partners.
- Prepare accurate and timely internal updates and contribute to donor reporting.
- Document implementation challenges, lessons learned, good practices and recommendations.
- Promptly report significant programme, financial, operational, compliance, safeguarding or security concerns to Solidar Suisse Headquarters.

**Financial and Compliance Oversight**

- Monitor project expenditure in cooperation with the relevant partner and Solidar Suisse finance colleagues.
- Follow up on expenditure against the approved budget and flag potential over- or underspending.
- Support partners in understanding and meeting financial, procurement and documentation requirements.
- Review the consistency between implemented activities, reported results and related expenditure.
- Contribute to budget forecasting, financial planning and project revisions.
- Support compliance with contractual obligations, donor conditions, partnership agreements and internal control requirements.

**Team Management**

- Directly supervise two Solidar Suisse staff members.
- Establish clear roles, priorities and performance expectations.
- Provide regular guidance, feedback, coaching and practical support.
- Ensure effective coordination and information-sharing within the project team.
- Promote a professional, respectful, accountable and collaborative working environment.
- Support staff development and address performance or operational challenges in a timely manner.

**Coordination and Representation**

- Represent Solidar Suisse in relevant coordination meetings, technical working groups and consultations.
- Maintain professional relationships with local authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, civil society organisations and other relevant stakeholders.
- Participate in relevant Protection and humanitarian coordination mechanisms.
- Coordinate with relevant WASH actors when required to support coherent implementation across both project components.
- Monitor contextual and humanitarian developments that may affect the project.
- Provide Solidar Suisse Headquarters with regular updates on the operating context, implementation environment, risks and emerging needs.
- Contribute to strengthening Solidar Suisse’s presence, relationships and understanding of the humanitarian context in Venezuela.

**Risk Management, Safeguarding and Accountability**

- Monitor contextual, operational, programme, safeguarding and security risks affecting project implementation.
- Support the development and application of practical risk mitigation measures.
- Ensure that partners understand and apply relevant safeguarding and accountability requirements.
- Promote accessible and confidential feedback and complaints mechanisms.
- Escalate serious concerns or incidents through the appropriate reporting channels.
- Support safe and conflict-sensitive implementation across all project activities.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Contribute to organisational learning and the further development of Solidar Suisse’s humanitarian engagement in Venezuela.
- Undertake other reasonable duties necessary for the effective implementation of the project and humanitarian response.
- Respond flexibly to changing project priorities and operational needs.

**Candidate Profile**

- University degree in humanitarian action, international development, social sciences, human rights, law, social work or another relevant field.
- At least five years of progressively responsible professional experience in humanitarian or development programming.
- Demonstrated experience managing humanitarian or development projects, including workplanning, monitoring, budget follow-up and reporting.
- Relevant experience in Protection programming and a sound understanding of protection principles, safeguarding, accountability and the do-no-harm approach.
- Experience working with and supporting national or local civil society organisations.
- Experience guiding partners and strengthening programme implementation through practical accompaniment, mentoring and constructive follow-up.
- Previous staff supervision or team management experience.
- Experience with donor-funded projects and related quality, reporting and compliance requirements.
- Ability to coordinate different technical and operational components within one project.
- Strong analytical, organisational and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities and respond constructively to changing circumstances.
- Willingness and ability to undertake regular field travel.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to work respectfully with diverse partners and stakeholders.
- Full professional proficiency in Spanish and English, both written and spoken.
- Good command of Microsoft Office applications.
- Good knowledge of the Venezuelan humanitarian and institutional context.

jobs.title: Field Monitoring Coordinators Third-Party Monitoring, DRC Humanitarian Fund
jobs.description:
**Background**

SoCha is preparing a proposal to provide independent third-party monitoring services for projects financed through the DRC Humanitarian Fund, administered by UNOCHA.

Monitoring activities will be conducted across seven priority provinces: North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Tanganyika, Maniema, Haut-Uélé and Bas-Uélé, as well as other locations where required.

The assignment will involve independent verification of humanitarian project implementation, including field visits, interviews with implementing partners and beneficiaries, observation of project activities, document reviews and remote verification where physical access is constrained.

SoCha seeks qualified Field Monitoring Coordinators to supervise and facilitate field monitoring activities within designated geographic areas.

**Position Summary**

The Field Monitoring Coordinator will be responsible for planning, coordinating and supervising TPM field activities within assigned provinces or deployment areas.

Working under the direction of the Team Leader, the Coordinator will oversee field monitors and enumerators, support operational access and logistics, ensure compliance with approved monitoring methodologies, and maintain the quality, timeliness and integrity of field data collection.

The Coordinator will play a central role in ensuring that SoCha can conduct credible, independent monitoring in insecure, remote and operationally challenging environments.

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. Field Monitoring Planning and Coordination**

- Support the development of project-specific mission plans, including site selection, sampling, monitoring methods, field schedules and resource requirements.
- Coordinate the deployment of field monitors and enumerators to assigned project locations.
- Liaise with implementing partners and relevant local stakeholders to facilitate field access and monitoring arrangements, while preserving the independence of verification activities.
- Organize field logistics, including transport, accommodation, communications and equipment, in coordination with SoCha's operations personnel and approved partners.
- Ensure field activities are conducted in accordance with approved mission plans, security procedures and contractual timelines.
- Support rapid mobilization for urgent or unplanned monitoring assignments.

**B. Supervision of Field Monitoring Teams**

- Supervise field monitors and enumerators operating within assigned geographic areas.
- Provide field teams with orientation on monitoring objectives, tools, sampling procedures, ethical standards and reporting requirements.
- Ensure consistent application of approved data collection methodologies across monitoring sites.
- Monitor field team performance, identify operational challenges and implement corrective measures.
- Provide technical guidance and troubleshooting support during fieldwork.
- Conduct field debriefings and consolidate monitoring observations and emerging findings.

**C. Independent Verification and Data Collection**

- Oversee the verification of humanitarian activities, outputs and assistance reported by implementing partners.
- Supervise field observations, key informant interviews, focus group discussions, beneficiary consultations and document reviews.
- Ensure appropriate verification of reported results against project records, physical evidence, beneficiary accounts and other relevant sources.
- Support the collection of geotagged photographs and other documentary evidence, subject to informed consent and safeguarding requirements.
- Ensure monitoring activities appropriately consider gender, disability inclusion, protection, accountability to affected populations and other cross-cutting issues.
- Identify discrepancies, implementation gaps, beneficiary concerns and other issues requiring follow-up.
- Support remote verification when physical access is restricted and alternative approaches have been approved.

**D. Field Data Quality Assurance**

- Review data collected by field monitors for completeness, consistency and adherence to approved methodologies.
- Work with the Data Analyst to identify and resolve missing information, inconsistencies and potential data-integrity concerns.
- Ensure monitoring teams submit data and supporting evidence through approved digital systems.
- Maintain appropriate field records, including site visit documentation, interview records, evidence logs and monitoring notes.
- Ensure findings are supported by verifiable evidence and distinguish confirmed observations from unverified claims.
- Contribute to the preparation of verification matrices and project monitoring reports.

**E. Security, Access and Operational Risk Management**

- Maintain current knowledge of access conditions, security risks and operational constraints in assigned provinces.
- Support the preparation of context-specific security assessments, movement plans, communication protocols and contingency arrangements.
- Ensure field teams comply with approved security and access procedures, including go/no-go decisions.
- Monitor changes in security, displacement, disease outbreaks and other factors affecting field operations.
- Promptly communicate security incidents, access restrictions and other operational concerns to the Team Leader.
- Support the identification of safe and feasible alternative monitoring arrangements where necessary.
- Maintain appropriate working relationships with local organizations and community networks that can facilitate access, without compromising monitoring independence.

**F. Safeguarding, Ethics and Accountability**

- Ensure all field monitoring activities comply with humanitarian principles, informed consent, confidentiality, Do No Harm and relevant safeguarding requirements.
- Ensure field monitors are trained in PSEA, protection-sensitive interviewing, data protection and ethical data collection.
- Promote safe, inclusive and voluntary participation of beneficiaries in monitoring activities.
- Ensure sensitive information is handled securely and shared only through authorized channels.
- Immediately escalate serious safeguarding concerns and other critical findings in accordance with approved reporting protocols.
- Identify and disclose potential conflicts of interest affecting field monitoring activities.

**G. Reporting and Communication**

- Provide regular field progress updates to the Team Leader, including completed activities, operational constraints, emerging findings and follow-up needs.
- Contribute to initial mission debriefings and the preparation of TPM reports.
- Prepare concise field summaries, including verified observations, discrepancies, beneficiary feedback and operational limitations.
- Support responses to UNOCHA feedback and requests for additional verification.
- Participate in coordination meetings, team reviews and lessons-learning activities as required.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- University degree in social sciences, research methods, humanitarian affairs, development studies, public administration or a related discipline.
- Relevant professional experience in humanitarian monitoring, field research, data collection or programme evaluation. The proposed team of Field Monitoring Coordinators must have a combined average of at least three years of relevant experience.
- Demonstrated experience supervising field monitors, enumerators or community-based data collection teams.
- Experience conducting or coordinating field research in humanitarian or development contexts.
- Strong understanding of qualitative and quantitative data collection methods, including interviews, focus group discussions, surveys and direct observation.
- Familiarity with digital data collection tools such as Kobo Toolbox, ODK or comparable platforms.
- Demonstrated knowledge of the geographic, logistical, security and community context of the proposed deployment area.
- Ability to coordinate field activities in insecure, remote or hard-to-reach locations.
- Understanding of safeguarding, PSEA, informed consent, confidentiality and ethical data collection requirements.

**Language Requirements**

- Proficiency in written and spoken French is required.
- Proficiency in the relevant local languages of the assigned deployment area, including Swahili, Lingala or other applicable languages, is required.
- Working proficiency in English is an advantage.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- More than five years of relevant humanitarian monitoring or field research experience.
- Previous experience coordinating TPM or independent verification assignments for UN agencies, humanitarian organizations or major donors.
- Established professional experience and operational networks in one or more of the seven priority provinces.
- Experience supervising monitoring activities in conflict-affected, displacement-affected or epidemic-affected settings.
- Familiarity with humanitarian interventions across several sectors, including Health, Nutrition, Protection, Food Security, Shelter/NFI, WASH, Education and CCCM.
- Experience implementing remote or community-based verification approaches.
- Training in field security, humanitarian protection, PSEA, research ethics and data protection.

**Expected Deliverables**

The Field Monitoring Coordinator will be responsible for:

- Inputs to project-specific mission plans, field schedules and access arrangements.
- Mobilization and supervision of field monitoring teams.
- Completed field monitoring activities in accordance with approved methodologies.
- Field progress updates and mission debriefing notes.
- Reviewed and verified field datasets and supporting evidence.
- Field monitoring summaries, including findings, discrepancies and operational limitations.
- Inputs to TPM reports, verification matrices and follow-up actions.
- Documentation of security and access constraints and recommended mitigation measures.

**Reporting and Working Arrangements**

The Field Monitoring Coordinator will report directly to the Team Leader and work closely with the Data Analyst, field monitors, SoCha's operational personnel and approved local partners.

At least five Field Monitoring Coordinators will be required across the assignment, collectively providing operational coverage of all seven priority provinces.

Coordinators will be expected to maintain operational readiness within their assigned deployment areas and travel to monitoring locations as required, subject to approved security and access procedures.

The precise level of effort and contractual arrangements will be determined by SoCha, consistent with the requirements of the final contract.

jobs.title: Country Director, Sudan
jobs.description:
Do you have the judgement, resilience, and leadership skills to guide an organisation through one of the world's most challenging operational environments?

Sudan presents an exceptionally complex humanitarian and development context. As Country Director, you will lead a dedicated team, navigate uncertainty and risk, build strong partnerships, and ensure that NCA continues to deliver meaningful programmes for communities affected by conflict and displacement.

We are looking for an experienced and grounded leader who can make sound decisions under pressure, **exercise prudence in complex and high-risk situations**, strengthen people and teams, and maintain strategic direction in a rapidly changing environment. Are you the leader we are looking for?

**About the position**

As Country Director, you will have overall responsibility for NCA's Sudan Country Programme and provide strategic leadership and oversight across programmes, operations, finance, security, and people management.

Reporting to the Head of Geographic Division for East Africa, you will lead a diverse Country Management Team and represent NCA in dialogue with authorities, donors, partners, and relevant coordination forums.

This is a senior leadership role combining strategic direction with the ability to navigate operational complexity, security risks, organisational change, and the realities of delivering humanitarian and development programmes in a conflict-affected context.

**Key responsibilities**

As Country Director, you will:

- Lead the strategic direction and implementation of NCA's Sudan Country Programme.
- Drive programme quality, impact, and accountability across the humanitarian and development portfolio.
- Lead and develop the Country Management Team and foster a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing organisational culture.
- Ensure effective security management, risk mitigation, safeguarding, and duty of care for staff and partners.
- Oversee financial management, compliance, resource allocation, and the organisational sustainability of the country programme.
- Represent NCA with donors, authorities, partners, and relevant coordination mechanisms.
- Identify opportunities and lead resource mobilisation efforts to sustain and develop the programme portfolio.
- Guide the organisation through change, uncertainty, and operational complexity while maintaining strategic focus.

**Qualifications and experience**

We are looking for a senior leader with substantial experience from international humanitarian and/or development work. You should have:

- A master's degree in international development, humanitarian action, political science, public administration, management, or another relevant field. Extensive and relevant professional experience may compensate for formal education.
- Significant senior leadership experience managing complex humanitarian and/or development programmes in fragile, conflict-affected, or high-risk environments.
- Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary teams, organisational change processes, and performance improvement.
- Proven experience with donor relations, resource mobilisation, financial oversight, risk management, and representation with senior external stakeholders.

Experience living and working in complex, fragile, or conflict-affected environments will be highly relevant. We also value a strong understanding of conflict sensitivity, localisation, and partnership-based programming.

Professional fluency in English is essential, while knowledge of Arabic is a significant advantage. You should also have strong digital literacy and be comfortable using technology for management, communication, and organisational oversight.

The position requires willingness and ability to undertake field travel in challenging operating environments and to live in shared accommodation in accordance with NCA's Sudan set-up.

**Personal qualities**

To succeed in this role, we believe you are:

**Strategic and decisive**

You make sound and timely decisions in complex and uncertain situations. You exercise strong judgement and balancing decisive action with careful consideration of security, financial, and organisational risks, while bringing conflictsensitivity to your decisions.

**A people-centred leader**

You invest in people and teams, build trust and accountability, and create the conditions for collaboration, learning, and strong performance.

**Resilient and adaptable**
You remain composed and effective when circumstances change rapidly. You can navigate setbacks and uncertainty without losing sight of strategic priorities.

**A diplomatic and influential communicator**
You build constructive relationships across cultures and stakeholder groups. You communicate with clarity and credibility and are comfortable representing the organisation at senior levels.

**What we offer**

This is an opportunity to lead one of NCA's most strategically important and challenging country programmes.

You will work alongside dedicated national and international colleagues and strong local partners to support communities affected by conflict, displacement, and crisis.

NCA offers a meaningful senior leadership role with significant responsibility and professional autonomy, as well as the opportunity to shape organisational impact in a highly dynamic environment. You will be part of a values-driven international organisation and supported by colleagues across NCA's country programmes and Head Office.

If you combine strategic leadership with resilience, **prudence, sound judgement, decisiveness, and a genuine commitment to people and partnerships**, we would like to hear from you.

**Ethical Commitments**

Norwegian Church Aid is committed to high standards of ethics and accountability in all that we do. As an employee, you will be required to sign the following documents when entering into an employment contract:

- **ACT Alliance Code of Conduct**
- **Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, Harassment, and Child Safeguarding Policy**

These are binding documents for all employees. We therefore ask you to familiarise yourself with them before applying. You can find the documents on our website: [https://www.kirkensnodhjelp.no/etterettelighet](https://www.kirkensnodhjelp.no/etterettelighet)

**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

Prospect Development drives our high-value private sector fundraising by providing the data-driven insights needed to advance donors and prospects efficiently through their giving journey. Our work secures funding, optimizes resource allocation, and protects organizational reputation through rigorous due diligence.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Global Prospect Development, the Prospect Development Officer sits within the Global Partnerships and Philanthropy team, playing a key role in supporting MSI’s sustainability by helping to shape team-level strategies and contributing to broader prospect research and management planning.

They are responsible for delivering advanced research and analysis, aligning research strategies with organizational goals, and providing expert strategic advice to senior staff and frontline fundraisers on primarily (but not exclusively) US and UK/Europe-based private donors. The Senior Officer takes ownership of strategic initiatives within their operational area and ensures the quality and alignment of research outputs with fundraising objectives. They will collaborate closely with frontline fundraisers to refine pipeline management, optimize portfolios, and execute proactive market scans and due diligence protocols. The right candidate will build and sustain positive relationships across internal teams and external vendors, while driving superior research and prospect management services that ultimately increase philanthropic support for our clients.

**Now is an especially great time to join MSI Reproductive Choices, as this role plus two others will join the global funding and innovation team!**

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- Strong project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and deliver high-quality work;
- Demonstrated knowledge of quantitative and qualitative analysis and business intelligence work in support of global non-profit fundraising; interpreting, and synthesizing data;
- Ability to develop and lead proactive prospecting methodologies and strategic research initiatives that support organizational goals, including advanced data mining, sophisticated constituent database queries, and process improvement;
- High proficiency in internet search engines and sophisticated search techniques, fundraising software, data retrieval services (e.g. LexisNexis, iWave, Foundation Directory, Relationship Science, etc.), MS Office; experience working with a relational database a necessity;
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills as well as an overall ability to be clear and concise in all communications; attention to detail a must.
- Ability to act with sensitivity and discretion while working with highly confidential information;

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- A minimum of 5+ years progressive experience in prospect development/database management
- Prior experience working at an international organization not required but would be an asset;
- Knowledge and curiosity about emerging concepts and practices in the fields of prospect development, strategic philanthropy, DAFs/Philanthropic advisors, Public/Private Partnerships, and impact investing, as it relates both U.S. and non-U.S. entities;
- Knowledge of global data-privacy regulations like GDPR;

**Formal education/qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree required

For the full job description, please email RecruitmentInbox@MSIchoices.org

**Location:** London, UK (minimum of 2 days per week in the office)

**Full-time:** 35 hours a week, Monday to Friday.

**Contract type: 1-year fixed term contract.**

**Salary**: £41,400 - £47,600 per annum + Benefits

**Salary band: BG 7**

**Closing date: 17th November (midnight GMT**). Interviews may take place before this date for exceptional candidates.

jobs.description:
## Trustee

**Help shape BNMT’s next chapter and secure lasting support for health equity in Nepal.**

## The opportunity

BNMT UK is seeking a Trustee to govern BNMT UK. You will bring strategic judgement, fresh perspectives and commitment to a partnership rooted in Nepali leadership. Expertise in fundraising or digital communication is a particular priority as we grow income, reach new supporters and build sustained commitment to our work.

**ROLE:** Trustee of the Britain Nepal Medical Trust

**STATUS:** Voluntary and unpaid; reasonable agreed expenses may be reimbursed

**TERM:** Normally three years, within BNMT’s staggered Board cycle

**MEETINGS:** Two half-day meetings in person in London each year, plus two intermediate 90-minute teleconferences

**CONTRIBUTION:** Meeting preparation and occasional agreed contributions between meetings

## The partnership

For 60 years, the Britain Nepal Medical Trust has worked to improve health and reduce poverty in Nepal through equitable access to care, locally led programmes and applied research.

Today, BNMT UK provides funding, advocacy, relationships and strategic support to Birat Nepal Medical Trust (BNMT Nepal), an independent, Nepali-led organisation. The two organisations are legally distinct; BNMT Nepal leads and delivers programmes in Nepal.

## Your strategic contribution

You will govern BNMT UK and help shape its future. Programme leadership and delivery sit with BNMT Nepal.

- **Set direction.** Help the Board choose priorities and assess progress against BNMT’s mission.
- **Secure lasting support.** Shape a sustainable income strategy, strengthen relationships and help BNMT reach new supporters.
- **Strengthen the partnership.** Support shared priorities with BNMT Nepal, respecting Nepali leadership and mutual accountability.
- **Provide sound oversight.** Safeguard charitable funds, oversee risk and uphold financial, safeguarding and regulatory responsibilities.

## Priority capabilities

We seek strong experience in at least one of the following, with a willingness to contribute across both:

- **Fundraising.** A record of building donor relationships, opening networks and turning a persuasive case for support into sustainable income.
- **Digital communication.** Experience of growing audiences and converting engagement into lasting support through clear storytelling and effective digital strategy.

## What you bring

- Commitment to health equity, locally led development and BNMT’s mission.
- Strategic judgement, integrity and confidence to challenge constructively and share responsibility for Board decisions.
- Leadership or decision-making experience, alongside the ability to listen and work respectfully across cultures.
- An understanding of trustee oversight, or a willingness to develop it, and time to contribute.

Knowledge of Nepal, the Nepali diaspora or UK charity governance would be valuable. A clinical or global-health background is not required.

## A Board with broader perspectives

We welcome applications from all backgrounds and particularly encourage people from the Nepali diaspora, women, and people from historically oppressed or under-represented communities. We value lived experience and are committed to an accessible appointment process.

## Joining the Board

Trustees receive an induction and are expected to prepare for meetings, contribute as agreed and uphold BNMT’s policies on conflicts of interest and confidentiality.

[https://www.britainnepalmedicaltrust.org.uk/become-a-trustee/](https://www.britainnepalmedicaltrust.org.uk/become-a-trustee/)
