jobs.title: Area HR Manager - Tawila - North Darfur/ SUDAN
jobs.description:
**Place:** Tawila / Sudan
**Starting date: December** 2026
**Duration of contract: 6** months renewal according funding

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organisation works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organisation. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview.

**JOB CONTEXT:**
Handicap International – Humanity & Inclusion (HI) initiated its operations in Sudan in early 2024, in Gedaref State, initially providing technical, financial and operational support to a national NGO, with activities managed remotely due to access constraints. Following HI’s registration with the Sudanese authorities in December 2024, the organisation progressively expanded its operational footprint. In January 2025, HI opened a base in West Darfur (El Geneina) and began direct implementation, including hygiene kit distributions for households with malnourished children, cash-based food assistance, and the strengthening of inclusive humanitarian approaches. In October 2025, HI opened an office and the launch of direct activities in Al Jazirah State, with a focus on physical rehabilitation (including stimulation therapy for children under five) and Inclusive Humanitarian Action, implemented in consortium with humanitarian partners. In January 2026, in light of the emergency in North Darfur, HI opened an office in Tawila to deploy Atlas Logistique teams, which are responsible for providing storage and transport services for humanitarian actors. An Emergency Medical team is also working alongside MSF Hospital to provide post-surgical rehabilitation care.

**YOUR MISSION:**
Reporting to the Country Director, you define and roll out the HR component of the Country’s operational strategy (Stratop). You are the preferred contact for HR operations centres at Headquarters. You ensure that HR activities are consistent with your budgetary framework and with HI’s HR frameworks. You actively analyse changes in context so as to identify the risks and opportunities in your scope of responsibility.

Your main missions are as follows:

· Management of the HR team at area level

· HR design of the Stratop and associated action plan monitoring: draft, revise and implement the operational strategy (Stratop) within your area of responsibility area, in line with HI's financial policies

· Standards roll out and HI's Expertise contribution in your scope of responsibility:

o Deploy and monitor the quality of all HI's HR policies, processes and tools

o Assist and supervise your team with the adaptation and contextualisation of HR frameworks

o Ensure the quality of the auditing, internal control and archiving procedures

· Operational implementation of HR:

o Oversee the dimensioning and quality of resources

o Oversee the Career Management and Skills Development systems

o Coordinate and guarantee the quality of the administrative management for all members of staff

o Assist managers with the implementation of HI's HR policies

o Legal and social aspects: maintain the social environment and ensure the compliance with the legal HR framework

o Support the Country Manager with the deployment of the HR part of the Code of Conduct and the PSEA, the Fraud and Corruption Policy and other institutional policies

· Emergency preparedness and response

Your main challenges to come on the period :

· Expertise: Contribute to national strategies in line with the global strategies

· Manage the HR department at area level

· Finalize the HR package at area level

· Business development: Contribute to the development of major opportunities

**CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POSITION:**

Tawila is a remote town in North Darfur, Sudan, currently hosting a very large population of internally displaced people affected by the ongoing conflict. Living and working in Tawila means operating in a highly challenging humanitarian and security environment, with limited infrastructure and very basic living conditions. Good level of internet access, and no specific issue regarding the water supply. Food supplies and other essential goods can be difficult to obtain, and access to healthcare is very limited (Medical evacuation service is available by ambulance for Chad). Movement is highly restricted and must follow strict security procedures, with travel outside the immediate operational area subject to security clearance. Working conditions are demanding, with high humanitarian needs and a constantly changing context requiring flexibility and strong resilience. Despite these constraints, Tawila offers expatriate staff the opportunity to work closely with affected communities and national colleagues in a context where humanitarian assistance is critically needed.

Travel to other parts of Darfur is planned, including Nyala, Zalengei and Geinena.

## **Requirements**

· Relevant training in HR management and development of humanitarian projects/operations, or equivalent, preferably in the field of international solidarity.

· You have at least 4 years of professional experience in emergency response and at least 3 years in a HR coordination/manager position or similar in emergency or post-emergency assistance.

Skills required:

· High capacity for analysis and synthesis.

· Ability to project quickly in an emergency context.

· Mastery of the management of the project cycle.

· Ability to handle conflicts.

· Strong flexibility and adaptation

· Ability to work remotely including capacity building and remote deployment

· Excellent communication includes constructive feedback.

· English required, knowledge of Arabic is an asset.

· Security : Personal security management

## **Benefits**

At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission:

- 6 months (renewal according funding) international contract starting from December 2026 based in Tawila;
- The international contract provides social cover adapted to your situation:
- Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
- Pension scheme;
- Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution;
- Repatriation insurance paid by HI;
- Salary from 2757€ gross/month upon experience;
- Perdiem: 685 € net/month - paid in the field
- Hardship: 500 € net/month paid with your salary
- Paid leaves: 25 days per year;
- R&R: 5 days every 8 weeks
- Position: Unaccompanied
- Housing: Collective taken in charge by HI;
- If you are resident in the country: local package.

jobs.title: Team Leader Third-Party Monitoring, DRC Humanitarian Fund
jobs.description:
**Background**

SoCha is preparing a proposal to provide independent third-party monitoring (TPM) services for projects financed through the Democratic Republic of the Congo Humanitarian Fund (DRC HF), administered by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA).

The assignment involves independent verification of humanitarian project implementation, including field monitoring, beneficiary consultations, remote verification and beneficiary verification surveys. Activities will cover multiple humanitarian sectors and geographically dispersed, insecure and hard-to-reach locations.

SoCha seeks a qualified Team Leader to provide overall technical and operational leadership for the assignment, ensuring the timely delivery of rigorous, independent and actionable monitoring findings.

**Position Summary**

The Team Leader will be responsible for the overall management, technical quality and operational delivery of TPM services. The position will serve as SoCha's principal focal point for the UNOCHA DRC Humanitarian Fund Unit (HFU), supervising the Field Monitoring Coordinators, Data Analyst and associated monitoring personnel.

The Team Leader will ensure that monitoring activities follow approved methodologies, contractual requirements and ethical standards, while maintaining operational readiness across the seven priority provinces.

**Key Responsibilities**

***A. Technical Leadership and Monitoring Methodology***

- Lead the development and implementation of the TPM Operational Plan, including risk-based prioritization, monitoring approaches, deployment schedules and quality-assurance arrangements.
- Oversee the design of project-specific monitoring plans, sampling strategies, data collection tools and means of verification.
- Ensure monitoring methodologies are appropriate to the relevant humanitarian sectors, including Health, Nutrition, Protection, Food Security, Shelter/NFI, WASH, Education and Camp Coordination and Camp Management.
- Ensure systematic triangulation of documentary evidence, field observations, stakeholder interviews and beneficiary feedback.
- Oversee remote monitoring approaches when physical access is restricted, subject to UNOCHA approval.

***B. Project Management and Operational Coordination***

- Manage day-to-day implementation of TPM assignments, ensuring adherence to agreed work plans, timelines and deliverables.
- Supervise Field Monitoring Coordinators and the Data Analyst, ensuring effective coordination between field operations, data management and reporting.
- Coordinate the mobilization of field monitoring teams, including urgent or unplanned assignments.
- Oversee operational planning, including staffing, logistics, access arrangements and security assessments, in coordination with SoCha's operational personnel and local partners.
- Monitor implementation progress, identify bottlenecks and initiate corrective action where necessary.

***C. Stakeholder Engagement and Contract Management***

- Serve as the principal technical and operational liaison with the UNOCHA DRC HFU.
- Coordinate with implementing partners to facilitate access to project documentation, sites, personnel and beneficiaries, while safeguarding the independence of monitoring activities.
- Participate in regular coordination and management meetings with UNOCHA.
- Provide timely updates on monitoring progress, operational constraints and emerging risks.
- Ensure potential conflicts of interest are identified and disclosed before assignments.

***D. Quality Assurance and Reporting***

- Oversee the preparation and quality assurance of TPM reports, Beneficiary Verification Survey reports and periodic synthesis reports.
- Ensure findings are evidence-based, appropriately triangulated and clearly distinguish verified results from observations, unverified information and allegations.
- Ensure reports assess implementation progress, quality of assistance, beneficiary perspectives, cross-cutting issues and areas requiring corrective action.
- Review all substantive deliverables before submission to UNOCHA.
- Ensure reports and supporting evidence are submitted in French and within contractual deadlines.
- Lead the preparation of biannual synthesis reports and presentations when requested.

***E. Risk Management, Safeguarding and Compliance***

- Ensure monitoring activities comply with applicable security, safeguarding, PSEA, data protection and Do No Harm requirements
- Oversee the implementation of security and access protocols, including go/no-go decisions, contingency planning and remote-monitoring alternatives.
- Ensure serious protection concerns, suspected fraud, aid diversion and other critical findings are escalated through approved channels within required timelines.
- Maintain appropriate procedures for informed consent, confidentiality and secure handling of sensitive information.
- Ensure all monitoring personnel receive appropriate training and comply with SoCha and UNOCHA requirements.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- University degree in monitoring and evaluation, social sciences, statistics, humanitarian affairs or a related discipline; a Master's degree is strongly preferred.
- **More than seven years of experience in team management**, preferably involving geographically dispersed monitoring or research operations.
- At least three years of relevant experience in monitoring, evaluation or independent verification, including in the DRC or a comparable complex operational environment.
- Demonstrated experience managing humanitarian or development monitoring assignments for UN agencies, international organizations or major institutional donors.
- Strong understanding of risk-based monitoring, mixed-methods research, field verification and data quality assurance.
- Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and operations in insecure, hard-to-reach or otherwise challenging environments.
- Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality analytical reports and manage demanding reporting schedules.
- Strong understanding of humanitarian principles, protection, safeguarding, PSEA and ethical data collection.

**Language Requirements**

- Fluency in written and spoken French is required.
- Working proficiency in English is required.
- Knowledge of relevant DRC local languages is an advantage.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- More than five years of experience specifically in humanitarian or development monitoring and reporting.
- Previous leadership of TPM assignments for UN agencies, humanitarian pooled funds or bilateral donors.
- Direct operational experience in eastern or northeastern DRC.
- Familiarity with the DRC Humanitarian Fund, humanitarian coordination structures and relevant sector standards.
- Experience with digital monitoring platforms, including Kobo Toolbox, ODK or similar systems.

**Expected Deliverables**

The Team Leader will be accountable for:

- The TPM Operational Plan and regular updates.
- Approved project-specific mission plans and monitoring methodologies.
- Timely delivery of TPM reports and supporting evidence.
- Oversight of Beneficiary Verification Surveys and associated reporting.
- Weekly progress updates during active assignments.
- Periodic synthesis reports and management presentations, as requested.
- Quality-assurance documentation, corrective action tracking and end-of-contract handover.

**Reporting and Working Arrangements**

The Team Leader will report to SoCha's designated Project Director or senior management representative and will serve as the primary point of contact with UNOCHA.

The position is full-time and dedicated to the contract. The Team Leader will supervise the core technical team and coordinate with SoCha's operations and security personnel and approved local partners.

The position requires travel within the DRC, subject to approved security and access procedures.

jobs.title: Data Analyst Third-Party Monitoring, DRC Humanitarian Fund
jobs.description:
**Background**

SoCha is preparing a proposal to provide independent third-party monitoring services for projects financed through the DRC Humanitarian Fund, administered by UNOCHA.

The assignment will involve field-based and remote verification of humanitarian assistance, including structured surveys, qualitative interviews, document reviews, beneficiary verification surveys and digital evidence collection.

SoCha seeks a Data Analyst to lead data management, quality assurance and analysis across TPM assignments, ensuring that monitoring findings are accurate, verifiable and supported by secure, well-managed datasets.

**Position Summary**

The Data Analyst will be responsible for the design and management of digital data collection tools, data quality-control systems, databases and analytical outputs supporting TPM missions and Beneficiary Verification Surveys (BVS).

Working closely with the Team Leader and Field Monitoring Coordinators, the Data Analyst will ensure that data collected across multiple provinces is complete, consistent, securely managed and suitable for rigorous analysis and reporting.

The position will also provide technical oversight of data processing and analysis for telephone-based beneficiary verification activities.

**Key Responsibilities**

***A. Digital Data Collection and Tool Development***

- Develop, program, test and maintain electronic data collection tools for TPM missions and Beneficiary Verification Surveys.
- Configure survey instruments and monitoring forms using KoboToolbox, ODK or comparable platforms.
- Integrate appropriate validation rules, skip logic, geographic references, timestamps and other quality-control features.
- Support the development of sampling frameworks and data collection protocols in coordination with the Team Leader.
- Ensure tools are adapted to sector-specific monitoring requirements, including the verification of humanitarian activities and reported outputs.
- Prepare data collection guidance and provide technical orientation to field monitors and telephone survey operators.

***B. Data Management and Quality Assurance***

- Establish and maintain secure systems for receiving, storing, cleaning, processing and archiving monitoring data.
- Conduct routine data quality checks, including assessments of completeness, consistency, duplication, outliers and other potential errors.
- Review geotagged records and supporting evidence, where appropriate, to identify discrepancies requiring verification.
- Monitor incoming data during fieldwork and communicate quality concerns promptly to the Team Leader and Field Monitoring Coordinators.
- Develop and maintain data quality dashboards, verification logs and issue-tracking systems.
- Ensure appropriate anonymization and secure handling of beneficiary information and other sensitive data.

***C. Data Analysis and Reporting***

- Conduct descriptive and comparative analysis of quantitative monitoring data, disaggregating findings by relevant characteristics where feasible and appropriate.
- Support the triangulation of quantitative data with qualitative findings, documentary evidence and field observations.
- Prepare tables, charts, summaries and analytical outputs for inclusion in TPM reports.
- Support the development of verification matrices comparing implementing partners' reported outputs with independently verified findings.
- Identify patterns, discrepancies, implementation gaps and potential data-integrity concerns.
- Contribute to periodic synthesis reports, including cross-project and cross-sector analysis where appropriate.

***D. Beneficiary Verification Surveys***

- Support the design of BVS sampling strategies and telephone survey instruments.
- Prepare beneficiary contact lists for secure use, including appropriate sampling and respondent tracking procedures.
- Provide technical oversight of electronic data capture by telephone survey operators.
- Monitor response rates, unsuccessful call attempts, sample composition and data quality.
- Clean and analyse BVS datasets and prepare statistical summaries and visualizations.
- Contribute to BVS reports, documenting sampling procedures, response rates, findings, limitations and data quality.
- Produce clean, anonymized datasets for submission to UNOCHA.

***E. Capacity Building and Technical Support***

- Train and support Field Monitoring Coordinators, field monitors and BVS operators in digital data collection procedures.
- Develop concise guidance on data quality, validation, secure storage and submission protocols.
- Troubleshoot technical issues affecting electronic data collection and synchronization.
- Support the development of remote-monitoring approaches when physical access is restricted.
- Recommend improvements to data collection systems and analytical processes throughout the contract.

***F. Data Protection and Compliance***

- Ensure data management practices comply with applicable confidentiality, informed consent, safeguarding and data protection requirements.
- Apply appropriate access controls, anonymization procedures and secure data-transfer protocols.
- Support the safe handling of sensitive beneficiary information and allegations of misconduct.
- Maintain appropriate documentation of data processing, cleaning and quality-assurance procedures.
- Support secure data handover, retention and deletion in accordance with contractual requirements.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- University degree in information technology, statistics, economics, data science or a related discipline.
- More than three years of experience using technology for data management and analysis.
- Demonstrated experience developing and managing digital data collection systems, preferably using Kobo Toolbox, ODK or similar platforms.
- Strong skills in data cleaning, validation, database management and statistical analysis.
- Experience analyzing quantitative survey data and producing clear analytical outputs for technical reports.
- Familiarity with sampling approaches, survey administration and data quality assurance.
- Demonstrated understanding of data protection, confidentiality and ethical handling of sensitive information.
- Ability to work effectively with geographically dispersed field teams under demanding timelines.

**Language Requirements**

- Proficiency in written and spoken French is required.
- Working proficiency in English is an advantage.
- Knowledge of relevant DRC local languages is an asset.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Previous professional experience in the DRC, particularly in humanitarian or development monitoring.
- Experience supporting TPM, independent verification or humanitarian monitoring assignments.
- Experience with telephone surveys, beneficiary verification and call-center data systems.
- Proficiency in analytical software such as Stata, R, SPSS, Python, Power BI or comparable tools.
- Experience with geospatial data, geotagged evidence and GIS applications.
- Familiarity with humanitarian programme indicators, disaggregation requirements and verification methodologies.
- Experience supporting monitoring assignments for UN agencies or major institutional donors.

**Expected Deliverables**

The Data Analyst will be responsible for producing or supporting:

- Programmed and tested digital data collection tools.
- Data management and quality-assurance procedures.
- Cleaned and validated TPM datasets.
- Data quality reports and discrepancy logs.
- Analytical tables, charts and verification matrices for TPM reporting.
- BVS sampling and response-rate documentation.
- Cleaned and anonymized BVS datasets and associated analytical outputs.
- Secure data archives and end-of-contract data handover materials.

**Reporting and Working Arrangements**

The Data Analyst will report directly to the Team Leader and work closely with Field Monitoring Coordinators, field monitors and telephone survey operators.

The position will provide technical oversight of data systems and quality assurance across all assigned monitoring activities. The Data Analyst role must remain distinct from the Team Leader and Field Monitoring Coordinator positions.

The level of effort and employment arrangement will be determined by SoCha, subject to the requirements of the final contract.

jobs.title: Research Manager for Nigeria, based in Abuja
jobs.description:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the PANDA Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT operates through three Initiatives: REACH, PANDA, and AGORA. This recruitment opportunity pertains to the PANDA Initiative.

PANDA is IMPACT’s lever on humanitarian aid responses which focusing on improving outcomes for beneficiaries through direct engagement with partners and their activities. Where REACH works through soft power and partnerships to affect systemic change, PANDA is direct action that allows us to ensure that system and its participants are trustworthy and delivering the most effective, efficient and equitable response possible. PANDA is praxis – it is how IMPACT manifests our vision of acting as a catalyst of change within the aid community to work through focused or multidimensional analysis of projects, programmes and policies to identify their results, strengths and weaknesses, and how they can be improved, then proposes or implements a concrete plan for improvement.

**We are currently looking for a Research Manager to support our team in Nigeria.**

**Department**: PANDA

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 4 months

**Location**: Abuja, Nigeria (with occasional stays in Dakar, Senegal)

**Starting Date**: ASAP.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Nigeria is among the world's most critical hunger hotspots, where protracted conflict, displacement, economic pressures, and climate shocks are driving rapidly worsening humanitarian needs. In the Northeast, more than 8.8 million people require urgent assistance, including 4.9 million children, sustained displacement, protection risks, severe funding shortfalls, a growing nutrition emergency, and a cholera outbreak. Food insecurity is expected to reach record levels, with an estimated 34.7 million people nationwide projected to face Crisis-level food insecurity or worse by August 2026. Meanwhile, the Northwest faces a different but equally severe crisis driven by chronic poverty, banditry, communal violence, and recurrent flooding, which have displaced hundreds of thousands of people (800,000 IOM DTM R18), damaged livelihoods and farmland, and contributed to sharp declines in agricultural production. Together, these overlapping shocks are undermining resilience, increasing humanitarian needs, and threatening both current food security and future harvests.

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence-base for the humanitarian community. Historically, IMPACT Initiatives has been present in both the Northeast and Northwest of Nigeria. Thematically, across 2021 – 2023 IMPACT Initiatives fielded [Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/7b6cde65/REACH_NGA_TOR_MSNA-Northwest_March-2022-1.pdf) (MSNAs), [Hard to Reach](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/0f980ce2/NGA-1809_Situation_Overview_Q1_Feb_Mar_2022.pdf) (H2R) assessments, [Area Based Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/7cddc3c2/REACH_NGA_TOR_Rapid_Area-Based_Assessments_in_Areas_of_Return_February_2021.pdf) (ABA), [Rapid Overviews of Areas of Return](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/07db0c79/REACH_NGA_ToR_Rapid_Overview_Of_Areas_Of_Return_ROAR_-Feb-2022.pdf) (ROAR), [Thematic Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/9fa6a7cf/REACH_NGA_Brief_assessment-of-H2R-Gujba-and-Tarmua-LGA_April-2022.pdf) (TA), [Rapid Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/6b1d770d/REACH_NGA_Yobe_Floods_Brief.pdf) (RA), and [WASH Infrastructure Mapping](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/afb497ac/REACH_NGA_Factsheet_WASH-Infrastructure-Maiduguri_May-2021.pdf), while also playing a key role in Famine Monitoring, Nutrition and Food Security Surveillance, and the Joint Market Monitoring Initiative (JMMI). Since 2026, IMPACT has reintroduced the MSNA, Acute Needs Analysis (ANA), JMMI and other thematic assessments in Nigeria in addition to the HARP TPM project which has been running since 2024.

## **PROJECT PRFILE**

The position is recruited for the Third-Party Monitoring (TPM) Project covering FCDOs Humanitarian and Resilience Programme (HARP) Facility. For this programme, IMPACT is in partnership with FACT Foundation. While in Nigeria, staff shall be hosted by FACT Foundation and for his or her mission, the Research Manager will fall under the direct responsibility and management of FACT and their delegates for all Administrative, Security, Logistics and Finance issues. S/he will therefore fully abide by FACT’s Security, HR, Administration, and Logistics rules and regulations, and in coordination with FACT, ensure that all IMPACT staff abide by them.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the management of the Country Representative, the Research Manager oversees the research activities and staff within the purview of the FCDO-funded Third Party Monitoring (TPM) Project. The Research Manager shall oversee and execute all research activities within the above-mentioned Project, meeting quarterly deliverables in a timely fashion while ensuring that the quality of research remains high. S/he will moreover liaise extensively with counterparts from Fact Foundation who are IMPACT’s partners in the Consortium for the Project, while supporting the Country Representative in stakeholder engagement with FCDO’s Implementing Partners.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Research Manager responsibilities include the following:

***Strategy development & implementation***

- With specific attention to the FCDO-funded TPM Project’s, and while supervised by the CR, the RM is to ensure that IMPACT has an up to date understanding of the country’s socio-economic situation, the impact of a crisis and the aid/humanitarian situation, as well as the humanitarian planning, coordination, response mechanism developments, and key humanitarian stakeholders.
- For the TPM Project, **develop and oversee the implementation of the project’s strategy**. Specifically, during the inception period, in conjunction with the CR, set out the project’s overall strategy, develop concomitant workplans for each staff member, and put in place the requisite structures for the staff members such that each individual has clarity as to how to work towards the common goal of completing deliverables in a timely manner and at a high standard, and ultimately supplying impact to FCDO and Implementing Partners at the outcome level.

## ***Research Planning***

- For the TPM Project, ensure that all the research is planned in line with the relevant project and programme objectives, as well as the Project and Country Strategy. This is to include:
- Ensure that all research complies with IMPACT’s HQ Research Department guidelines and standards.
- Ensure that al necessary Secondary Data Reviews are conducted and integrated into the research.
- Ensure that research ToRs are validated by HQ prior to the commencement of data collection.
- Ensure that research ToRs are understood by the team and updated accordingly.
- Keep track of progress and delays of all assigned assessments throughout the research cycle.
- Liaise with FACT Foundation, to include their two assessment and data staff in the research.
- Liaise with FACT Foundation to ensure that the portion of the research carried out by them is validated by IMPACT HQ.
- Where necessary, proactively support the team by conducting research (research design. ToRs, tool building, data management, data analysis, product drafting).
- While supported by the CR, conduct dissemination and stakeholder meetings with FCDO and Implementing Partners.

***Research Implementation***

- Liaise with FACT Foundation, to **ensure that the data is collected in the fashion and format that allows IMPACT to clean and analyse the data**.
- Ensure that all collected data is stored **in line with IMPACT’s Data Management Guidelines**, as well as with the data management plan Annex in the Research ToR.
- Ensure that data is revised and cleaned, **with all revisions recorded** as per IMPACT data management guidelines.
- **Oversee all the analyses of the collected data**, as stipulated in the Research ToRs.
- Ensure that data and its analysis **do not contain personal information** and are validated by IMPACT HQ, before sharing to external parties.
- Supervise and where necessary support the team with the analysis and drafting of the information products.
- **Review all products** before they are sent to the CR or IMPACT HQ for validation.
- Ensure that all written products are validated by IMPACT HQ **before release to FCDO and Implementing Partners**.

***Team Management and Leadership***

- Ensure that all staff members understand and are able to perform their roles and responsibilities, as well as their reporting and validation duties to HQ.
- Ensure that all staff members have **clear and regularly updated ToRs, Workplans, and Key performance Indicators (KPIs)** against which their performance will be appraised.
- **Promote team building, productivity, and staff welfare**.
- Mentor and support the team **to build capacities, improve efficiency and performance**.
- **Promote the growth and development of staff** within the organisation, actively linking with HQ to provide feedback and support retention and internal mobility. Identify capacity building opportunities for growth, proactively provide high-performing staff with opportunities to surge (a short-term deployment to another mission) and develop pathways for junior staff to grow and move into management or specialist positions.
- **Ensure communication and linkages with HQ** are made immediately in case of the occurrence of an HR-related problem.

***Internal Coordination and Communication***

- Facilitate clear and seamless communication within the IMPACT TPM team across Senegal and Nigeria, as well as the FACT Foundation team in Nigeria.
- Ensure regular reporting to the CR.

***INFLUENCING - External Engagement***

- With the support from the CR, on a quarterly basis, engage with FCDO and the Implementing Partners to share findings and hold analysis and lessons learned workshops.
- Under the supervision of the CR, and where necessary, engage with the humanitarian response beyond the remit of the TPM Project.
- In conjunction with FCDO and Implementing Partners, support the CR in the dissemination of selected research with key stakeholders and coordination forums.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Academic** Excellent academic qualifications, including a master’s degree in a relevant discipline (International Relations, Political Sciences, Social Research, Economics, Development Studies, or similar)
- **Management experience** Previous experience in a management role in an INGO at field level. Proven track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts
- **Familiarity aid system** Familiarity with the aid system, and the research community.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high level presentations/briefings.
- **Years of work experience** At least 3 years of relevant working experience or proven progression within IMPACT.
- **Research skills:** Excellent research and analytical skills an asset. Experience in assessments. M&E, field research, evaluations is an asset.
- **Software skills:** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Ability to multitask with tight deadlines, on numerous research cycles in complex environment.
- **Level of independence** A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the \[relevant\] region is desirable.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required.
- **Security environment** Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’180 CHF and 3’240 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situational security training;
- Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

jobs.title: COORDINATEUR/TRICE COMPLIANCE -NOUAKCHOTT
jobs.description:
Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim (ACF) est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim et les situations mettant en danger les populations. Présente dans plus de 46 pays, elle compte plus de 5 000 collaborateurs.

Chez ACF, la conformité, l’anticipation des risques et le renforcement des contrôles contribuent directement à la qualité et à la redevabilité de notre action humanitaire.

Dans un contexte opérationnel exigeant, nous recherchons un·e **Coordinateur·trice Compliance** pour garantir la conformité des opérations, renforcer le contrôle interne et promouvoir une culture de transparence auprès des équipes et partenaires.

**Votre mission**

Sous la supervision du Directeur Pays Adjoint Support, vous assurez la gestion globale de la conformité et du contrôle interne de la mission Mauritanie.

**Vos principales responsabilités :**

- **Gestion des risques et conformité :** identifier et atténuer les risques financiers et opérationnels, veiller au respect des procédures internes et des exigences des bailleurs, réaliser des contrôles, audits internes et investigations si nécessaire.
- **Coordination des audits :** planifier et piloter les audits internes et externes, coordonner les échanges avec les auditeurs et le siège, garantir la qualité des pièces justificatives et assurer le suivi des recommandations jusqu’à leur clôture.
- **Renforcement des capacités :** former et accompagner les équipes ACF et les partenaires sur la conformité, les risques et les exigences des bailleurs.
- **Amélioration continue :** capitaliser les leçons apprises, suivre les actions correctives et contribuer au renforcement durable du contrôle interne.
- **Management et valeurs :** encadrer, développer et évaluer les collaborateurs, favoriser un environnement inclusif et performant et promouvoir les valeurs d’ACF ainsi que les principes de Safeguarding et de prévention de l’exploitation et des abus sexuels (PSEA).

**Le profil recherché**

**Formation**

- Master (Bac+5) en Comptabilité, Finance, Contrôle de gestion, Audit, Management ou domaine équivalent.

**Expérience**

- Au moins 5 ans d’expérience en gestion financière, audit, contrôle interne ou conformité.
- Au moins 3 ans d’expérience dans le secteur humanitaire ou du développement international.
- Expérience solide dans la gestion des exigences des bailleurs et la conduite d’audits.
- Expérience avérée en gestion de consortiums et de projets financés par des bailleurs institutionnels.
- Expérience en coordination et management d’équipes multiculturelles.

**Compétences techniques**

- Excellente maîtrise des règles et exigences des bailleurs, notamment de l’Union européenne.
- Maîtrise avancée de l’audit, du contrôle interne et de la gestion des risques.
- Excellentes capacités d’analyse et de résolution de problèmes.
- Niveau avancé sur Excel, excellente maîtrise du Pack Office et connaissance des logiciels comptables et financiers.

**Langues**

- Français courant obligatoire.
- Anglais professionnel fortement apprécié.

**Qualités attendues**
Rigueur, intégrité, esprit critique, autonomie, adaptabilité, capacité à influencer et accompagner le changement, et aptitude à travailler dans des environnements exigeants et multiculturels.

**Pourquoi rejoindre ACF ?**

- Contribuer à la qualité et à la redevabilité des programmes humanitaires.
- Collaborer avec des équipes engagées et expertes.
- Développer votre expertise dans un environnement international stimulant.
- Participer à des projets à fort impact auprès des populations les plus vulnérables.

**Conditions du poste**

- **Lieu :** Nouakchott, Mauritanie.
- **Durée :** 12 mois.
- **Type de contrat :national ou international.**
- **Département :** Compliance.
- **Mobilité :** déplacements réguliers sur les bases opérationnelles.
- **Statut :** poste non accompagné.
- **Rémunération :** selon les grilles salariales d’ACF, complétées par les avantages prévus par les politiques de l’organisation.
- **Prise de poste :** dès que possible.

jobs.title: Emergency Watsan Coordinator H/F
jobs.description:
Context

To fulfill its mission of assistance to victims of conflicts, epidemics or natural disasters, MSF-Switzerland has created an Emergency Pool, of which members are experienced individuals capable of evaluating a situation, opening and coordinating emergency projects.

The candidate is expected to

- work in all contexts set by the emergency cell
- have the flexibility to work in different positions depending on his/her profile
- work in emergency contexts with regular cells and fill gaps in regular projects if needed.

Duty Station

All countries where the emergency desk opens activities, which require an urgent response. On call, the Emergency Watsan technical Referent should be available within 48 hours for rapid and short interventions. He/she is part of a core group of medicals, para-medicals and support staff responsible for responding to:

- epidemic outbreaks
- nutritional crises
- displaced populations and/or refugees’ camps
- conflict contexts
- natural disasters
- exploratory missions
- Short gaps filling in the field on regular missions

Responsibilities

The main responsibilities of the Emergency Watsan Coordinator are structured in 4 main activities:

- Direct technical support to field operations (regular missions and emergencies)
- Contribution to missions' operational strategies
- Management and supervision of Watsan team
- Follow up of WASH specific supply and budget line in mission.

1. **Direct technical support to field operations**

- Promote and implement water & sanitation activities of the mission (implement or facilitate)
- Participate in:
- Exploratory missions
- Program support visits
- Assume the post of WATSAN Coordinator, where appropriate, in emergencies.

1. Contribution to missions’ operational strategies

- Share information with medical and logistic coordinators to identify potential Water, Hygiene and Sanitation related activities to develop
- Participate in the development of appropriate project strategies based on analysis of the situation
- Advise on Emergency preparedness capacity when appropriate

1. Management and supervision

- Contribute to the definition of Watsan team required in emergency
- Organize and prioritize the Watsan team members according to needs.
- In the field provides coaching to Watsan and logistic teams both local staff and expatriate

Associate Research Manager for Syria, based in Damascus
jobs.description:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO with headquarters based in Paris and presence in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for an Associate Research Manager to lead our Early Recovery, Markets, and Durable Solutions work in Syria.**

**Department**: IMPACT Syria mission

**Position**: Associate Research Manager Contract duration: 6 months

**Starting Date**: 1 December 2026

**Location**: Damascus, Syria.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

After more than a decade of conflict, economic collapse, and large-scale displacement, a regime change in December 2024 marked a new phase in Syria’s history. Conditions remain volatile, marked by regular armed clashes, prolonged socioeconomic and infrastructure challenges, and limited access to basic services such as healthcare, education, water, and electricity. While it is widely acknowledged that Syria needs large investments in development in order to recover from years of destruction and economic degradation, the humanitarian response also continues at scale due to high levels of need after fifteen years of conflict, exacerbated by the economic situation and poor basic services infrastructure.

Active in Syria since 2013, the IMPACT Syria mission has been producing key information products over the last decade to provide an evidence base for an informed humanitarian response. Activities have ranged from monthly humanitarian situation overviews and market monitoring, to displacement tracking, to supporting joint planning processes through the provision of multi-sectoral needs data, to providing evidence for durable solutions via area-based assessments.

## **POSITION PROFILE**

The Associate Research Manager will be responsible for leading research workstreams around Area-Based Assessments in support of Durable Solutions, market monitoring in support of economic analysis and recovery, and other related thematic assessments and analyses. Under the supervision of the Senior Research Manager (SRM), the ARM will lead on the development and timely implementation of the team’s strategy and research cycles.

This position requires a profile that can be both analytical and managerial, as the Associate Research Manager’s job can range from coordinating with external partners (whether data actor, sector stakeholder, or donor) to analytical oversight of research products, as well as support on data collection logistics, reporting, and financial planning.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Associate Research Manager’s responsibilities will include:

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Under the guidance of the SRM, direct management of two team members, including recruitment, capacity building and staff career management, with potential for growing the team as funding allows.
- In coordination with the SRM, development and implementation of capacity training plans for team members.
- Day-to-day management of team members, including the development of work plans and performance indicators.

***PROJECT/RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure all assessments and analysis are planned and implemented in a structured and coherent manner, in line with relevant project and strategic objectives, and with global REACH guidelines;
- Oversee all of the team’s research cycles, including reviewing ToRs, methodology notes, tools, products and dissemination strategies.
- Ensure the writing and production of timely, accurate and analytically rigorous outputs;
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in assessment design and planning;
- Monitor output achievement and ensure timely completion of the project.
- Actively advocate for the improving of analysis within REACH products, and using common methodologies, tools and analysis frameworks across workstreams where relevant.

***GRANTS MANAGEMENT***

- Under the guidance of the SRM, manage grant components, including conceptualisation of new projects, drafting proposals, regular reporting, and M&E. Lead in identifying funding opportunities and strategic positioning for the team.
- Support the SRM / Country Representative in the financial management of all grants covering the team’s projects, including oversight of budget and expenditure with regards to data collection.
- Ensure that contractual obligations are met at a high-quality standard in terms of programs deliverables.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- In coordination with the SRM and Country Representative and where relevant, represent REACH with donors, partners, and the wider response community in Syria, particularly with the Solutions Working Group, Data for Solutions Working Group, and Cash Working Group.

***STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION***

- Work with key sectors and partner organizations and working groups to understand the various relevant information gaps within Syria and identify how REACH can fill these gaps.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of the REACH Research Unit’s strategy, ensuring workstream research strategies are integrated within the wider strategy.
- In coordination with the SRM, develop and implement dissemination strategies to strengthen the impact of the team’s research cycles.
- Engagement with HQ on research and/or coordination and provide support to relevant IMPACT Global Community of Practices (CoPs).
- The Associate Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Years of work experience** At least 3 years of relevant and progressive working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as program management, evaluation and assessments.
- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research design, data collection, and data analysis experience required. Solid understanding of IMPACT Research Quality Assurance standards also required.
- **Understanding of aid system** Good understanding of the response system and key actors, as well as of the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums preferred.
- **Management experience** Demonstrated progressive staff management skills, including remote management and inspirational leadership.
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with displacement, durable solutions, area-based and movement-related research highly desirable.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the region is desirable but not decisive.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting and external engagement with donors and other high-level stakeholders.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility and work independently;
- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, including a master’s degree in a relevant discipline.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset.
- **Security environment** Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Arabic is an asset.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’180 CHF and 3’240 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst for Ethiopia, based in Kampala
jobs.description:
**BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for a Senior Data Analyst or Data Specialist, depending on profile, to work with our team in Ethiopia.**

**Position:** Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist (depending on profile)

**Contract duration**: 5 months

**Location**: Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa

**Starting Date**: ASAP.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Since 2018, Ethiopia has experienced escalating insecurity and unrest, including large-scale displacement, loss of life, and widespread destruction of property, following significant domestic political changes. These crises have compounded the effects of recurring climate-related shocks affecting large parts of the country. In November 2020, conflict erupted in the northern Tigray region, triggering significant displacement across Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions. Since August 2023, renewed conflict in Amhara has further intensified humanitarian needs, leading to the declaration of a state of emergency and restrictions on movement across the region. Together, these crises have severely disrupted livelihoods, constrained access to essential goods and staple commodities, and increased the vulnerability of affected populations, placing additional pressure on humanitarian response capacities across the country.

## **JOB PROFILE**

The Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist position is based in Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa. The position is fully dedicated to the Ethiopia mission and will report directly to the Deputy Country Representative. The postholder will lead the mission’s data team, coordinating its work across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units in close collaboration with Research Managers, the GIS Specialist and relevant HQ technical teams.

The postholder will provide technical leadership and backstopping throughout the research cycle, from methodology and sampling design to data collection, cleaning, analysis, validation and dissemination. The role is responsible for coordinating data officers and interns, agreeing priorities and resource needs with Research Managers, maintaining reusable analysis systems, and ensuring compliance with IMPACT research standards and data protection requirements. The appointment level will depend on the selected candidate’s experience and technical skills; both profiles will carry responsibility for leading the data team.

During the assignment, the Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist will be hosted by Acted, IMPACT's global partner, and will be under the responsibility of its delegates for all administrative, security, logistics and financial matters. The postholder will fully comply with Acted and IMPACT rules and procedures, including those relating to data protection and information security.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

- **Planning and coordination:** Estimate deadlines and resource requirements for each research cycle across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units. Coordinate team members’ workloads, agree data team priorities with Research Managers, and flag risks, capacity gaps and delays early, in writing, to the relevant Research Managers and direct manager.
- **Research design:** Support assessment teams in designing methodologies, sampling strategies (including sample size calculations and survey weighting), data analysis plans and data collection tools, in line with IMPACT research standards.
- **Data collection and cleaning:** Oversee the review, testing and deployment of XLSForms on IMPACT’s Kobo server, data checks during collection, and data cleaning in line with IMPACT’s Data Cleaning Minimum Standards. Where relevant, train enumerators and partner staff on data checks and cleaning.
- **Analysis systems:** Maintain and develop the mission’s R-based cleaning and analysis workflows, including IMPACT R packages, templates and Shiny applications, under version control and with up-to-date documentation so that they can be reused across research cycles.
- **Information products:** Review country-level information products and dissemination strategies to maximise the use of findings, in accordance with IMPACT research standards and in close coordination with the direct manager.
- **Data quality:** Improve data quality and monitoring at country level, including resolving discrepancies, keeping geospatial and administrative reference data up to date in coordination with GIS colleagues, and ensuring collected data is correctly georeferenced.
- **Data protection:** Ensure compliance with IMPACT’s data protection policy and SOP on personally identifiable information in all research cycles. This includes anonymisation and disclosure-risk checks before any dataset is shared, secure transfer, storage and deletion of data, and compliance with data-sharing or data processing agreements with partners.
- **Capacity building:** Lead the development and implementation of an ongoing capacity-building plan for country data officers and interns, with support from relevant technical colleagues and HQ teams. Provide training, mentoring and regular feedback on data cleaning, analysis and tools, and coordinate with Research Managers on staff development and performance.
- **Partner engagement:** At the request of the line manager, support partners on data processing, data sharing and the use of findings, and represent IMPACT on data matters in relevant coordination forums.

***DELIVERABLES***

- Lead weekly data team meetings, maintain a shared task tracker with clear responsibilities and agreed timelines, and follow up on progress and outstanding actions.
- Provide technical guidance to data officers and interns on cleaning, analysis and troubleshooting, implement and track the capacity-building plan, and provide input to their performance appraisals in coordination with Research Managers.
- Regularly liaise with project focal points and Research Managers to monitor deadlines and resource needs, anticipate delays, and communicate risks and agreed corrective actions in writing.
- Conduct internal technical validation of all research cycles, including review of sampling, data collection tools, cleaning and analysis outputs, to ensure alignment with IMPACT/HQ guidelines before submission to HQ for validation.
- Ensure regular maintenance of all mission dashboards, including Power BI and Shiny, and contribute to the design and development of new dashboards when required.
- Keep documentation, including READMEs, SOPs and decision logs, up to date for all workflows and dashboards maintained by the data team, with code under version control and clear maintenance responsibilities.
- For every dataset shared outside IMPACT, document the anonymisation applied, disclosure-risk checks and transfer, in line with the relevant agreement and applicable IMPACT procedures.

## **REQUIRED SKILLSET**

- At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in data management and analysis, preferably in humanitarian settings.
- A master’s degree in a relevant discipline, such as statistics, data science or social sciences, is preferred.
- Fluency in English is required.
- Excellent communication and data visualisation skills.
- Strong skills in R and in data cleaning and survey analysis workflows; familiarity with IMPACT’s R packages is an asset.
- Proven skills in Power BI and R Shiny.
- Experience with KoboToolbox or ODK and XLSForm design.
- Sound knowledge of sampling methods, sample size calculations and survey weighting.
- Experience with Git/GitHub; GIS skills in QGIS or ArcGIS are an asset.
- Knowledge of humanitarian data protection practice, including anonymisation of microdata and disclosure-risk assessment.
- Experience supervising or mentoring data staff, including remotely.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities across many research cycles, at times under tight deadlines.
- Strong ability to work independently in support of colleagues and partners.
- Ability to work in an intercultural environment.
- Previous experience in Ethiopia or the Horn of Africa is highly preferred.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
