jobs.title: Trustee(s)
jobs.description:
## About HelpAge

HelpAge International is a global non-profit organisation working to improve the lives of older people around the world. Founded in 1983, it works through the HelpAge global network, a worldwide alliance of more than 200 organisations across 99 countries, with a particular focus on low and middle-income countries. Through research, advocacy, policy influence and partnership, HelpAge promotes the rights, wellbeing and inclusion of older people, while addressing challenges including poverty, inequality, ageism, climate change and humanitarian crises. As population ageing reshapes societies across the globe, the organisation’s Strategy to 2030 is strengthening its role as a supporter, convenor and thought leader, helping to build a fairer and more just world for older people.

HelpAge International is now seeking to appoint up to six Trustees over the coming year. Trustees play a central role in the governance and strategic leadership of the organisation, ensuring it fulfils its charitable purpose, remains financially sustainable and delivers its mission effectively. Working alongside fellow Board members and the Executive Team, Trustees contribute independent judgement, strategic oversight and constructive challenge. They support organisational performance, oversee risk and sustainability, help guide long-term strategic direction and act as ambassadors for HelpAge’s mission and values within an increasingly complex international environment.

Successful candidates will bring senior leadership, Board, advisory or executive experience, together with sound judgement, integrity and a commitment to effective governance. HelpAge is particularly seeking expertise in finance and audit, fundraising and income generation, governance and UK charity law, and international development and global partnerships. Finance is a priority for this campaign, and the Board would especially welcome a UK-based senior finance leader who understands charity governance and has the potential to succeed the current Treasurer in due course. Applications are also encouraged from people whose professional experience, networks or connections would strengthen the Board’s representation in Europe, Latin America and East Asia.

All candidates should have an interest in ageing and the issues affecting older people. This may come through experience in healthcare, social care, insurance, financial services, life sciences, public policy, research, international development or another relevant field. Above all, candidates should share HelpAge’s commitment to the rights, dignity and inclusion of older people and to an effective and globally representative Board.

## About the role

Trustees play a central role in the governance and strategic leadership of HelpAge International. The Board is responsible for ensuring the organisation fulfils its charitable purpose, remains financially sustainable, and delivers its mission effectively through sound governance, appropriate oversight and clear strategic direction.
As a global organisation working through a network of more than 200 members across 99 countries, HelpAge brings together partners, practitioners, researchers and advocates committed to advancing the wellbeing, rights and inclusion of older people worldwide. Trustees contribute independent judgement, constructive challenge and specialist expertise to support the organisation in achieving its ambitions.
Trustees act collectively, bringing a broad range of perspectives, experience and insight. They support and hold accountable the Executive Team, contribute to strategic decision-making, oversee risk and organisational performance, and act as ambassadors for HelpAge's mission and values.

## Principal responsibilities

Working with fellow Trustees, the successful candidates will:
•Contribute to the development,scrutiny and oversight of organisationalstrategy.
• Ensure HelpAge International fulfils itscharitable objectives and remains trueto its mission and values.
•Oversee financial stewardship, riskmanagement and organisationalsustainability.
•Monitor organisational performance andhold the Executive Team to account fordelivery against agreed objectives.
•Contribute specialist expertise andexternal perspectives to Boarddiscussions and decision-making.
• Support effective governance andcompliance with relevant legal andregulatory requirements.
• Promote a culture of accountability,inclusion and respect throughout theorganisation.
•Act in the best interests of HelpAgeInternational at all times.
•Serve as ambassadors for HelpAge andsupport its relationships with partners,stakeholders and supporters.

## **Person Specification**

We anticipate appointing up to six Trustees over the next 12 months. Collectively, these appointments will strengthen the breadth of expertise, perspectives and geographic representation across the Board. Candidates are not expected to demonstrate experience across all of the areas listed below. We are seeking a complementary mix of skills, knowledge and backgrounds that will support the Board in governing an international organisation operating across multiple regions and contexts. Candidates may bring relevant perspectives on ageing and longevity through experience in fields such as healthcare, social care, insurance, financial services, life sciences, public policy, research, international development or related sectors.

### Essential criteria

***Commitment and values***
•Commitment to the vision, mission and values of HelpAge International.
•An interest in issues affecting older people and ageing populations.
•Commitment to equality, inclusion, human rights and the dignity of older people.
•Understanding of the responsibilities of charity trusteeship, or the willingness to develop this knowledge.
***Strategic leadership and judgement***
•Experience operating at a senior leadership, board, advisory or executive level.
•Ability to think strategically and contribute to long-term organisational decision-making.
•Sound judgement and the ability to assess complex information and competing priorities.
• Ability to offer both support and constructive challenge.
***Communication and collaboration***
•Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
•Ability to work effectively as part of a diverse and international Board.
•Ability to build positive relationships and work collaboratively with people from different cultures and backgrounds.
• Willingness to listen, learn and contribute thoughtfully to discussion and debate.
***Personal qualities***
• Integrity and a commitment to high standards of governance.
• Ability to maintain confidentiality and manage sensitive information appropriately.
• Commitment to collective responsibility and effective Board working.
• Willingness and ability to devote the time required to fulfil the role.

### Terms of appointment

***Tenure***
Trustees are appointed for two three-year terms. In exceptional circumstances an extension for a further three years may be possible.
***Time commitment***
Trustees are expected to attend Board meetings, committee meetings and occasional additional sessions throughout the year.
The Board meets four times annually, with three meeting held virtually and one held in person. Trustees are expected to participate in Board committees and may also contribute to focus groups, events and other activities between formal Board meetings. International travel may be required.
***Remuneration***
The position of Trustee is unremunerated. Reasonable travel and associated expenses will be reimbursed.

jobs.title: Référent.e gestion des équipements F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La gestion de parc équipements à MSF couvre l’ensemble du cycle de vie des équipements, depuis la définition des besoins et leur référencement jusqu’à leur maintenance, leur utilisation, leur transfert et leur sortie de parc. MEMO est l’outil de référence permettant de traduire et mettre en œuvre ces pratiques sur les terrains MSF-Paris.

Sous la responsabilité du Responsable du pôle Support Technique et en étroite collaboration avec le Référent Processus et Outils Métier (RPOM), le/la Référent·e Gestion de Parc Équipements est le/la référent·e siège sur les politiques, processus et bonnes pratiques de gestion de parc. Il/elle accompagne les équipes terrain sur leurs mises application et assure leur traduction cohérente dans MEMO. Le poste combine expertise métier, amélioration continue, accompagnement terrain, administration fonctionnelle de MEMO, qualité des données et pilotage.

**Principales responsabilités :**

**Politiques, processus et bonnes pratiques**

- Définir, formaliser et mettre à jour les politiques, processus, procédures et bonnes pratiques liés au cycle de vie des équipements.
- Assurer une veille sur les pratiques terrain, capitaliser les retours d’expérience et proposer des améliorations adaptées aux besoins opérationnels.
- Traduire les politiques et processus en règles de gestion, référentiels et pratiques opérationnelles, en assurant leur cohérence avec les processus de maintenance et les exigences techniques.
- Accompagner les responsables et coordinateurs logistiques dans leur appropriation et leur mise en œuvre.

**Accompagnement, support et formation des équipes terrain**

- Être l’interlocuteur privilégié des équipes terrain sur la gestion de parc et son application dans MEMO ; analyser les difficultés et proposer des solutions.
- Accompagner les logisticiens terrain et animer les échanges avec les Points Focaux Mission, en favorisant le partage des bonnes pratiques entre missions.
- Définir et actualiser les contenus de formation ; organiser et animer formations, briefings et webinaires.
- Développer l’autonomie des équipes et contribuer à la clarification des rôles et responsabilités liés à la gestion de parc.

**Traduction des processus de gestion équipements dans MEMO**

- Identifier les besoins en paramétrage fonctionnel de MEMO en cohérence avec les politiques et processus définis.
- Maintenir les catalogues, référentiels, données de référence et modèles de plans de maintenance, en lien avec les référents techniques.
- Identifier les besoins d’évolution, contribuer aux spécifications fonctionnelles et tester les nouvelles versions avec l’éditeur.
- Garantir la cohérence entre les évolutions de MEMO et les processus de gestion de parc.

**Suivi, qualité des données et amélioration continue**

- Accompagner l’identification des prioritéset analyser la qualité/cohérence des données.
- Développer des indicateurs de qualité et de performance en collaboration avec les Référents Techniques métier.
- Capitaliser les retours d’expérience et proposer des évolutions des processus, politiques et outils.

**Transversalité**

- Collaborer avec les départements du siège, les autres entités MSF et les référents techniques pour assurer la cohérence des pratiques.
- Participer aux projets transversaux et aux instances de gouvernance des processus et outils métier, en lien avec le RPOM.

**Dossiers de fond en cours :**

- Politique de gestion de parc équipements (intersection): Révision et mise à jour de la politique en étroite collaboration avec les autres OD
- BASICS gestion de parc équipements (intersection): Révision et mise à jour des Basics en étroite collaboration avec les autres OD
- Processus/Outil : Révision et mise à jour du protocole SAV et retour définitif au siège des équipements et de sa traduction dans les outils de suivi (MEMO/PowerBI)
- Analyse : Rapports d’analyse et suivi d’activité dans PowerBI (définition des besoins, indicateurs clés, maquettes de rapport)
- Organisation (contenu et format) et animation des webinaires thématiques (en étroite collaboration avec les référents techniques du POS)
- Révision et mise à jour (contenu et format) du module « Gestion de parc équipements » de la formation en présentiel « T.L.B. »

**Profil recherché :**

**Expériences :**

- Une expérience significative avec MSF ou dans le secteur associatif en tant que logisticien
- Au moins une expérience en administration de gestion de parc d’équipement.
- Une maîtrise de l’outil MEMO.

**Compétences :**

- Bonne compréhension du cycle de vie des équipements et des processus de maintenance.
- Capacité à formaliser des politiques, processus et bonnes pratiques et à les traduire en règles opérationnelles.
- Capacité à analyser les besoins utilisateurs et à les traduire en exigences fonctionnelles.
- Compétences en paramétrage applicatif, Excel et analyse de données ; connaissance de Microsoft 365 / Power BI appréciée.

**Langues :** Français et Anglais = Niveau B2
**Qualités requises :**

Aptitude à coopérer, rigueur, qualité d’analyse. Autonomie et capacité à travailler en équipe. Sens du service. Patience et persévérance. Qualités d’analyse et de synthèse.

**Conditions d'emploi :**

**Statut :** CDD de 9 mois à temps plein. Poste cadre, basé à Paris ou Mérignac.

**Rémunération et avantages** : 50,8 K€ brut annuel sur 13 mois. 22 jours de RTT par an. Télétravail selon les règles en vigueur chez MSF (2 j/sem.). Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%. Titres-restaurant de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF). Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

**Poste à pourvoir :** Janvier 2027.

En raison de contraintes administratives liées à la durée du contrat, les candidats doivent déjà disposer d'une autorisation de travail en France (citoyen de l'Union européenne) ou d’un titre de séjour leur permettant de travailler sur le sol français.

jobs.title: ESOL Instructor
jobs.description:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:**

The ESOL Instructor is responsible for providing integrated English language instruction for non-native English speakers. The instructor must be able to successfully develop and tailor curriculum and materials to the needs of students enrolled into the program including the support of student recruitment, registration, attendance tracking, retention, progress, and assessment.

This is a part-time, approx. 7 hours per week, reporting to the Adult Education Specialist. Classes and registrations are held at the IRC Richmond office.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Deliver integrated ESOL instruction
- Plan and prepare curricula and lesson plans for mixed-level classes to meet the English language learning needs of students. Integrated ESOL combines English language lessons with job skills and workforce preparation, digital literacy skills, civics, and other life skills.
- Tune lesson activities to meet student needs across a range of English proficiency levels, from the most basic through intermediate and advanced levels of speaking, comprehension, reading, and writing.
- Utilize and oversee community volunteers as classroom assistants, managing the delivery of lesson plan activities through those assistants in breakout groups.
- Document student progress with goal setting and conference notes and assist in recruitment and retention activities.
- Orient and conference with current and potential students, assisting students in completing necessary intake and enrollment forms, both virtually, using phone and web-based platforms, and in-person.
- Administer English language assessments to measure and track student progress and gains.
- Assist with record-keeping and data entry to support program administration and compliance with programmatic requirements. Document student progress by keeping accurate and timely attendance records, case notes, assessment data, program participant surveys, and observations of student progress.
- Maintain a positive learning environment. Facilitate student learning activities that build cultural and community knowledge and encourage collaboration and positive peer support.
- Maintain open and effective communication with adult education team members. Report regularly on program goals, client attendance, learning activities, student progress and any problems or concerns with clients or program.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree (4-year) preferred.
- Completion of a certificate program in Adult Education, TEFL, TESL, and/or TESOL is preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant teaching experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with immigrants or refugees preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies**

- Strong desire to support vulnerable individuals and families and enthusiasm for working in a multi-cultural setting.
- Enthusiasm for adult education and language learning.
- An interest in immigrant and refugee and asylee issues and the resettlement process.
- Strong communication abilities, including the ability to lead classes and oversee community volunteers and adult learners.
- Detail oriented and comfortable working with online databases.
- Comfortable working in a cross-cultural environment, in-person, online, and over the phone, with adult learners, sometimes with little or no English proficiency.
- Ability to take initiative, work independently on projects, and follow through on critical tasks.
- Ability to work in a collaborative environment, co-teaching and facilitating learning through others.
- Strong time management skills and comfortability with computer and web-based office and communication platforms.
- Fluent in spoken and written English. Bi-lingual abilities in a language spoken by an IRC client group are desired.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $22.75 - $24.20/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Grants Coordinator
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better futur

The IRC responds to people’s acute and longer-term needs with integrated programs that improve health and safety, prioritize children’s education, foster economic wellbeing, and empower communities to regain control over their lives. Our work engages some of the most pressing issues in contemporary humanitarian action, including access, conflict sensitivity, coordination and impact.

The IRC began its programs in Yemen in October 2012, establishing its presence in the south of the country in the Red Sea coastal city of Aden. Following the outbreak of war in March 2015 and the resulting humanitarian crisis, the IRC launched an emergency response in the southern governorates of Aden, Lahj, Abyan, Shabwah and Al Dhale, and later expanded. Yemen's operating environment requires a combination of direct implementation and partner-led approaches. The Grants Coordinator will support a diverse portfolio implemented across multiple geographic areas through both IRC teams and local partners, ensuring high-quality donor compliance, coordination, reporting, and award management. Our programs cover health, WASH, nutrition, economic recovery and development, education, child protection, and women’s protection and empowerment.

The IRC has worked in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) for more than forty years. Today, more than 2,200 staff work across the region, including in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria and Yemen, supporting people affected by some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.

**Scope of work**

The Grants Coordinator manages a large, multi-donor grant portfolio for IRC Yemen and ensures the timely development, submission and reporting of funding proposals. The role covers all grants administration activities, including proposal development, donor compliance, contract management and internal and external reporting, while keeping systems and documentation current. The Grants Coordinator also leads process-improvement initiatives and provides training and mentoring to country program staff and partners to strengthen donor management and compliance.

**Job summary**

The Grants Coordinator is a strategic role responsible for managing IRC Yemen’s grant portfolio, ensuring compliance with donor requirements, and leading the development of high-quality proposals and reports. Reporting to the Deputy Director of Programs (DDP), the Grants Coordinator supervises the grants team, coordinates inter-departmental efforts to secure and manage funding, and serves as the primary focal point for donor communications and risk mitigation. The role requires exceptional organizational skills, advanced writing ability, and the capacity to work effectively in a complex, conflict-affected environment.

The Grants Coordinator works closely with all departments, including program, METAL, finance, supply chain, HR and partnerships, and liaises with the regional office in Amman and with IRC headquarters grants and technical units.

**Working relations**

- **Reports to:** Deputy Director of Programs (DDP)
- **Directly supervises:** Grants Manager, Grants Officer and Communications Senior Officer
- **Key internal collaborators:** Technical Program Coordinators, METAL staff, Field Coordinators, the Partnerships team, Finance and Supply Chain teams, the Awards Management Unit, and Regional and HQ Grants units
- **External:** Donor representatives, local partners, government counterparts, and clusters and working groups

**Main responsibilities**

**Proposal development and business development**

- Ensure that IRC’s proposal development system is understood and followed across management, program, finance and operations, resulting in timely, high-quality submissions.
- With the DDP and HQ colleagues, proactively identify new funding opportunities by monitoring donor strategies, policies and funding trends, and keep the opportunity pipeline up to date.
- Support the DDP and technical leads in new program design and in maintaining the Yemen business development strategy, in line with the country Strategic Action Plan (SAP).
- Prepare for and lead Go/No-Go meetings for funding opportunities as required.
- Oversee the development of all concept notes and proposals, acting as lead writer or editor, and develop efficient process-management tools for proposal development.
- Define and communicate clear roles, responsibilities and timelines for each department, and facilitate cross-departmental coordination.
- Review all proposal documents to ensure coherence across narratives, logframes and budgets, and ensure that outputs are accurate, complete, compliant with the solicitation and submitted on time.
- Interpret donor solicitations and donor-specific rules and regulations to ensure responsive and compliant proposal design.
- Act as focal point with HQ and external consultants during proposal review, editing and submission.

**Grants administration**

- Maintain a broad and deep understanding of IRC policies and of the terms and conditions across the grant portfolio and ensure that the Grants unit develops and maintains the procedures needed to apply them.
- Review donor agreements and coordinate their review and signature with the relevant HQ offices; coordinate approval of pre-award spending as required.
- Coordinate all project revisions, amendments, extensions and budget realignments, in consultation with the DDP.
- Ensure timely and productive facilitation of Project Cycle Management (PCM) meetings, including design, opening, implementation, closing and lessons-learned meetings; capture action points and follow up to completion.
- Maintain and regularly disseminate the grants tracker, including grant opening and closing dates, and share portfolio updates internally and with the Awards Management Unit.
- Work with the Finance team to review spending plans and financial health, and to ensure effective spending, amendments, and closeout.
- Ensure that the Opportunity Tracking Information System (OTIS) is updated and maintained throughout the award lifecycle.
- Ensure that the grants filing system is respected and that all donor contractual documents, reports and key correspondence are filed consistently in up-to-date shared libraries.
- Ensure that all communication with IRC colleagues and donors is constructive, clear and organized.
- Act as focal point for communication with HQ on all grants administration functions.

**Donor compliance and relations**

- Serve as first point of contact for grants and compliance questions in-country, and advise staff (including senior management, finance and procurement) on resolving compliance issues.
- Coordinate with HQ on specialized compliance matters as required.
- Proactively assess risks in managing donor contracts throughout the project cycle; anticipate them, inform and support all concerned, including the Senior Management Team (SMT), to take timely mitigation measures.
- Raise compliance issues early with program staff, the DDP and the SMT, and flag any projected inability to meet contractual obligations, reporting deadlines, spend rates or significant budget variances.
- Develop and update compliance cheat sheets for all grants.
- In coordination with the DDP and the Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coordinator, help ensure appropriate and effective IRC and donor visibility at program sites and in materials.
- Support donor visits and field monitoring, working with staff to plan and run them smoothly.

**Reporting**

- Oversee the development and delivery of all internal and external reports in collaboration with the program, finance, supply chain and METAL teams.
- Maintain a comprehensive reporting tracker and regularly update relevant team members on upcoming deadlines and specific report requirements.
- Lead the production of well-written, high-quality reports that meet donor and IRC requirements.
- Review all reports and supporting documents for completeness and accuracy.
- Coordinate HQ and technical unit reviews and approvals before donor submission.
- Ensure strict compliance with internal and donor deadlines.

**Team leadership and staff management**

- Supervise the Grants team and provide on-the-job training, especially in proposal development and report writing.
- Set clear expectations and annual performance objectives, give regular and timely feedback, and complete documented semi-annual performance reviews and probationary reviews.
- Hold regular one-to-one meetings with each direct report, at minimum monthly.
- Ensure clear roles and responsibilities and a logical portfolio allocation across team members.
- Provide development plans that build technical capacity, encourage knowledge sharing within the team, and support career growth.
- Oversee recruitment of new staff as required, and ensure comprehensive onboarding and training for new hires.
- Approve and manage time, attendance and leave requests to ensure adequate coverage; ensure accurate, timely timesheet submission.
- Work with Human Resources to identify, document and address performance issues in line with national staff employment policies.
- Promote staff care and well-being, model healthy work-life balance, and support appropriate responses to identified staff care needs.
- Act in accordance with the IRC Global HR Policies and Procedures, and model a high standard of compliance with all applicable policies.

**Partnerships and program approach**

- Help ensure that Go/No-Go discussions and program design are consistent with the SAP partnership ambition and program approach.
- Embody IRC’s partnership values (partner as equals, partner first) and engage partners proactively in program design and development.
- Promote full partner collaboration in program design and resource allocation, and in key program delivery decisions through PCM.
- Ensure that IRC’s partnership strategy, approach and management are well represented and resourced in donor proposals and reports.
- Participate in due diligence and collaborative partnership risk management as appropriate, and support negotiation of partner sub-award agreements with the Partnerships Lead, the Awards Management Unit and the Compliance Unit.
- Coordinate with the Partnerships Lead to obtain any donor approvals relating to partnerships.
- Provide training, coaching and mentoring to partners on grants management, compliance, business development and proposal writing, in line with partner project support plans.
- Participate in reviewing the performance of the partner, of IRC and of the partnership, including successes, challenges and lessons learned.
- Serve as a member of the PWG and share responsibility for delivering its functions.

**Representation and country program management**

- In coordination with the DDP, build and maintain effective working relationships with donors, government actors, UN agencies, international and local NGOs, local partners and other stakeholders, and represent IRC in relevant meetings, consultations and forums.
- Contribute actively to country program strategy discussions, including SAP revision.
- Stay up to date on new IRC priorities, policies and process changes, and keep the Grants, Partnerships and METAL teams informed.
- Provide training and mentoring to country program staff on donor compliance, program reporting and proposal development.
- Perform other relevant duties as assigned by the supervisor to further IRC programs.

**Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, social sciences, business administration or a related field. Equivalent experience in a similar role may be considered in place of formal education.
- Training in grants management, donor compliance or project cycle management is preferred.

**Experience**

- At least five years of humanitarian grants management experience in a multi-donor, multi-sector environment.
- Demonstrated experience supervising and developing a team.
- Demonstrated experience in an inter-departmental coordination role, balancing the priorities of a range of stakeholders.
- Extensive experience leading the development of large, multi-sector funding proposals.
- Advanced skills in drafting and compiling donor reports, including coordinating inputs and producing complex documents across departments.
- In-depth knowledge of institutional donor compliance. Knowledge ECHO, EU, FCDO, GFFO, SIDA, BMZ and USAID requirements is a particular advantage.
- Experience in a conflict-affected or protracted crisis setting is strongly preferred; experience in a range of operational settings is preferred.

**Skills and abilities**

- Exceptional English writing and editing skills, with the ability to draft and edit detailed donor documents with minimal oversight.
- Proven program design, METAL, logframe and budget-building skills.
- Strong leadership, coaching and team-management skills, including the ability to lead a team in a complex working environment.
- Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritize multiple tasks and deadlines.
- Proven ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and stakeholders, and to represent IRC effectively with donors.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with meticulous attention to detail.
- Strong cross-cultural communication skills, and sensitivity to interpersonal differences and a range of viewpoints.
- Reliable, patient and resilient; able to work independently in a fast-paced, insecure environment with restricted personal freedoms.
- Full professional competency in Microsoft Office, especially Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
- Strong commitment to IRC’s vision, mission and core values.

**Language and travel**

- **Language:** Fluency in written and spoken English is required. Arabic is desirable.
- **Travel:** Occasional travel to program sites, subject to security conditions.

**Commitment to client responsiveness:** IRC Yemen places the people we serve, our clients, at the center of our programming. Staff have an important role in supporting client-responsive programming by raising awareness among communities and clients of existing feedback mechanisms, how to use them, and how to access services and understand eligibility, and by helping build an institutional culture that listens to clients and uses their feedback to shape program design and delivery.

**Returning national candidates:** We strongly encourage national and returning national candidates to apply. If you are a citizen of Yemen currently residing outside your home country, you may be eligible for a relocation package, depending on IRC’s operational needs and the requirements of the role.

**Equal opportunity:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit, without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, age, marital status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Diversity and inclusion:** IRC strives to build a diverse and inclusive team at all levels, one that embodies our culture statement and creates a working environment characterized by critical reflection, power sharing, debate and objectivity, so that we can deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Gender equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce, including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Mission France - Référent.e projet pluridisciplinaire migration F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Référent.e projet pluridisciplinaire migration pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Au sein du projet Migration de MSF sur le Littoral Nord, vous contribuez à définir, planifier, mettre en œuvre et suivre les activités médico-psycho-sociales et de protection. En lien étroit avec la coordination du projet et les référent·es techniques, vous veillez à la qualité des soins, à la bonne articulation des différentes disciplines et à une réponse cohérente, adaptée aux besoins des personnes accompagnées.

Vous supervisez les responsables des pôles santé somatique, santé mentale, travail social, ainsi que promotion et médiation en santé. Votre rôle est de faire vivre une approche pluridisciplinaire, qui prend en compte à la fois les situations individuelles et les besoins de santé des communautés.

**Principales responsabilités :**

**Piloter et suivre les activités du projet**

- Planifier, mettre en œuvre et suivre les activités sur le Littoral Nord : soins de santé primaires, santé mentale, protection, maraudes et activités post-traversée.
- Contribuer à l’évolution de la stratégie du projet selon le contexte et les besoins du terrain, et participer aux évaluations et missi Eons exploratoires si nécessaire.
- Suivre les indicateurs et les données d’activité, analyser les tendances et proposer des actions correctives pour renforcer la pertinence, la qualité et l’efficience des opérations.
- Participer à l’élaboration du plan annuel, des propositions de projet, des budgets et des rapports opérationnels et narratifs.
- Garantir une prise en charge pluridisciplinaire et centrée sur la personne
- Favoriser la collaboration entre les équipes médicales, de santé mentale et de protection, notamment par des échanges professionnels adaptés et le respect du secret médical partagé.
- Organiser la gestion des situations complexes médico-psycho-sociales et de protection, en priorisant les besoins, en clarifiant les limites de prise en charge et en assurant des parcours de référencement et de suivi lisibles.
- Veiller au consentement des personnes avant tout partage d’informations, à la confidentialité et à la protection des données.
- S’assurer de parcours adaptés pour les personnes victimes de violences sexuelles et pour l’accès aux soins d’avortement sécurisé, avec des procédures opérationnelles claires.
- Intégrer les retours des personnes accompagnées et les besoins exprimés par les communautés dans l’amélioration des activités.

**Encadrer, soutenir et développer les équipes**

- Superviser les responsables de pôles, clarifier les rôles et responsabilités et assurer un suivi régulier des performances.
- Identifier les besoins de formation et accompagner le développement des compétences, notamment en matière d’intégration de la protection dans la prise en charge médicale.
- Contribuer au recrutement, à l’intégration et à la formation des nouveaux membres de l’équipe, en coordination avec les ressources humaines.
- Promouvoir un environnement de travail collaboratif et respectueux, faciliter la coopération pluridisciplinaire et traiter les difficultés d’équipe.
- Gérer les ressources et veiller à la qualité et à la sécurité
- Veiller à la disponibilité et à la bonne gestion des médicaments, dispositifs, consommables et matériels médicaux, en coordination avec la logistique et le service approvisionnement.
- Suivre les consommations et préparer les commandes médicales, dans le respect des protocoles et des procédures applicables.
- Contribuer à l’application des mesures d’hygiène, de sécurité et de prévention des risques sanitaires pour le personnel, ainsi qu’au suivi des événements indésirables.
- Veiller à la sécurité des personnes accompagnées, au fonctionnement des mécanismes de plaintes et de retours, et au signalement des situations d’abus.

**Représenter MSF et travailler en réseau**

- Entretenir des relations de travail constructives avec les partenaires associatifs, les autorités sanitaires et les acteurs locaux, notamment l’ARS et les structures de santé pertinentes.
- Représenter MSF dans les réunions externes liées aux activités et contribuer aux actions de plaidoyer en coordination avec le·la coordinateur·rice de projet.
- Participer à l’analyse du contexte et à la mise en place des protocoles de sécurité adaptés aux opérations.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Diplôme de médecine ou diplôme paramédical obligatoire.
- Au moins 3 ans d’expérience en lien avec le diplôme et expérience antérieure sur le terrain avec MSF indispensables.
- Expérience de projets Migration indispensable.
- Expérience confirmée de gestion d’équipe et de management pluridisciplinaire, notamment dans les domaines de la santé mentale, des soins de santé primaires et de l’accès aux droits.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Leadership, vision stratégique, sens de l’organisation, capacité à développer les équipes, esprit de coopération, flexibilité et gestion du stress dans des environnements changeants et parfois difficiles, y compris la nuit.
- Permis B souhaitable.

**Langues et outils :**

- Français courant obligatoire et anglais maîtrisé à l’oral souhaité.
- La connaissance d’autres langues est fortement désirée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 598.40 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an.
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

jobs.title: Consultancy - PowerBi Dashboard
jobs.description:
## BACKGROUND

In April 2026, the IMPACT HR Department initiated the development of an HR Power BI Dashboard to strengthen data-driven decision-making and improve workforce planning across the organization. The project responds to the current fragmentation of HR data across multiple systems, including the software where our base of employees is (CORE), JIRA, and country-level trackers, which requires significant manual consolidation and limits timely access to strategic workforce information.

The purpose of this assignment is to finalize, validate, and fully operationalize the HR Power BI Dashboard by developing automated data integrations, ensuring data quality, and delivering user-friendly reporting tools. The dashboard will serve as a centralized source of HR information, providing real-time visibility on key workforce indicators and reducing administrative reporting efforts.

The dashboard is expected to provide automated reporting on key HR metrics, including workforce composition, recruitment performance, vacancy management, turnover, expatriation processes, contract management, diversity indicators, and workforce planning trends, enabling HR and senior leadership to make informed and timely decisions.

## THE ASSIGNMENT

The assignment consists of finalizing, validating, and operationalizing IMPACT’s HR Power BI Dashboard to establish a centralized, automated, and reliable HR analytics platform. The overall objective of the assignment is to strengthen data-driven decision-making, improve workforce planning capabilities, and enhance the efficiency, quality, and accessibility of HR reporting across the organization.

The consultant will begin by conducting a review of existing HR data sources, reporting processes, and dashboard requirements to assess current functionality, identify data gaps, and validate business needs. Based on this assessment, the consultant will design and implement the required technical solutions to integrate data from CORE, JIRA, and other relevant HR data sources in excel files into a single reporting environment.

Building on these integrations, the consultant will finalize and refine interactive Power BI dashboards that provide real-time visibility on key HR indicators, including workforce composition, recruitment performance, retention and turnover trends, diversity metrics, expatriation processes, contract management, and workforce planning. Particular attention should be given to ensuring data accuracy, consistency, user experience, and alignment with the reporting needs of HR Leadership and Senior Management.

The consultant will also establish appropriate data validation and quality assurance mechanisms to ensure the reliability and sustainability of the dashboard over time. Comprehensive technical documentation and user guidance materials will be developed to support future maintenance and administration of the platform.

Finally, the consultant will conduct testing, validation, and knowledge transfer sessions with relevant stakeholders, incorporate feedback into the final product, and support the deployment of a fully operational HR Power BI Dashboard. The assignment should ensure that IMPACT possesses a sustainable, user-friendly, and scalable HR reporting solution capable of supporting strategic workforce management and organizational decision-making.

The consultant will be expected to review and finalise the existing HR Power BI dashboard, building on the work already completed. The assignment should focus on correcting identified data and categorisation issues, integrating missing historical data sources, developing missing or enhanced indicators and visuals, and improving the usability of the dashboard.

The existing dashboard and the detailed HR Dashboard Gap Mapping will be provided as reference material for the consultancy work.

### Deliverable 1: Workforce dashboard finalisation

Finalise the“IMPACT’S Workforce: all staff” dashboard, including:

- Review and correct the workforce categorisation and mapping, in particular the treatment of National Staff, International Staff, Global non-HQ staff and HQ Staff.
- Establish the required connection to the relevant National Staff Excel data source, including the historical source required to report workforce evolution.
- Add HQ Staff to the gender split.
- Add workforce evolution including National Staff.
- Enhance geographic reporting with a graph showing staff distribution by country and staff type, with particular visibility of the National versus International split and percentage by country.

### Deliverable 2: Global and International staff profile and evolution

Finalise the current HQ/International staff profile and evolution pages around the revised population definition: eg Global (HQ-based staff, International Staff working for Geneva/Global teams and SYNI) and International (non-Global International Staff). Apply this categorisation consistently to the relevant metrics, visuals and filters.

Develop or adjust the following:

- Numerical staff distribution by country, complementing the existing map, with comparison against the equivalent point one year earlier.
- Average age evolution allowing analysis by Global versus International population, in addition to the existing analysis by grade.
- Review the categorisation used in relevant grade and contract-type visuals.
- Redesign the filters so that they are useful and consistent across the relevant dashboard pages.
- Where required because current 2025 data is not reliable, connect the relevant historical Excel data source (excel file) for historical comparisons.

### Deliverable 3: Diversity dashboard redesign and completion

Reorganise and complete the diversity reporting, including:

1\) Overall GN/GS ratio monitoring. Develop an overview allowing HR to monitor:

- overall Global South/Global North ratio for the combined relevant workforce at the selected reporting date; evolution of the GS/GN ratio;
- GS/GN ratio by grade; evolution of this ratio by grade.

2\) Diversity profile: Develop a complementary diversity profile in which the GN/GS filter operates on the relevant analytical visuals, including:

- contract type;
- gender;
- country of assignment;
- nationality list/ranking.

Ensure that the nationality ranking can be filtered by GN/GS so that Global South nationalities can be isolated without requiring a duplicated page.

In addition:

- Restore an expatriation evolution visual and create/connect the required historical Excel-based source.
- Include the National versus International share of surges within the diversity dashboard as an indicator of National Staff deployment, even if this information is also available within surge reporting.

### Deliverable 4: Staffing dashboard, vacancy reporting

Complete and enhance vacancy/recruitment reporting, including:

- Integrate the historical Excel source for vacancies, correcting/reconciling reporting for 2025 and earlier with the current data.
- Add a historical view of the number of vacancies remaining open at the end of each month.
- Develop vacancy-rate reporting, with clear numerator and denominator definitions.
- Develop a separate due-vacancy rate, covering vacancies already due versus the relevant total population of positions.
- Add the split of vacancy openings between New Position and Replacement.
- Add reporting on the initial planned duration of positions opened, including:
- overall average initial duration;
- breakdown by country where supported by the source.
- Add vacancy closure outcomes using the relevant historical/agreed categories, including National Recruitment, Internal Mobility, External Recruitment and Cancelled Position.
- Add reporting on positions closed by candidate type, including External Recruitment, ongoing staff and former staff.

### Deliverable 5: Recruitment duration analysis

Develop a coherent duration-to-close analysis for recruitment, including:

- overall average duration to close a position;
- duration by closure/recruitment type, including external versus internal;
- duration by country;
- duration by grade.

The dimensions should work as filters or drill-downs around the same core duration metric rather than as disconnected measures.

The consultant should also review the existing operational time\_to\_done\_hours measure against the recruitment duration-to-close definition and ensure that the appropriate metric is used for HR recruitment reporting.

### Deliverable 6: Surge reporting

Complete the surge reporting, including:

- Integrate the historical Excel source for surges, correcting/reconciling reporting for 2025 and earlier with the current data.
- Add a country breakdown/ranking of surge requests opened, allowing HR to identify the countries generating the highest surge demand.
- Add the number/share of surges filled by National Staff versus International Staff, including historical evolution where the data allows.

### Deliverable 7: Staff retention, exits and turnover

Introduce Staff Retention Rate as a headline KPI at the beginning of the “Staffing our Teams dashboard”.

In addition, develop the underlying exit/turnover reporting, supported by the current source and historical Excel data, including the required voluntary/non-voluntary exit analysis and associated historical reporting.

### Deliverable 8: Staff Performance and Development indicator

Introduce a new Staff Performance and Development indicator showing: % of eligible staff with an appraisal carried out during the past year. The metric definition and treatment of the reporting/reference period should be validated during implementation.

### Deliverable 9: Contractual visibility

Develop the contractual-visibility reporting using the already connected current data source, including:

- contract duration of current International Staff in Grades 3 and 4;
- contract duration granted to newly onboarded International Staff in Grades 3 and 4;
- number of International Staff whose contracts end within the following four months, by grade;
- International Staff whose contracts end within the following four months as a percentage of total International Staff;
- The existing source is connected, but the usability/readability of this reporting needs to be improved.

### Deliverable 10: Cross-cutting data validation and technical documentation

- For all developments and data-source integrations described in the deliverables above, the consultant will:
- reconcile newly integrated historical data with current reporting to ensure continuity of the relevant indicators;
- validate the calculations developed or modified as part of the assignment;
- test and resolve identified inconsistencies in workforce categorisation and other reporting logic;
- document the principal calculation rules and definitions used for the new or modified indicators;
- document the relevant data sources, source dependencies and connections introduced or modified through the assignment;
- document known data-quality limitations that cannot be resolved within the scope of the consultancy;
- provide sufficient technical documentation to allow the HR team or a future Power BI developer to understand and maintain the solution.

### Deliverable 11: Final dashboard testing and handover

Following completion of the developments above, the consultant should:

- conduct functional testing of the new and modified measures, visuals and filters;
- support HR validation against the agreed gap/needs mapping;
- correct issues identified during validation;
- ensure consistent filter behaviour across the dashboard;
- provide the final updated Power BI dashboard together with the information required for its continued maintenance.

The list above describes the substantive development requirements to be costed by the consultant. Existing visuals and functionality that are to be retained without substantial modification, as well as minor dashboard clean-up such as removal of obsolete visuals, are not listed as separate deliverables. The detailed HR Dashboard Gap Mapping will be shared with the selected consultant as the functional reference for implementation.

jobs.title: Junior National Lawyer (Ukrainian Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
**General Background**

GRC are policy makers, lawyers and development experts dedicated to promoting accountability and strengthening justice systems through the application of international law. With ongoing operations in some of the world’s most complex legal and security environments, Global Rights Compliance continues to provide specialised legal expertise, policy solutions, and strategic advisory services to uphold justice and strengthen the rule of law globally.

Mobile Justice Teams (MJTs) are groups of local and international experts and practitioners collaborating with and in support of local justice actors, such as Ukraine’s Office of the Prosecutor General (OPG) and Regional Prosecutor Offices (RPOs), to advance Ukraine's capacity to investigate and build complex command-level cases into international crimes through tailored support and the institutionalisation of international standards and best practices. The MJTs are organised across thematic areas to address context-specific and cross-cutting legal issues. The teams work in the most affected regions of Ukraine to provide advisory and case-building support, focusing on supporting prosecutors and investigators in their investigations and prosecutions.

We are seeking a Junior National Lawyer to join our team in Ukraine. The Junior National Lawyer assists the team working on a specific category of international crimes (e.g. crimes against humanity, genocide, and aggression) or a designated thematic area within the team’s mandate (e.g. air strikes, detention-related crimes, pillage of essential resources, SGBV, crimes against and affecting children, occupation-related crimes).

**The Role**

- Support legal and factual research.
- Support in developing standard operating procedures, tools and methodologies, providing strategic advice on investigations and case-building, and delivering tailored capacity-building initiatives
- Prepare drafts of legal documents including legal analysis, advisory notes, memorandum, submissions to UN agencies etc.
- Assist in delivering other project objectives.
- Assist in maintaining regular dialogue with other actors, including international organisations and local CSOs, to foster meaningful collaboration, avoid duplication and promote complementarity and harmonisation of support.
- Facilitate meetings and other interactions with relevant stakeholders including interpretations where required.
- Assist in the ongoing development of the team’s work by identifying potential areas for future activity and collaboration.
- Perform other tasks as requested (or authorised) by the MJT Lead and reasonably foreseen under the scope of work.

**Your Background**

- Qualified in law (LLB mandatory).
- 2+ years professional legal experience practising law within a law firm, prosecution service, court, etc.
- Knowledge of the Ukrainian justice system, including criminal and criminal procedural legislation.
- Ideally ICL / IHL experience, in a practical application.
- Practical experience working with Ukrainian justice actors, preferably within a national or international prosecution team.
- Flexible, able to work in a changeable environment.
- Administratively competent.
- Able to provide written and oral translations of legal texts.
- Practical experience of working with highly sensitive material and an ability to demonstrate the requisite skill in storing, sharing and working with such material.
- Fluency in English and Ukrainian, written and verbal skills.
- Fluency or competency in Russian is advantageous.
- Ability to travel to the affected regions of Ukraine is desirable.

**MSF International**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

**CONTEXT**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s sections, associations and branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

The International Secretary General (ISG) plays a key role in defining with the MSF Executive Committee (ExCom) the movement’s ambitions and priorities and ensuring their implementation. They are supported by the Senior Executive Committee (ExCom) Officer and the International Secretariat Support Officer in the full accomplishment of the mandate entrusted by the MSF Movement.

The International Secretariat Support Officer:

o Reports hierarchically to the Senior ExCom Officer;

o Has frequent check-ins with the International Secretary General and the Deputy Secretary General (DSG);

o Works closely with the Executive Assistants to members of the ExCom and the International Board (IB);

o Interacts with the MSF International team, the MSF Movement, and interlocutors outside MSF.

The International Secretariat Support Officer operates at the heart of the organisation, fulfilling a pivotal role in creating the conditions that allow the ISG and DSG to perform at their highest level. This means managing complex schedules, preparing briefing materials, coordinating cross functional communication, and acting as a trusted point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. It involves anticipating needs before they arise, filtering information intelligently, and ensuring priorities stay aligned with organisational goals. The postholder helps to maintain momentum, clarity, and efficiency across the core MSF International Secretariat Team.

**PURPOSE OF THE JOB**

The position of International Secretariat Support Officer will support the International Secretary General and the Senior ExCom Officer on tasks which allow them to focus on the development and follow-up of key executive dossiers. These tasks include some foundational administrative support, but the International Secretariat Support Officer supports far beyond administrative coordination - they act as a strategic partner, proactively anticipating needs, streamlining decision-making, developing substantial background briefings, and helping to ensuring the International Secretary General’s time is focused on the highest impact priorities.

**ACCOUNTABILITIES**

1. **Support to the International Secretary General and Deputy Secretary General (70%): serve as a trusted partner helping to prioritise initiatives and manage competing demands, anticipating needs and proactively resolving issues.**

- Provide proactive full diary management, full travel management, and full administrative support; act as a “gatekeeper” and protecting the ISG and DSG’s time to allow their focus to remain on the priority areas.i. Support with annual international administrative planning.
- Prepare briefing materials, agendas, and follow up actions for non-ExCom internal and external ISG/DSG meetings. Where relevant, track key initiatives, follow up with stakeholders, maintain visibility into progress, and conduct research and synthesise information. This may be applicable to the International Office (IO) Leadership Team (LT) and IB.
- Draft, edit, and proofread correspondence (emails, letters, social media, and reports) with a high-level of accuracy, handling sensitive information with the highest level of confidentiality.

**2. Support to the Senior Executive Committee Officer (30%): serve as a trusted partner helping to prioritise initiatives and manage competing demands, anticipating needs and proactively resolving issues.**

- Provide administrative support for the coordination of the Executive Committee; proactive scheduling, vote and record-keeping, information-sharing, and maintenance of online groups and spaces.
- Initiates and leads on logistical arrangements for Core and Full ExCom F2F meetings.
- Produce content as requested, including email and outcome drafting.

**3. Other tasks as requested by the International Secretary General and Senior Executive Committee Officer.**

**AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY**

- Complexity of the MSF structure and wide scope of ISG engagements
- Autonomy to proactively anticipate needs and make decisions within as per agreed direction and frameworks
- Fast-paced dynamics and changing engagements

jobs.title: Intersectional Procurement Manager - RDC
jobs.description:
**Rattachement hiérarchique:** Cette position est redevable devant le Intersectional Supply Emergency Steering Committee (ISSC), composé d’un représentant du département approvisionnement de chaque centre opérationnel participant aux activités d’achat mutualisées.

Rattachement fonctionnel Intersectional Procurement Advisor à la Global Procurement Unit

**Domaine:** Supply

**Lieu:** Intervention d’urgence Ebola, Bunia, République démocratique du Congo (RDC)

Contrat Contrat à durée déterminée à 100 %

**Nombre de postes:** Deux postes, l’un pour une prise de fonctions immédiate et l’autre pour une prise de fonctions dans un délai de 3 mois, en février 2027.

**Durée:** 3 mois plus période de suivi post affectation Ebola de 21 jours

**Date de début:** 01 Décembre 2026

**Fermeture publication**: 09 Novembre 2026

**I. CONTEXTE**

Une épidémie d’Ebola, causée par le virus Bundibugyo, a été déclarée le 18 mai 2026 dans la province de l’Ituri (RDC). Depuis, la situation évolue rapidement et se propage aux zones avoisinantes. MSF a mis en place une réponse d’urgence pour soutenir les autorités sanitaires et les communautés touchées.

Compte tenu de l’évolution de la situation, cette réponse s’inscrit probablement dans la durée. MSF se prépare donc à une intervention prolongée, articulée autour de plusieurs phases de déploiement. Afin de garantir la sécurité opérationnelle et le respect des normes de MSF, tout le personnel est tenu de se conformer au code de conduite de l’organisation, ainsi qu’aux procédures spécifiques liées aux interventions contre Ebola.

OCBA, OCB et OCG s'approvisionnent localement à Bunia, un marché instable, limité et partagé avec de nombreuses autres ONG qui se disputent les mêmes fournisseurs. Bunia est également la principale plaque tournante d'approvisionnement pour les projets menés par d'autres organisations de la communauté.

**II. OBJECTIF DU POSTE**

L’Intersectional Procurement Manager (IPM) définit et met en œuvre la stratégie d’achat pour les catégories d’achat identifiés comme prioritaires, afin de répondre aux besoins communs des activités d'urgence des centres opérationnels (OC) présents à Bunia,.

L’objectif de ce poste est de renforcer la disponibilité et la qualité des biens et services, d’améliorer la maîtrise des risques, et de mutualiser les efforts d’approvisionnement afin de générer des économies sans compromettre la qualité. Il vise également à simplifier la gestion des catégories d’achats gérés en intersection et éviter la mise en concurrence entre les centres opérationnels.

Le poste a par ailleurs pour finalité d’assurer une approche cohérente et harmonisée des approvisionnements au sein du mouvement MSF, à travers l’alignement des méthodologies, pratiques, outils et processus d’achat, dans le respect des protocoles, standards et procédures de MSF ainsi que de la réglementation locale, afin de renforcer la capacité des centres opérationnels à répondre efficacement aux besoins opérationnels.

Pour ce poste spécifiquement le titulaire sera chargé de coordonner les activités « source to contrat » pour les achats locaux pour les trois OCs, en mettant l'accent sur l'évaluation du marché et la négociation des contrats avec les fournisseurs afin de garantir les prix et la disponibilité des produits.

**III. RESPONSABILITÉS CLÉS**

Domaines d’intervention requis et objectifs spécifiques :

1. **Piloter les achats stratégiques inter-OC en contexte d’urgence**

• Identifier et hiérarchiser les principales catégories d’achats effectués de manière récurrente par OCBA, OCB et OCG à Bunia.

• Réaliser une évaluation rapide du marché : identification des fournisseurs, qualification, vérification juridique et administrative, validation des prix – en s’appuyant dès à présent sur les informations disponibles dans le cadre du programme national,

• Négocier et signer des accords-cadres intersectoriels / contrats locaux pour ces catégories, validés par les coordinateurs opérationnels/techniques de OCBA, de OCB et de OCG.

• Consolider les besoins confirmés et les projections basées sur des scénarios (et non sur des prévisions historiques) des trois OC.

• Tenir à jour une liste de fournisseurs indiquant leur statut de conformité et les prix validés, partagée entre les trois OC.

**2. Gérer un réseau fonctionnel pour les achats intersection**

• Organiser des réunions régulières des parties prenantes et rendre compte régulièrement au Comité de pilotage des urgences d’approvisionnement et au GPU.

• Briefer les nouveaux points focaux achat / Supply et répondre à d’autres demandes de briefing ad hoc.

• S'assurer que les départements financiers reçoivent leurs copies des contrats et soient informés pour vérifier si les prix facturés sont conformes aux prix convenus.

• Veiller à ce que les produits soumis à la TVA soient répertoriés en collaboration avec le BIP (bureau des protocoles) et que l'application de l'exonération de la TVA soit accrue.

• Garantir la cohérence entre les termes contractuels des fournisseurs et les documents nécessaires pour l'application de l'exonération de TVA.

• Faire du réseautage avec d'autres organisations – Ex. Log Cluster et autres plateformes.

• Coordonner le travail avec les Responsable achats des OCs (PMs) afin d'éviter les chevauchements et la concurrence sur les mêmes activités. Le IPM se concentrera sur les catégories mutualisées convenues tandis que les PMs se concentreront sur les priorités propres à chaque OC, tout en collaborant étroitement sur les besoins opérationnels.

• Assurer l'implication adéquate des parties prenantes clés, y compris les référents techniques pour la validation des sources et des articles, afin de garantir une mise en œuvre réussie de la stratégie d’achat.

• Communiquer en temps opportun sur les problèmes, opportunités ou toute mise à jour importante liée à l'activité achat intersection.

• Fournir un soutien technique et accompagner le personnel des OCs pour contribuer au développement des meilleures pratiques et des capacités en matière d’achats.

**Hors périmètre :**

• Validation technique des sources pour les articles logistiques et médicaux nécessitant une telle validation.

• Passer les commandes aux centrales d’achat.

• Les activités transactionnelles comme le placement des commandes, la réception des marchandises et la facturation restent du ressort de chaque OC.

• Évaluation du marché en dehors de Bunia.

**IV. RESULTATS ATTENDUS**

• Signature de contrats intersectoriels pour ces catégories, et pas seulement une liste de fournisseurs.

• Liste de fournisseurs avec vérification de conformité et prix validés, partagée entre OCBA, OCB et OCG.

• Vue d’ensemble consolidée des besoins confirmés par rapport aux projections basées sur des scénarios.

**V. CRITERES DE SELECTION**

**Connaissances pratiques / techniques**

• Diplôme universitaire en administration des affaires, gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, achats ou similaire.

• 4+ ans d'expérience en achats/approvisionnement, incluant analyse de données, sourcing, négociation complexe et gestion de contrats ou dans un domaine similaire comportant les mêmes composantes.

• Connaissances approfondies des processus de chaîne d'approvisionnement et de budgétisation financière requises.

• Expérience internationale (en dehors du pays d'origine) et des missions de terrain dans le domaine des achats ou d'autres fonctions de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, en tant que responsable ou chef d'équipe d'approvisionnement ou postes similaires, avec MSF est requise.

• Connaissance du RDC et expérience en intelligence de marché sont des atouts.

• Une expérience professionnelle dans un contexte d'urgence constitue un atout

**Planification et organisation**

• Esprit analytique, compétences organisationnelles et autonomie indispensables.

• Orientation sur les résultats et sens du service client requis.

**Communication et Influence**

• Capacité à travailler de manière transversale, dans un environnement multiculturel et à distance sont nécessaires.

• Capacités d'écoute, diplomatie avérée et aptitude à développer un réseau professionnel.

• Capacité à motiver et mobiliser les différents interlocuteurs.

**Exigences Pratiques**

• Capacité avérée à travailler avec Office et ERP, en particulier une maîtrise d'Excel est indispensable.

• Maîtrise du français parlé et écrit, niveau minimum B2, est obligatoire. Swahili/Lingala sont un atout.

• Résident de l’espace Schengen ou titulaire d’un visa Schengen un atout (permet un déploiement rapide).

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. MSF expects all staff to share this commitment and promote an environment where abuse and misconduct is not tolerated.**

**We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.**

**Note: All offers of employment will be subject to reference checks and to appropriate screening checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her/their understanding of these recruitment procedures.**

About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

**Job summary**

Provide case management services to children in accordance with established guidelines, prepare reports, and develop plans that address their needs. The role includes providing support and counseling, referring children to appropriate services, ensuring confidentiality, following up on cases, and documenting success stories, while maintaining the protection and safety of beneficiaries.

**Qualifications and education requirements**:

Technical diploma or bachelor's degree in Social Work, Social Sciences, Psychology, Counseling, or another relevant field.

Completion of CP Case Management training.

Familiarity with and commitment to humanitarian and protection standards.

**Required Skills and Experience**:

- Effective communication skills.
- Priority and time management.
- Data analysis
- Ability to work remotely.
- Report preparation skills.
- Technical computer skills
- Outlook
- Teams
- Word
- Excel
- PowerPoint
- OneDrive

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

- Provide case management services to children and adhere to the relevant case management guidelines.
- Prepare case reports and provide recommendations.
- Develop case management plans that address identified needs based on risk assessments and comprehensive assessments, seeking support from the supervisor when necessary.
- Provide support and counseling services to children and their parents or caregivers.
- Refer children and families to other services when necessary.
- Maintain the confidentiality and privacy of case management files.
- Ensure that the best interests of the child guide every service provided and every decision made concerning the child.
- Close cases in accordance with the minimum standards outlined in the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
- Safeguard the psychological and physical well-being and safety of beneficiaries.
- Maintain the case management tracking sheet, ensuring that all relevant information is recorded and updated monthly according to case developments.

- Regularly update the service mapping to ensure its availability and relevance to the case management process.
