- Provide technical guidance to field teams to ensure the relevance, quality, and effectiveness of DRR, CCA, SRSP, AA, MPCA, RRM, and FSL interventions
- Ensure programmes comply with standards, donor requirements, humanitarian principles, and sector best practices
- Support the development of high-quality proposals, budgets, technical narratives, and implementation plans
- Ensure timely submission of mission reports in accordance with internal and external reporting systems
- Strengthen integrated approaches by mainstreaming gender, protection, accountability, environment, nutrition, and inclusion across programmes in coordination with other departments
- Anticipate operational and technical challenges and support teams in identifying timely solutions
- Participate and support regular project review meetings and follow through sector specific action plans and agreements
- Support CD and DCD budget oversight of on-going resilience programs

**Objective 3: Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning, and Knowledge Management**

- Ensure the collection, consolidation, analysis, and use of programme data to support evidence-based decision-making and programme improvement
- Support the development of monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) systems and resilience indicators
- Lead learning reviews, technical workshops, evaluations, and knowledge-sharing initiatives
- Monitor changes in disaster, climate, food security, livelihood, and social protection contexts to inform programme adaptation
- Document and disseminate best practices, lessons learned, and technical guidance across the mission

- Facilitate effective coordination between programme teams, support departments, and field offices
- Promote technical leadership and visibility in resilience and humanitarian programming

**Objective 5: Team Leadership, HR management and Capacity Strengthening**

- Ensure clear roles, effective communication, and collaboration across teams and departments
- Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, learning, punctuality and continuous improvement

**Objective 6: Emergency Preparedness, Response, and Security Compliance**

- Coordinate with Heads of Base, Security Focal Points, and Logistics teams to maintain safe programme implementation
- Ensure timely reporting of security incidents and compliance with mission security protocols by all supervised staff and immediately report incidents to the Logistics Coordinator and Country Director
- Support business continuity and operational readiness Action Against Hunger’s team and offices in coordination with Humanitarian Action Manager

## **Do you meet the profile required criteria?**

- Expertise in vulnerability, risk, capacity, and needs assessments, including participatory and community-based approaches.
- Experience in developing anticipatory action frameworks, contingency planning, early warning-early action systems, and forecast-based interventions.
- Strong understanding of climate risk analysis, adaptation strategies, and resilience-building approaches for vulnerable communities.
- Expertise in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL), knowledge management, and evidence generation.

- Proven experience managing programs related to DRR, CCA, SRSP, AA, MPCA, RRM, and FSL in disaster-prone, climate-vulnerable, conflict-affected, or fragile contexts.

jobs.title: Deputy Lead – Autonomous Region of Bougainville
jobs.description:
## Job Brief

This role is open to both suitably qualified International and PNG national candidates.

**Program Background**

DT Global has been engaged by the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to manage the next phase of Australia’s investment in strengthening the delivery of law and justice services in Papua New Guinea for a 4-year period to 31 December 2027.

The Australia-PNG Law and Justice Partnership (APLJ) seeks to contribute to PNG’s law and justice sector capacity to provide inclusive, safe, secure and accountable law and justice foundations for peaceful and prosperous communities, equitable economic development and private sector growth. The program aligns with GoPNG’s law and justice sector goal of ‘building peaceful and prosperous communities together’.

In the Autonomous Region of Bougainville, APLJ maintains an office in Buka and works closely with the ABG and law and justice stakeholders to support Bougainville’s evolving law and justice sector.

A central element of this work is the Shaping Bougainville Justice (SBJ) program, an ABG-led reform agenda supporting the progressive development of a law and justice system tailored to Bougainville’s constitutional, institutional and social context. SBJ involves complex and interrelated policy, legislative, institutional and operational reforms, including the development and transition of justice institutions and functions to Bougainville. This requires close cooperation between the ABG, GoPNG law and justice agencies and other stakeholders, together with sustained technical assistance to translate policy and legislative reforms into functioning institutions and improved services for the people of Bougainville.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [**www.dt-global.com**](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**The Role**

The Deputy Lead – ARoB is responsible for the effective day-to-day operation of the APLJ Buka office and the coordinated management and delivery of the ARoB activity portfolio. Working under the direction of the ARoB Lead, the position oversees operational systems, personnel and resources; coordinates implementation across workstreams; monitors budgets, risks and performance; and ensures timely, compliant and value-for-money delivery of activities supporting law and justice priorities in Bougainville. The Deputy Lead supports stakeholder engagement and acts for the ARoB Lead when formally delegated.

This is a unique opportunity to work in post-conflict Bougainville. This role will be part of planned initiatives aimed at strengthening the accessibility, responsiveness, accountability of law and justice services throughout the ARoB. Respectful relationship building, understanding of Bougainville’s context, and a ‘do no harm’ approach in all aspects of the role will be critical.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position:

[**https://tinyurl.com/v9krzkrz**](https://tinyurl.com/v9krzkrz)

**About You**

**Qualifications**

· Relevant tertiary qualification in Human Resource Management, Organisational Development, Business Management, International Development or a related discipline

**Essential Experience and Knowledge**

· Minimum 10 years’ experience in leading a human resources function, preferably on donor-funded international development programs and/or with complex organisations

· Demonstrated experience managing teams and supporting change management processes

· Demonstrated ability in HR policy and strategy development, workforce planning, employee relations, talent management and performance management functions

jobs.title: Burundi Stagiaires Charges des Operations Informatiques (Fixed-Term)
jobs.description:
## Description de l’organisation

Fondée en 2006, One Acre Fund aide 5,5 millions de petits exploitants agricoles à accroître la productivité de leurs exploitations. Présents dans neuf pays qui regroupent les deux tiers des agriculteurs africains, nous fournissons des produits agricoles de qualité, des plants d'arbres, des crédits accessibles, des formations agricoles modernes et une large gamme d'autres services agricoles. En moyenne, ce modèle permet à tout agriculteur d'augmenter ses revenus et ses actifs de plus de 35 % sur les terres qu'il exploite, tout en améliorant durablement sa résilience. Tout cela est rendu possible grâce à notre équipe de plus de 9 000 employés à temps plein, issus d'horizons et de professions diverses. Pour en savoir plus, consultez notre article: [Pourquoi travailler ici](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here).

Avec la saisons 27A, nous servons 612147 ménages de cultivateurs répartis dans 1222 collines dans les 5 provinces du pays à savoir:

- Gitega: Bugendana, Gishubi, Gitega, Nyabihanga, Mwaro, Kiganda, Muramvya, karusi, Shombo;
- Butanyerera: Muhanga, Matongo, Kiremba, Tangara, Kayanza, Ngozi, Muhanga, Tangara, Kirundo;
- Buhumuza: Butaganzwa, Nyabitsinda, Muyinga, Butihinda, Ruyigi, Cankuzo, Gisuru, Gisagara
- Bujumbura: Isare
- Burunga: Matana.

Rejoignez le programme de stage des jeunes professionnels One Acre Fund en tant que Stagiaire Chargé des opérations informatiques pour lancer votre carrière. Nous vous donnons les moyens de progresser dans ce programme conçu pour les jeunes professionnels motivés. Vous aurez droit à une expérience de travail dans l'une des principales institutions du secteur agricole au Burundi et au-delà, où vous résoudrez des défis, développerez des solutions et apprendrez auprès de dirigeants inspirants.

En tant que Stagiaire Chargé des opérations informatiques, vous soutiendrez les opérations IT quotidiennes du pays en participant à la configuration des équipements informatiques, à la gestion des stocks, au dépannage de base, à l’assistance aux utilisateurs et à la documentation.

Sous la supervision directe de l’équipe IT, vous apprendrez et appliquerez les procédures standard de support informatique, les pratiques de gestion des actifs et le dépannage réseau de base dans un environnement stimulant et passionnant.

Conformément aux processus, politiques et procédures établis, les principales responsabilités de ce rôle comprennent :

- Exécuter les tâches assignées dans le système de gestion des services et escalader rapidement lorsqu’un accompagnement est nécessaire.
- Assister la configuration des appareils, le contrôle qualité, l’étiquetage et la configuration de base.

- Soutenir les étapes de déclassement et d’élimination des équipements.
- Participer aux contrôles de routine des appareils et aux réparations de base sous supervision.
- Fournir une assistance de base pour les terminaux et les logiciels (aide aux mots de passe/comptes, problèmes d’applications courantes, dépannage de base du système d’exploitation) dans le respect des SLA.
- Documenter les symptômes, les démarches effectuées et les résultats pour permettre une escalade efficace.

Dès que possible

jobs.title: Program Assistant, NVPPA
jobs.description:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Program Background:**

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which the International Rescue Committee (IRC) serves newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal. NVPPA operates alongside other federally funded programs, such as initial resettlement services and Matching Grant, and is designed to complement rather than replace or duplicate these programs.

**Job overview**

Program Assistant role provides the administrative backbone for NVPPA's direct financial assistance. Working from requests submitted by Career Navigators, this position is responsible for preparing requests for disbursement: confirming that required documentation is on file, that the requested use of funds aligns with the participant's approved Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) and ORR's eligible use categories, and that the vendor or training provider is an active, appropriately licensed or accredited entity. This role will work closely with the Finance team, Business Operations team, and will report directly to the Deputy Director.

**Major responsibilities**

**Direct financial assistance processing**

1. Receive direct financial assistance requests from Career Navigators and prepare them for administrative review and processing.
2. Initiate a Purchase Request or Purchase Order (PR/PO) or a non-PO invoice in the system for expense processing.
3. Liaise closely with Finance Coordinators to ensure direct financial assistance requests are correctly recorded in the system using appropriate budget codes and accurate client IDs.
4. Follow IRC Global Supply Chain protocols and IRC financial controls in all transactions.

**Vendor Management**

- Make sure new vendors are created in the system before initiating a direct financial assistance request. This will require completing forms within and outside the system, collecting up-to-date information from the vendors, and ensuring there are no discrepancies.
- Liaise closely with the Master Data Management Team to ensure vendor cards are active and updated.

**Records and reporting support**

1. Maintain complete and audit-ready financial assistance records for each participant, including request forms, approvals, vendor documentation, invoices, and proof of payment.
2. Liaise closely with Career Navigators to ensure a signed client Receipt of Payment is received and kept on file.
3. Record assistance transactions and service data accurately and on time in IRC's financial system and in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO), as assigned.
4. Flag anomalies, incomplete requests, duplicate requests, or vendor concerns to the Finance Manager and program leadership.

**Coordination and administrative support**

1. Coordinate with Career Navigators to resolve missing documentation or eligibility questions so that participant requests are not delayed.
2. Respond to vendor and training provider inquiries about payment status.
3. Attend regularly scheduled virtual meetings as part of the review, evaluation, and program maintenance process.

**Job Requirements**

1. 1-2 years of demonstrated experience in a human services field, preferably in a nonprofit or social services setting.
2. Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to build rapport with clients by phone and video.
3. Ability to deliver services remotely to clients across states and time zones, protect client confidentiality and sensitive documents, and work independently as part of a fully virtual team.
4. Experience managing a high-volume of requests, with strong organization, prioritization, time management, and follow-through.
5. Ability to build and maintain productive internal and external relationships.
6. Ability to research and navigate workforce, education, and social service systems in unfamiliar local markets.
7. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, video conferencing, and remote collaboration tools, and with tracking and reporting information in a database.
8. Commitment to anti-racism, ongoing learning, and equitable service to all eligible clients.
9. Fluency in spoken and written English.

**Preferred**

1. Undergraduate degree in a related field
2. Experience in workforce development, career coaching, or case management.
3. Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant.
4. Experience with Efforts to Outcomes (ETO).
5. Familiarity with credential evaluation, professional licensing, or recertification pathways.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $19-$28/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Project Director – CDC Capacity Building for Global, Regional, and National Immunization Programs (Global)
jobs.description:
***About Corus:*** Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class organizations working to deliver the holistic, lasting solutions needed to end extreme poverty once and for all. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our brands. Our nonprofit and for-profit subsidiaries include IMA World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and Farmers Market Brands. Our more than 800 employees around the globe are experts in their fields and dedicated to helping the world's most vulnerable people break the cycle of poverty and lead healthy lives. Further details about the organization can be found at: [https://corusinternational.org](https://corusinternational.org/)

Today, IMA offers extensive expertise in managing and implementing highly successful and complex donor-funded programs in global health security, vaccine-preventable disease immunization, nutrition, maternal and child health, health systems strengthening (HSS), malaria, HIV/AIDS, and neglected tropical diseases (NTDs). IMA has managed an average of $100 million annually over the last four fiscal years, through grants and contracts from the United States Government (including CDC, DoS, and others), FCDO, World Bank, the Global Fund, UNDP, and private donors.

***About the job:***

IMA World Health, a member of Corus International, is seeking a **Project Director** to lead an anticipated 5-year CDC-funded project titled **- Capacity Building for Global, Regional, and National Immunization Programs**.

The program's goal is to strengthen immunization programs in priority countries so they can better prevent, control, and eliminate/eradicate vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs) like polio, measles, and rubella, reduce illness and death from these diseases, and respond to emerging global health threats. will build stronger systems in priority countries to prevent, detect, and respond to VPDs. This includes improving immunization services, strengthening VPD surveillance, and expanding the capacity to prepare for and manage outbreaks. The Recipient will also create and carry out targeted approaches to reach high-risk groups who are un- or under-immunized. Additionally, the Recipient will promote long-term sustainability of immunization programs-such as supporting evidence-based decisions through National Immunization Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs)-and enhance program evaluation to increase impact.

The Project Director will lead the technical approach of the project and serve as the primary liaison with CDC, country governments, and other implementing development partners on the progress and reporting of all activities under the award. S/he will ensure the project's goals, objectives, and strategy are achieved and that contractual requirements are met on time and within budget. S/he is responsible for directing the project team with an integrated vision, applying effective leadership and strategic planning skills, management experience, outstanding interpersonal skills, and strong written and oral communication skills. The Project Director supervises the day-to-day work of staff and oversees project implementation to ensure quality programming.

The Project Director also ensures that all management systems, from technical to MEL to finance, actively support timely and accurate project reporting and cost effectiveness for successful implementation of the project. The Project Director is also responsible for ensuring compliance with Corus's policies and procedures and CDC rules and regulations, including responsibility for ensuring sub-awardee compliance and monitoring the quality of program implementation.

The competencies required to be successful in this position include a theoretical and practical understanding of global health systems and integration strategies to address prevention, early detection, and response to infectious disease threats; programming in conflict and fragile settings; personnel and project management skills; the ability to motivate and lead teams; and the demonstrated ability to operate at advanced levels of authority and accountability for achieving results. The candidate must demonstrate proven experience in coordinating public health systems and resources in fragile settings. The position will report to the Program Director, Global Health Security and Immunization. The Project Director will be expected to visit project sites periodically.

**The Project Director will report to Corus HQ and may be remote, depending on circumstances.**

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Provide overall management, strategic direction, and technical leadership to the project to achieve expected project results within budget and timeframe.
- Serve as principal liaison to CDC and the country governments, ensuring high levels of coordination, while nurturing relationships with all key stakeholders (including partner organizations at the national and subnational level) on administrative, financial, and programmatic matters related to the project.
- Liaise with CDC, other donors, and implementing partners and stakeholders, to ensure coordination of and harmonization with other relevant public health mechanisms, private sector engagement, and USG activities globally.
- Ensure results-oriented technical components and high-quality and timely deliverables and reports.
- Oversee implementing partners and advise on technical issues.
- Lead project teams (e.g., technical, program, finance, and operational staff) to ensure program tasks, deliverables, and responsibilities are met; staff management includes hiring, supervising, and mentoring project staff.
- Oversee project deliverables, including ensuring programmatic and financial report preparation and high-quality timely submission, and ensuring cross-cutting issues are effectively integrated into project implementation.
- Direct preparation of annual work plans, project activity updates, and other project-related communication and reporting materials.
- Represent the project in all technical, policy, and programmatic forums at all levels (country, national, and international). Identify lessons learned and best practices for external dissemination.
- Oversee implementing partners and advise on technical issues.
- Ensure compliance with CDC rules and regulations, working with the headquarters grants and contracts team.

**Qualifications:**

- Advanced graduate degree in public health, medicine/nursing, international development, or related field experience. Doctoral degree or MD/MPH an asset.
- Minimum of 10 years' experience in the implementation and management of international donor/CDC funded health projects, with substantial knowledge and experience related to immunization systems and vaccine preventable disease surveillance highly preferred.
- Proven technical expertise using new approaches to build capacity in national immunization and VPD surveillance programs.
- Knowledge of USG framework of global health security and its immunization related implications and priorities, especially in fragile contexts, and familiarity with CDC policy and strategies.
- Knowledge of and experience with CDC rules and regulations required.
- Demonstrated experience in developing and maintaining strong relationships with government agencies, international donor agencies, and private sector stakeholders.
- Experience collaborating and coordinating with local and national host government agencies and aligning program activities and results with national strategies.
- Demonstrated leadership qualities, including technical, management, and evaluation expertise for complex programs in resource-constrained countries; prior experience as a Project Director/Chief of Party for CDC-funded projects similar in scope and size is required.
- Strong staff supervision skills and demonstrated ability to coordinate programs with partners from a broad range of backgrounds and experiences; demonstrated ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams.
- Experience building the capacity of national non-government partner organizations and government systems to achieve CDC's goal of strengthening national ownership for future funding.
- Strong communication skills, including both written and oral presentation skills; proven ability to develop and communicate a common vision among diverse public and private partners.
- English fluency with professional proficiency in writing required
- Working fluency or better in other language an asset, especially French, also potentially Spanish, Arabic, etc.
- Experience working fragile contexts preferred.
- Ability to travel to project sites as needed.

jobs.title: Education and Child Protection Officer (Training Facilitator)
jobs.description:
The **International Rescue Committee (IRC)** responds to the world’s most pressing humanitarian crises and helps people whose lives and livelihoods have been shattered by conflict and disaster. In Poland, IRC is supporting refugees and host communities with economic recovery, livelihood programs, and social protection initiatives to foster resilience and self-reliance.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

REAL Talk is a two-year, EU-funded project that prevents gender-based violence (GBV) and cyber GBV among adolescents aged 11–16 in Poland, Italy and Estonia. It works with adolescents and with the adults around them: caregivers, especially fathers and male caregivers, and school staff and educators. IRC Poland leads the project’s work with caregivers and delivers all activities in Poland, together with IRC Italia (coordinator), Una Casa per l’Uomo, the University of Tartu and the International Child Development Initiatives (ICDI).

The **Education and Child Protection Officer (Training Facilitator)** is IRC Poland’s facilitator for REAL Talk. Working in tandem with another facilitator, the post holder delivers sessions of the project’s Cross-Cultural Socio-Emotional and Relational Education Model: dedicated sessions for adolescent boys, the “Cycle of Aware Fatherhood” workshops for fathers and male caregivers, and training for teachers and educators. The post holder also takes part in the project’s mandatory transnational training for facilitators, which starts on 12 November 2026.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Facilitation and delivery**

- Facilitate sessions of the Model with adolescents aged 11–16 at the partner school: dedicated sessions for boys, and mixed-gender groups co-facilitated with the female facilitator. Groups have 10–15 adolescents and follow a series of 5–8 sessions of 100–120 minutes, reaching around 40 adolescents in Poland.
- Deliver the “Cycle of Aware Fatherhood”: a series of 4–6 workshops of 60–90 minutes for small groups of 3–8 fathers and male caregivers (around 15 in total), on masculinity, emotional literacy, non-violent role modelling and parenting in the digital age.
- Co-facilitate, with the female facilitator, mixed-gender information sessions for parents and caregivers on adolescent relationship violence, social media and online safety (around 80 caregivers).
- Co-deliver training for school staff (around 30 teachers, in groups of about 10) and online basic training sessions for educators across Poland (around 80 participants).
- Create a safe, trauma-informed and non-judgmental space in every session. Respond to disclosures following IRC procedures and refer participants to support services through the agreed referral pathways.

**2. Preparation and learning**

- Take part in, and prepare for, the mandatory transnational capacity-building sessions for facilitators (online, in English). The first session is on 12 November 2026, and further sessions follow through January 2027.
- Study the Model and adapt session plans and materials to the Polish context and to participants with migrant or refugee backgrounds, together with the female facilitator and the project lead.
- Prepare sessions, materials and logistics, and stay in contact with participants, especially fathers, in line with the project’s engagement and retention strategy for caregivers.
- In November 2026, support colleagues, where needed, in focus group discussions and key informant interviews for the project’s research on online masculinity norms.

**3. Partnerships and coordination**

- Coordinate with the partner school (leadership, teachers and school counsellors) on schedules, venues, consent procedures and the recruitment of participants.
- Plan, deliver and debrief sessions jointly with the female facilitator, and exchange practice with facilitators from the project’s partner organizations in Italy and Estonia.
- When requested, support other REAL Talk activities in Poland, such as consultations with adolescents and caregivers, the Champions workshop, the national webinar and the study visit to Poland.

**4. Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL), safeguarding and compliance**

- Administer pre- and post-session questionnaires and feedback tools, and collect signed attendance lists and consent forms, following MEAL guidance and data protection (GDPR) requirements.
- Record sex-disaggregated session data and write short session reports. Contribute lessons learned to the project’s deliverables and donor reports.
- Apply the IRC Child Safeguarding Policy, the IRC Poland Child Protection Response Procedure and the IRC Way standards at all times. Report any concern immediately to the Protection and Safeguarding Coordinator.
- Make sure session materials carry the EU funding acknowledgement required by the donor.
- Mainstream gender equality, inclusion and a Do No Harm approach in all activities.
- Carry out other duties assigned by the supervisor, within the scope of the project.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

- **Working time:** part-time. The indicative workload is around 230 hours over the assignment; the exact working time is confirmed in the offer.
- **November 2026 – January 2027:** onboarding, five online transnational training sessions of about two hours each (the first on 12 November 2026) and, if needed, support to the research activities. The successful candidate must be able to start in time for the first session.
- **February – May 2027 (dates to be confirmed):** delivery of sessions with adolescents, fathers, parents, teachers and educators, as the partner school is confirmed and the school semester allows. The rest of the assignment covers follow-up and reporting.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree (Master’s preferred) in education, pedagogy, psychology, social work, sociology, gender studies or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Additional training in facilitation, child protection or trauma-informed practice is an asset.

**Experience**

- At least 2 years of experience facilitating group sessions or workshops with adolescents and/or adults (such as parents or teachers) in a school, NGO, youth or community setting.
- Experience addressing sensitive topics, such as relationships, consent, violence, masculinity or online risks, in a participatory and non-judgmental way.
- Experience in gender equality, GBV prevention, engaging men and boys, positive parenting or child protection is strongly preferred.
- Familiarity with approaches such as Engaging Men through Accountable Practice (EMAP), Engaging Adolescent Boys in Accountable Practice (EABAP) or My Safety, My Wellbeing is an asset.
- Experience working with refugee or migrant communities, or in EU- or donor-funded projects, is an asset.

**Skills and competencies**

- Strong facilitation skills: able to build trust quickly with adolescent boys, fathers and teachers, and to manage group dynamics.
- Commitment to gender equality, an anti-racist and Do No Harm approach, and to modelling respectful behaviour. Ability to work in close tandem with a co-facilitator and in an international team.
- Good planning and organizational skills, attention to detail and reliable record keeping.
- Good digital skills: Microsoft Office, Teams, Zoom or Google Meet, confidence delivering online sessions, and an understanding of social media and online safety.
- Languages: Polish (fluent or native) and English (upper-intermediate or higher, as the transnational training is delivered in English). Ukrainian and/or Russian is an asset.
- Willingness to travel within Poland, and to deliver some sessions in the late afternoon or evening.
- Right to work in Poland.

Appointment is subject to the safeguarding screening for work with minors required by Polish law and IRC policy, including a certificate from the National Criminal Register, a check in the Register of Sexual Offenders and, where applicable, certificates from other countries of residence.

*We encourage male candidates to apply as the sessions are to be delivered to adolescent boys.*

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: 100 PLN/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Intensive Case Management Caseworker
jobs.description:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Job Overview:**

The Intensive Case Management Caseworker will address barriers to safety and wellness for especially vulnerable refugees, asylees, and other ORR-eligible populations. The ICM caseworker will be expected to provide strengths-based, client-centered case management to single-headed refugee households; survivors of domestic violence and gender-based violence; older refugees; youth and young adults without parents or permanent guardians; refugees experiencing mental health or psychological difficulties; refugees with physical disabilities or medical conditions; unanticipated refugee arrivals and secondary migrants; and refugees who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer (LGBTQ). They work closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:** Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Determine client eligibility for ICM programming and conduct intake assessments, review program expectations, outcomes, and confidentiality with each potential client.
- Develop individualized, SMART Self-sufficiency plans for each client enrolled in the ICM program.
- Evaluate client progress every six months during active program enrollment to determine the client’s progress towards goals and work with the client to identify new needs and actions needed.
- Assist clients in navigating healthcare and social service systems, which may include helping clients apply for benefits and attend and schedule appointments.
- Conduct community outreach and maintain a strong network of service providers that meet client needs. The ICM caseworker may also be expected to maintain a strong relationship with local and state level refugee coordinators and health coordinators to ensure client needs are met.
- Provide clients with extended orientation on a variety of topics such as women’s health, navigating transportation systems, and navigating physical healthcare systems at the local level.
- Respond to client crises, with guidance from supervisor as needed.
- Assist clients with requesting financial assistance when applicable and track the received financial assistance within case files.
- Maintain up-to-date documentation in client’s case file to ensure services are properly documented throughout the client’s service period; document all services provided in IRC’s database, Efforts to Outcomes (ETO).
- Attend relevant trainings and meetings at the local and national level.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Safety and Wellness Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers
**Other Internal and/or external contacts:** The Intensive Case Management Caseworker (Safety and Wellness Caseworker) will be responsible for developing relationships within the network of external relations with grant partners, social service agencies, and government entities.

***Internal:** IRC RSS, Employment team, Youth program and other IRC programs*

***External:** social service agencies, community education presentations, and community outreach*

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $23.50). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Travel Agency Services (North Africa) for Journalists under the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices Project
jobs.description:
Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) invites travel agencies legally registered and licensed in Tunisia to submit offers for booking round-trip flights to Tunis for fellows from Libya, Algeria and Morocco under its “MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices 2026–2027” programme. This will be a service contract running from 10 November 2026 to 30 June 2027. Interested agencies are invited to apply by 9 November 2026.

**1. Introducing MiCT**

Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) is a non-profit organisation that delivers expert media services in complex and challenging contexts with passion, precision, and agility. Through our collaborative work with our partners, we foster transparent, inclusive, and fair dialogue, supporting resilient societies that thrive.

Across three continents and 15 countries, MiCT facilitates the training of journalists and media producers, programme and content development, radio and film production, magazine and book publishing, media research and monitoring, and supporting our partners’ financial viability.

**2. The MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices Programme**

Since 2022, the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices has supported at-risk journalists and media professionals from conflict regions, enabling them to continue their essential work in safety. The programme is part of the Hannah Arendt Initiative and a member of the Journalists in Distress Network. It offers stipends, security and equipment support, (mental) health services, legal aid, relocation, and professional development through regional hubs.

**3. Services required**

The fellowship brings participants from North Africa to Tunis for stays of typically two to three months. MiCT is seeking a reliable, transparent and cost-effective travel agency for the 2026 and 2027 fellow groups. The expected volume is small, about 8–9 round-trip tickets per year (maximum 10), mostly from Libya, followed by Algeria and Morocco.

The tender documents, including the Terms of Reference and Annex 1 – Bidder Application Form, are available without registration in a read-only online folder at: [CfP-FCV-NorthAfrica-2026-02](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1f_ub_P1UK_vNiAqvToATGjC-K0vIYvUg?usp=sharing)

jobs.title: Country Director – Yemen – based in Sanaa
jobs.description:
## **Fixed term contract: 12 months, from 01/12/2026**

## **PUI all around the world**

**With its 40 years of experience, Première Urgence Internationale:**

- Supports close to **6** millions beneficiaries
- With more than **100** millions € yearly budget
- Present in **22** countries, on **5** continents

Thanks to the work and commitment of :

- More than **2000** national staffs
- Around **200** expatriates from 45 different nationalities
- And **90** employees at HQ

PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity.

Learn more on [our history](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [our values](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [our areas of intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

## **What about the Country Director ?**

As Country Director, you will be responsible for the smooth functioning and the development of the mission. For this purpose, you will be responsible for:

- **Safety & Security:** You will be responsible for the safety & security of the mission.
- **Programmes:** You will coordinate the teams and ensure that the programmes implemented on the mission are properly carried out. You will also monitor needs and suggest new operations and development tracks for the mission.
- **Human Resources:** You will ensure that the mission is adequately staffed and supervise the teams (defining objectives, follow-up).
- **Logistical, administrative and financial monitoring:** You will ensure that logistical and administrative practices in place respect PUI procedures and formats and are in compliance with donors’ rules and regulations.
- **Medical and technical monitoring:** You will ensure that medical and technical practices respect PUI’s procedures and formats and are in compliance with PUI’s operational framework and policy.
- **Representation:** You will represent the association in its relations with partners, donors, the media and different authorities.
- **Relations with Headquarters:** You will ensure that information is properly circulated between Headquarters and the field and ensure that due dates are respected.

## **The challenges that await you**

- Ensuring access to affected populations in a complex and evolving operational context
- Strengthening engagement and negotiations with authorities to facilitate programme implementation
- Navigating a changing humanitarian and security landscape
- Developing sustainable funding strategies in a context of limited resources and growing humanitarian needs.

## **What you will need to succeed**

- **Training**: You hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in Humanitarian action: project management, a technical background related to one of our activity sectors, in human resources management, financial management…
- **Experience**: Strengthened by minimum 3 years of experience in the field with international NGOs in project coordination, you master international team management, the project cycle and security management. Previous experience as Country Director or in an equivalent position would be appreciated. You already worked with Première Urgence Internationale? It would be a definite asset!
- **Skills**: You master humanitarian project management and team management, you have a detailed knowledge of donors’ prerequisites. You also have excellent writing skills.
- **Qualities**: You are a good communicator, both in writing and orally. You demonstrate good team spirit, leadership skills and the ability to make decisions, trustworthiness and a sense of responsibility, organisational skills, reactivity, ability to be thorough and to adapt. You have a strong resistance to stress and particularly in unstable circumstances.
- **Languages**: English has no secrets for you! All the better, it is mandatory for this position. If you speak Arabic and/or French, it would be a definite asset.

## **A word from the manager**

*« With nearly 20 years of experience in Yemen, PUI has built strong relationships and earned community acceptance, enabling us to reach remote and hard-to-access areas across both the North and South. Health remains at the heart of our work and is a key priority in the humanitarian response. Over the years, PUI has developed strong expertise in health, sexual and reproductive health (SRH), and nutrition, delivering essential services to underserved communities where needs are greatest. Our Yemen team is deeply committed to the humanitarian response and to PUI’s mission of supporting the most vulnerable. Ready to make a difference? Join us! »*

## **PUI will offer you**

- **Status:** Cadre with a Fixed-Term Contract
- **Monthly Gross Income:** 3 740,00 – 4 010,00 EUR depending on your experience in International Solidarity + 50€ per semester of seniority with PUI
- **Insurance** including medical coverage and complementary healthcare, 24/24 assistance and repatriation
- **Housing** in collective accommodation
- **Daily Living Expenses** (« Per Diem »)
- **Break Policy:** 5 working days each 2 months + break allowance
- **Paid Leaves Policy:** 5 weeks of paid leaves per year + return ticket every 6 months

## **Our commitments**

PUI is committed to preventing all forms of inappropriate behavior in the workplace, including harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct, while promoting the well-being of children and adults with whom PUI interacts.
PUI expects all employees to fulfill their professional duties and responsibilities in accordance with PUI’s Ethical Framework. All employees will receive appropriate training and commit to promoting, disseminating, and upholding the principles set forth in its Ethical Charter.
The holder of this position may potentially have access to personal data concerning children and vulnerable adults as part of their work (Category 2 in the safe recruitment risk classification). Consequently, all recruitments will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate background checks, which include criminal record and counter-terrorism financing checks.
Première Urgence Internationale considers the diversity of nationalities, genders, beliefs, backgrounds, and statuses within its Human Resources as a major asset for its humanitarian work. The organization is therefore committed to strictly upholding the principle of non-discrimination throughout its recruitment process.
We are dedicated to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.
Please note that Première Urgence Internationale shall not in any case request a financial contribution for administrative costs related to recruitment. Any such information would be fraudulent, please disregard it.
**Early applications are encouraged, as we may close the process earlier than the deadline mentioned above if a suitable candidate is identified.**
You recognize yourself in this profile and you adhere to our commitments? You feel ready to take up the challenge and to join PUI great family?

jobs.title: Venezuela: Auxiliar de Logística en Terreno (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Medialuna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales (Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad) la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El/La Auxiliar de Logística en terreno brindará apoyo operativo y logístico para el desarrollo de las jornadas de salud en terreno, especialmente aquellas realizadas a través de las unidades móviles de salud de la Cruz Roja Venezolana. Será responsable de apoyar la preparación, movilización, organización y disposición de los medicamentos, insumos, materiales, mobiliario y equipos necesarios para garantizar el adecuado funcionamiento de las jornadas, de acuerdo con la planificación operativa y los procedimientos establecidos.

Asimismo, participará activamente en el alistamiento de las unidades móviles, las actividades de cargue y descargue, el montaje y desmontaje de los espacios de atención y el control de los suministros utilizados durante cada jornada. Apoyará la verificación, organización y reposición de los materiales y equipos al finalizar las actividades, asegurando que las unidades móviles queden debidamente acondicionadas para su siguiente despliegue. El cargo requiere disponibilidad para adaptarse a los horarios y necesidades operativas de las jornadas, así como para desarrollar actividades logísticas en diferentes condiciones de terreno, conforme a los procedimientos de la Cruz Roja Venezolana y los lineamientos de la Cruz Roja Alemana.

*Reporte*

El/La Auxiliar de logística en terreno reportará al Oficial de Cadena y Suministro.

*Lugar de trabajo*

Caracas, con disponibilidad para viajar a los sitios de implementación de proyecto.

*Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:*

Será el/la encargado(a) de:

- Apoyar al responsable de cadena de suministro en el alistamiento logístico de las actividades de salud, preparación para desastres y respuesta a emergencias, de acuerdo con la planificación operativa.
- Recibir, contar y verificar los medicamentos, insumos, materiales y equipos que ingresen a la bodega, contrastándolos con los documentos de entrega y reportando cualquier diferencia o daño.
- Clasificar, ubicar y almacenar los bienes de forma ordenada y segura, siguiendo los procedimientos establecidos y las indicaciones del personal responsable para el manejo de medicamentos.
- Mantener actualizados los registros de inventario, incluidas entradas, salidas, traslados, devoluciones, existencias y ubicación de los bienes.
- Realizar conteos físicos periódicos y reportar diferencias, pérdidas, daños, productos próximos a vencer o necesidades de reposición.
- Preparar y verificar los bienes requeridos para jornadas de salud, actividades de preparación, despliegues y operaciones de respuesta, utilizando las solicitudes aprobadas y listas de comprobación.
- Apoyar el cargue, descargue y despacho de bienes, verificando sus cantidades y condiciones físicas. Organizar la carga dentro del vehículo para protegerla durante el traslado, en coordinación con el conductor.
- Registrar y archivar los movimientos de bienes mediante actas de entrega y recepción, notas de salida, formularios de inventario y demás soportes requeridos.
- Verificar los bienes y equipos que regresen de las actividades en terreno, registrar las devoluciones y organizar su almacenamiento o reportar las necesidades de reposición.
- Apoyar el montaje y desmontaje logístico de jornadas y operativos, incluida la organización de espacios, mobiliario, carpas, señalización, materiales y equipos.
- Mantener ordenados y disponibles el archivo físico y digital de los soportes logísticos para seguimiento, rendición de cuentas y auditoría.
- Cuidar los bienes, equipos e insumos bajo su responsabilidad y reportar de inmediato pérdidas, daños, incidentes de seguridad o incumplimientos de los procedimientos logísticos.
- Realizar otras tareas de bodega y apoyo logístico relacionadas con el cargo, según las necesidades de las actividades.

**Para calificar como constructor(a) del sistema humanitario venezolano, deberá cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:**

- Educación secundaria completa (bachiller). Formación técnica o estudios en logística, administración, gestión de almacenes o áreas afines (deseable).
- Experiencia comprobable en labores operativas de bodega, almacenamiento, organización, control de inventarios, preparación, movilización y despacho de suministros.
- Experiencia en actividades de cargue, descargue, organización de mercancías, equipos y materiales, así como en el mantenimiento del orden y las condiciones adecuadas de almacenamiento.
- Experiencia o conocimientos básicos en el manejo de medicamentos, insumos médicos o suministros humanitarios (deseable).
- Capacidad para organizar y mantener actualizados inventarios, registros de entradas y salidas, actas de entrega y recepción y otros soportes logísticos.
- Manejo básico de hojas de cálculo y otras herramientas informáticas para el registro y reporte de información (deseable).
- Capacidad y disposición para realizar actividades de alta exigencia física, incluyendo la movilización frecuente de equipos, mobiliario y suministros, cargue, descargue, instalación y desmontaje de espacios de atención, siguiendo las medidas de seguridad correspondientes.
- Disponibilidad para trabajar en terreno y adaptarse a los horarios operativos de las jornadas de salud, incluyendo actividades de alistamiento previo y posterior, horarios extendidos y fines de semana, cuando las necesidades operativas lo requieran.
- Capacidad para trabajar de forma independiente y en equipo, siguiendo instrucciones, procedimientos establecidos y medidas de seguridad.
- Experiencia en contextos de emergencia, jornadas de salud, actividades comunitarias o trabajo con voluntariado (deseable).
- Experiencia con el Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Medialuna Roja (deseable).
- Compromiso con los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y de la Medialuna Roja.
- Fluidez oral y escrita en español.

jobs.title: Emergency Coordinator – SYRIA – based in Damascus
jobs.description:
## **Fixed term contract : 8 months from 01/12/2026**

## **Deadline for application: 20/11/2026**

## **PUI all around the world**

**With its 40 years of experience, Première Urgence Internationale :**

- Supports close to **6** millions beneficiaries
- With more than **100** millions € yearly budget
- Present in **22** countries, on **5** continents

Thanks to the work and commitment of :

- More than **2000** national staffs
- Around **200** expatriates from 45 different nationalities
- And **90** employees at HQ

PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity.

Learn more on [our history](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [our values](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [our areas of intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

## **What about the Emergency Coordinator?**

As Emergency Coordinator, under the responsibility of the Head of Mission, you will responsible for the implementation of PUI’S emergency response programmes in the country. For this purpose, you will be responsible for:

- **Programme implementation and coordination:** You will coordinate and develop the emergency response in the country, in direct link with the technical, support and field coordination.
- **Strategy:** You will be involved in strategy development and propose new interventions or new modalities for emergency responses.
- **Human Resources:** You will organize, supervise and support teams for exploratory missions, assessments and emergency response.
- **Evaluation and context monitoring:** You will ensure a continuous analysis of needs and response.
- **You will represent the organization** and coordinate with other NGO’s and external actors in emergency response.
- **Security:** You will ensure the security of the teams supervised and contribute to the security management of the mission.

## **The challenges that await you**

- The implementation period is short (8 months)
- There is no possibility of obtaining a No-Cost Extension (NCE)
- A significant budget must be spent within the eight-month timeframe
- The project may face operational and implementation challenges in the field

## **What you will need to succeed**

- **Training**: You hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in humanitarian project management. Training in Health, livelihoods, agriculture or WASH and training in Personal security training (HEAT training) would be appreciated.
- **Experience**: You are strengthened by minimum 2 years in emergency response or a similar position in an international context. You have experience in project/humanitarian coordination. An experience in assessing needs will be an added value, as well as an experience in humanitarian access strategies and negotiation. Knowledge of health programs, public health programs, public health systems and/or multisector assistance would also be appreciated. You already worked with Première Urgence Internationale? It would be a definite asset!
- **Skills**: You master the project cycle management, and have a good and proven capacity to build skills as well as coordination and organizational skills. You have excellent writing skills and know the main humanitarian donors. You also have strong communication and negotiation skills, and an ability to work in unstable contexts. You master the use of Excel and Office Pack.
- **Qualities**: You are able to work independently and to take the initiative and the responsibility in a proactive approach. You are self-motivated, flexible and adaptable to the needs of the team and organization in addition to having strong commitments in humanitarian principles. You show diplomacy and open-mindedness, resilience to stress and have good analytical skills. You are organized and able to manage priorities and varied workload. You have problem-solving and leadership skills, and are able to work and manage professionally and maturely. You are able to integrate into the local environment, taking account its political, economic and historical characteristics. You have also a strong resilience to stress.
- **Languages**: English has no secrets for you! All the better, it is mandatory for this position. If you speak Arabic and/or French, it would be a definite asset.

## **A word from the manager**

*« We are looking to recruit a candidate with strong experience in leading emergency projects. The ideal candidate should be able to take decisions independently and have solid knowledge of project cycle management. Strong communication and reporting (written) skills are also required. Previous experience in the Middle East, as well as prior experience with PUI, would be considered strong assets. Arabic language skills would also be an added value. »*

## **PUI will offer you**

- **Status:** Employé(e) with a Fixed-Term Contract
- **Monthly Gross Income :** 2 930,00 – 3 070,00 EUR depending on your experience in International Solidarity + 50€ per semester of seniority with PUI
- **Insurance** including medical coverage and complementary healthcare, 24/24 assistance and repatriation
- **Housing** in collective accommodation
- **Daily Living Expenses** (« Per Diem »)
- **Break Policy:** 5 working days every 2 months + break allowance
- **Paid Leaves Policy:** 5 weeks of paid leaves per year + return ticket every 6 months

## **Our commitments**

PUI is committed to preventing all forms of inappropriate behavior in the workplace, including harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct, while promoting the well-being of children and adults with whom PUI interacts.

PUI expects all employees to fulfill their professional duties and responsibilities in accordance with PUI’s Ethical Framework. All employees will receive appropriate training and commit to promoting, disseminating, and upholding the principles set forth in its Ethical Charter.

The holder of this position may potentially have access to personal data concerning children and vulnerable adults as part of their work (Category 2 in the safe recruitment risk classification). Consequently, all recruitments will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate background checks, which include criminal record and counter-terrorism financing checks.

Première Urgence Internationale considers the diversity of nationalities, genders, beliefs, backgrounds, and statuses within its Human Resources as a major asset for its humanitarian work. The organization is therefore committed to strictly upholding the principle of non-discrimination throughout its recruitment process.

We are dedicated to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.

Please note that Première Urgence Internationale shall not in any case request a financial contribution for administrative costs related to recruitment. Any such information would be fraudulent, please disregard it.

**Early applications are encouraged, as we may close the process earlier than the deadline mentioned above if a suitable candidate is identified.**

You recognize yourself in this profile and you adhere to our commitments? You feel ready to take up the challenge and to join PUI great family?

jobs.title: Grants and compliance coordinator (F/M) - Yemen
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Yemen**

Yemen remains one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises, after more than a decade of conflict, economic decline, climate shocks, and political instability. In 2026, over two-thirds of the population require humanitarian assistance, including 9.4 million people identified as most in need of life-saving support.

The health system is under extreme strain, with only 59.3% of health facilities fully operational and 19.3 million people requiring healthcare services, including more than 660,000 pregnant women in need of urgent care. Cholera continues to pose a major public health challenge, adding pressure to an already weakened system.

The operational environment remains highly volatile, marked by security incidents, service disruptions, funding cuts, and economic challenges that regularly affect humanitarian activities.

Médecins du Monde operates across northern and southern Yemen, with a coordination office in Sana’a and field offices in Aden and Marib. Its interventions focus on two strategic priorities:

- Supporting 29 health facilities to deliver primary healthcare services, including outpatient care, vaccination, nutrition, and reproductive health.
- Providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through healthcare facilities and community-based networks trained in identification, referral, and awareness-raising activities.

**About the role**

You will be responsible for providing technical expertise on grants and compliance while playing an essential coordination lead role amongst all departments. You are a key in ensuring all departments have a clear understanding of their role and responsibilities as regards to grants and compliance aspects.

You are actively involved in the country strategy and the overall project cycle management, especially through contracts management (including partnerships), reporting, donor communication, fundraising and compliance.

**Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator in charge of programs and the technical management of the HQ program officer, you will work in close collaboration with the general coordinator, the deputy general coordinator in charge of support services, along with other key departments when relevant (MEAL, field coordinators, etc.).

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator in charge of programs, your main responsibilities are the following:

- Support country strategy development through donor mapping, strategic opportunity identification, and donor engagement
- Lead fundraising efforts, identify funding opportunities, and build relationships with donors and key stakeholders
- Coordinate the development of grant proposals, budgets, and project design processes with technical and support teams
- Ensure effective grant management, donor compliance, contract follow-up, and timely donor communications
- Oversee the preparation and submission of high-quality donor reports and visibility materials
- Manage partnerships, including partner identification, due diligence, agreements, and performance monitoring
- Ensure compliance with donor requirements and MdM procedures, while supporting audits and risk management processes
- Facilitate coordination between departments and represent MdM in relevant meetings, forums, and donor engagements

**You are the right match if you...**

- Hold a master’s degree in one of the related fields or project management
- Have 5 years of proven experience in humanitarian and/or development contexts, with at least 2 years in a similar role
- Demonstrate strong knowledge in partnerships, multi-sectoral, regional and/or co-funded programming management
- Are skilled in developing high-quality funding proposals, reports and have experience working with institutional donors
- Experience /knowledge of the region
- Speak English fluently. Arabic is highly appreciated.

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Are uncomfortable working in complex, unstable, or rapidly evolving humanitarian contexts that require flexibility, resilience, and adaptability
- Prefer close supervision and highly structured processes rather than taking initiative, anticipating needs, and working independently
- Do not have strong written English skills or experience producing donor proposals, narrative reports, and other high-quality programme documentation
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 392 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting in December 2026
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Aden
- Frequent visits to Sanaa and to the field, depending the security conditions.

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.
