jobs.title: Engineering Analyst (Renewables), NPSA-9, DS- Kyiv or Lviv, National position
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Ukraine, through its Energy and Environment Portfolio, supports national and local authorities in restoring and transforming Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in line with the principles of sustainability, resilience, and transparency. Since the onset of the full-scale war, UNDP has prioritized assistance to ensure continuity of essential services and accelerate the green recovery of Ukraine’s public infrastructure.

Within this framework, UNDP is implementing the Technical Assistance to the Renewable Energy Solutions (RES) Programme, financed through the IKI Renewable Energy Investment Grant under the European Investment Bank (EIB) facility. The Action is delivered under the Direct Implementation Modality (DIM) and coordinated with the Ministry for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport of Ukraine, the EIB, and GIZ.

The project aims to support the large-scale deployment of renewable energy technologies—including solar photovoltaic systems, biomass installations, and heat pumps—in public buildings such as schools, kindergartens, hospitals, and municipal facilities. This initiative is designed to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, enhance local energy resilience, and accelerate Ukraine’s alignment with EU Green Deal objectives.

The Action specifically contributes to:

- Strengthening local institutional capacity for project design, procurement, and implementation of renewable energy sub-projects;

- Ensuring technical quality, financial accountability, and environmental compliance during sub-project delivery;

- Supporting municipalities to obtain prosumer (active electricity consumer) status through the development of the net-billing mechanism;

- Enhancing transparency and governance through anticorruption and sanctions-screening systems;

- Promoting knowledge exchange, digital monitoring, and replication of successful models across Ukrainian communities.

UNDP’s Technical Assistance (TA) component serves as the enabling pillar of the RES Programme. It bridges investment, governance, and capacity development by providing:

1. Institutional support and capacity building for Final Beneficiaries (municipalities, utilities, and communal institutions);

2. Technical review of documentation provided for sub-project implementation and support for incorporating applicable environmental and social requirements into procurement and contract management;

3. Contract management for goods, works, and services financed under the EIB-BMWK framework;

4. Oversight, monitoring, and integrity assurance through red-flag tracking, sanctions screening, and compliance reviews;

5. Technical assistance for operationalizing the net-billing system and helping municipalities become self-sufficient clean-energy producers; and

6. Structured knowledge and digital platforms to enable real-time data tracking, reporting, and learning.

The project forms an integral part of UNDP’s Green Energy Recovery and Decarbonization Agenda and complements related EIB-financed frameworks.

Within this context, UNDP Ukraine is recruiting a highly qualified and experienced national professional for the position of Engineering Analyst (Renewables). The position will support the implementation of the RES Programme with a specific focus on the technical review of design documentation, support to procurement processes, and monitoring of the installation and commissioning of renewable energy and energy efficiency solutions in public facilities. The Engineering Analyst (Renewables) will help ensure the quality, safety, and compliance of implemented works, contributing to energy security, continuity of public services, and infrastructure resilience under wartime and post-war recovery conditions.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of Project Manager and in close collaboration with Project team,Engineering Analyst (Renewables) will perform the following:

1.Ensure technical review and engineering support for renewable energy and energy efficiency projects.

- Review and evaluate technical project documentation, baseline information, design calculations, drawings, Bills of Quantities (BoQs) and equipment specifications for solar PV, other renewable energy and energy efficiency projects under the RES Programme, assessing their completeness, consistency and suitability for implementation.

- Review project designs for compliance with national legislation, applicable regulations, technical standards and donor requirements, and recommend corrective actions to address identified discrepancies.

- Verify sub-project budgets, cost estimates and BoQs using specialised software, such as AVK, and applicable construction cost estimation methodologies.

- Support the preparation and review of technical and contract-related documentation, including scopes of work and technical specifications, ensuring that design requirements are accurately and consistently reflected in the relevant project documentation.

- Participate in technical evaluation panels, assess bidders’ qualifications and technical proposals, including the compliance of proposed equipment and materials and the completeness and consistency of BoQs, and provide recommendations in coordination with the procurement team.

- Prepare technical clarifications in response to bidders’ questions and support the resolution of technical issues related to project documentation, design solutions, equipment, materials and implementation requirements.

- Cooperate closely with GIZ and project stakeholders to identify appropriate technical solutions and provide technical advice during project planning, design review and implementation.

- Identify and assess technical requirements, constraints and implementation risks, and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.

- Review contractors’ proposed schedules for equipment supply, installation, testing and commissioning, and provide recommendations on their feasibility and alignment with project timelines.

- Support technical monitoring of contract implementation through site visits, review of progress reports and verification of equipment and works against contractual requirements, quality and safety standards, and agreed schedules.

- Review proposed changes to designs, equipment, materials or works, assess their implications for scope, cost and timelines, and provide technical recommendations for UNDP’s consideration and approval.

- Support the technical verification of completed works and supporting documentation for acceptance and payment, including records of testing and commissioning.

2.Support in contract management, construction supervision, and commissioning of the project sites.

- Monitor and supervise the implementation of construction and installation works carried out by contractors.\Manage technical aspects of contracts with construction companies and equipment suppliers.

- Ensure that installed equipment, materials, and works comply with approved project designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, and quality standards.

- Coordinate and maintain effective communication with contractors, author and technical supervisions, final beneficiaries, and other relevant stakeholders.

- Conduct technical monitoring missions on sites and provide supervision throughout project implementation.

- Identify and address technical issues arising during construction and installation phases.

- Monitor compliance with UNDP and EIB social and environmental standards during the project implementation.

- Support testing, commissioning, and acceptance procedures for completed renewable energy installations.

- Verify completion of works and compliance prior to project handover.

3.Provision of operational support of the RES Project, monitoring, reporting, capacity building and facilitating knowledge sharing.

- Support final beneficiaries in obtaining prosumer status and completing related administrative and technical requirements where necessary.

- Monitor and evaluate the operational performance of installed renewable energy systems.

- Assess energy generation, energy savings, and greenhouse gas emissions reductions, including CO ₂ savings achieved through project interventions.

- Support the development and delivery of training activities for personnel of final beneficiaries to ensure proper operation and maintenance of installed systems.

- Collect, analyse, and document good practices, lessons learned, and project success stories.

- Contribute technical inputs to project monitoring, evaluation, and reporting requirements.

- Prepare and maintain technical records, performance data, and project documentation.

Support the dissemination of project results and knowledge-sharing activities.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

- The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, the Engineering Analyst will provide technical support for the implementation of the RES Programme, including the review of technical documentation, support to procurement, technical monitoring of contracts, and verification of completed works. The incumbent will work closely with the project team, procurement colleagues, contractors, final beneficiaries and other relevant stakeholders in accordance with the approved project document and UNDP rules and procedures

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in the field of Electrical Engineering, Civil and Industrial (Structural and Architectural) Engineering, Renewable Energy (preferably related to Solar Energy) or other closely related fields are required; or

- A first university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, with a combination of additional two years of qualifying relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of master’s degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of professional experience in implementing energy efficiency and/or renewable energy projects for public buildings and public utilities, as well as solar power station projects in the municipal sector using national financial instruments.

- Proven ability to draft, edit and produce written proposals, advisory documents, analytical documents and results-focused reports.

- Proven track record of strong knowledge of the renewable and, in particular, solar energy equipment market, including modules, inverters, monitoring systems, and Balance of System (BOS) components, as well as battery energy storage systems (BESS), with a clear understanding of technical and logistical aspects of system integration.

- Experience and good understanding of Ukrainian legislation in the field of renewable energy, in particular, the regulatory framework governing the operation of solar power plants, grid connection procedures, net-billing mechanism, and energy storage system requirements.

jobs.description:

Background

UNRWA | United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees

The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) provides essential services and humanitarian assistance to Palestine refugees across Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, the Gaza Strip and the West Bank. Its services include education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure rehabilitation, microfinance and emergency assistance.

The Department of Legal Affairs advises on and promotes the consistent interpretation and application of international law throughout the Agency. It develops strategies to promote and implement relevant areas of public international law, including international human rights law, international humanitarian law, refugee law and United Nations law. Particular emphasis is placed on the status and mandate of the Agency, the privileges and immunities of the Agency and its personnel, related responsibilities, and the observance of humanitarian principles.

The Department also provides legal advice and training on the interpretation and application of the Agency’s regulatory framework, including General Assembly resolutions, Staff and Financial Regulations and Rules, associated administrative issuances, and organizational directives. It advises Headquarters and Field departments on governance and management matters, particularly those involving administrative, contractual and procurement law. In addition, the Department provides technical expertise and advice on amendments to the Agency’s regulatory framework, including the drafting of regulations and rules, as well as the preparation and review of legal opinions on complex or sensitive financial matters, particularly those concerning the interpretation of the Agency’s Financial Regulations and Technical Instructions.

Furthermore, the Department reviews drafts of all types of Agency contractual instruments and arrangements, including complex contracts for the procurement of goods and services, memoranda of understanding with partners, and funding agreements. It also provides related training to strengthen the consistent interpretation, application and implementation of the Agency’s contractual and legal requirements.

Training component: Learning elements and expectations

Upon completion of the assignment the JPO will have/ will be able to:

- Legal research, analysis and application of international and general law.

- Legal drafting, advisory work and case management.

- Understanding of UNRWA’s mandate, operations and institutional framework.

- Interpersonal, communication and stakeholder coordination skills.

- Professional judgement, discretion, confidentiality and ethical conduct

The JPO training programme includes the following learning elements:

- Year 1 – Induction and practical learning: Structured induction, guided legal reading, mandatory UN training, daily on-the-job learning, progressive case management and potential Field Operations visits, followed by a review of learning needs and a development plan for Year 2.

- Year 2 – Advanced legal practice and collaboration: Increased responsibility for complex legal matters, including litigation, legal opinions, contracts and procurement, alongside participation in legal training and coordination across UNRWA and the wider UN system, strengthening legal expertise, professional judgement and stakeholder engagement.

- Year 3 – Consolidation and career development: Consolidation of legal expertise through progressively independent work, continued mentoring and feedback, and career development discussions to identify further learning needs and future opportunities within the UN system.

- Duty Travel and Training Allowance (DTTA) : An annual allowance of USD 4,000 supports relevant learning activities, duty travel and professional development related to the assignment.

Content and methodology of supervision:

- Director, Department of Legal Affairs. Purpose: direct supervision, guidance, advice, task assignment, performance monitoring and evaluation. Frequency: daily, through regular meetings, review of deliverables, and feedback on progress and quality of work.

- Heads of the General Law Unit and the International Law Unit. Purpose: substantive guidance, coordination and advice on assigned legal cases and activities across both Units. Frequency: as required, through regular interaction and review of ongoing work.

- Legal advisers and counterparts across the UN system: Purpose: professional exchange, coordination and exposure to legal practice across the UN system. Frequency: as required, through the legal advisers’ coordination mechanism.

- The Associate Legal Officer’s individual workplan will be based on the Department’s annual workplan and will define substantive activities and expected outputs. Progress will be monitored through regular discussions, review of assigned cases and deliverables, and ongoing feedback. The Associate Legal Officer will also participate in official meetings with the Director, as applicable and contribute to follow-up actions, ensuring practical exposure to the Agency’s legal mandate and the work of the Department.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Associate Legal Officer will report to the Director of Legal Affairs and work under their direct daily supervision, with full immersion in the Department’s daily work and activities. The role will have a cross-cutting focus, working closely with both the General Law Unit (covering international administrative law, commercial and institutional matters, and litigation), and the International Law Unit (covering privileges and immunities, protection, neutrality, international human rights mechanisms, and international humanitarian law). The JPO will handle a diverse portfolio of cases across both Units, participate in official meetings and related follow-up actions, gain a thorough understanding of the Agency’s legal mandate in a highly politicised context, and engage with legal advisers across the UN system.

Responsibilities (summary of duties/tasks):

1. Supports the Department’s Legal Advisory Work (30%)

• Participates in the daily work and activities of the General Law and International Law Units, gaining exposure to the full range of legal matters handled by the Department.

• Supports the Director of Legal Affairs in providing legal advice to UNRWA leadership and Directors of Divisions and Departments, including on sensitive and complex legal issues.

• Develops a comprehensive understanding of the Department’s legal functions, priorities and advisory responsibilities.

2. Manages an Assigned Portfolio of Legal Matters and Projects (30%)

• Handles an assigned portfolio of legal cases and issues across the General Law and International Law Units, under the direct supervision of the Director of Legal Affairs.

• Contributes to litigation and matters arising under the Agency’s internal justice system, the preparation and review of diplomatic correspondence, including notes verbal, and the provision of legal opinions on international law issues.

• Reviews commercial contracts and supports legal aspects of procurement and other operational activities.

• Undertakes designated legal projects to strengthen the Agency’s legal practices and frameworks, including the development of standard agreement templates for engagement with partners.

• Liaises with relevant Agency stakeholders, including Human Resources, Partnerships and the Executive Office, under the guidance and supervision of the Director of Legal Affairs.

3. Participates in Official Meetings and Follow-up Actions (25%)

• Participates in meetings led by the Director of Legal Affairs and other senior legal officers on substantive, operational and strategic legal matters.

• Contributes to meeting preparation and follow-up, including conducting legal research, drafting documentation and supporting the implementation of agreed actions.

• Develops an understanding of UNRWA’s management structures, decision-making processes and engagement with governments, beneficiaries, partners and other stakeholders.

5. Engages in Legal Coordination Across the United Nations System (15%)

• Participates, through the Director of Legal Affairs, in coordination and information-sharing with legal advisers and counterparts across the United Nations system.

• Gains exposure to the work of the United Nations Office of Legal Affairs and other UN legal offices, including inter-agency coordination mechanisms on legal matters.

• Develops an understanding of common legal issues, institutional practices and approaches to legal advice and coordination across the UN systems.

Competencies

Key competencies

- Excellent oral and written communication skills, including strong legal drafting and analytical skills.

- Ability to work effectively in an international and multicultural environment, maintaining confidentiality and discretion at all times.

- Legal Research and Analysis

- Negotiation and Problem-Solving

- Stakeholder Engagement

- Teamwork and Collaboration

- Planning and Organizing

- Analytical Skills

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Master degree or equivalent in law or a Bachelor’s degree in law plus a minimum of 2 years of paid and relevant working experience. Admission to practice at a national Bar.

- In exceptional cases candidates with a Bachelor’s degree plus a minimum of 4 years relevant working experience can be considered.

- Substantive parts of the candidates’ academic training (Bachelor and/or Master) must have taken place in a developing country that appears on the list of eligible countries. eligible-countries-DC-JPOs.pdf

Working experience:

- Minimum of 2 years relevant working experience after obtaining first university degree in the legal field, with an exposure to development and humanitarian activities of international organisations being an asset.

- Minimum of 4 years relevant working experience for candidates with a Bachelor’s degree.

- Specialisation in public international law and/or the law of international organisations is an asset.

- Experience in international administrative law and/or litigation is an asset.

- Work experience within the UN system should not exceed 1 year, including UNV, (paid) UN internship and UN consultancy.

- All paid work experience since obtaining Bachelor’s degree will/can be considered.

Languages:

jobs.title: Asistente de Planificación Territorial - Geográfico - NPSA5
jobs.description:
1.Enfoque por niveles (Tiered Approach) para el reclutamiento

- En línea con el compromiso de salvaguardar la capacidad y apoyar al personal que ya forma parte de la Organización, la mayoría de las vacantes de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV se publican utilizando un proceso de postulación por niveles, mediante el cual: Nivel 0 (Tier 0): Personal internacional (IP) de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV con contratos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos serán abolidos o cuyos contratos serán terminados o no renovados durante 2026. Nivel 1 (Tier 1): Otros funcionarios de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV con contratos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA). Nivel 2 (Tier 2): Personal de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV con contratos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares, así como Voluntarios de la ONU en las categorías de Expertos y Especialistas. Nivel 3 (Tier 3) o sin nivel indicado: Todos los demás tipos de contrato de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV y de otras agencias, así como candidatos externos. Por favor, tome nota del(los) nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si corresponde, y asegúrese de cumplir con los criterios de elegibilidad para postular.

2. Oficina/Unidad/Descripción del Proyecto

Desde 2023, el Ministerio de Vivienda y Urbanismo (MINVU) y el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) mantienen un acuerdo de colaboración orientado a fortalecer la planificación urbana y territorial sostenible, promoviendo ciudades más integradas, resilientes y equitativas, en concordancia con los desafíos de desarrollo de la Región Metropolitana.

En este contexto, la Secretaría Regional Ministerial de Vivienda y Urbanismo de la Región Metropolitana requiere la contratación de un(a) Asistente de Planificación Territorial, con énfasis en aspectos geográficos, para apoyar los procesos de actualización, modificación y seguimiento del Plan Regulador Metropolitano de Santiago (PRMS), instrumento estratégico que orienta el desarrollo urbano y territorial de la Región Metropolitana.

La persona contratada participará en la elaboración de análisis y diagnósticos territoriales, formulación y evaluación de propuestas de planificación territorial, definición de criterios territoriales, actualización de la planimetría del PRMS y análisis de tendencias urbanas, aportando antecedentes técnicos para la gestión del crecimiento urbano, la protección ambiental, la identificación de riesgos y la localización de infraestructura y equipamientos. Asimismo, colaborará en procesos de Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica (EAE), coordinación interinstitucional y participación ciudadana asociados a modificaciones de instrumentos de planificación territorial.

Su trabajo contribuirá a fortalecer las capacidades técnicas de la SEREMI Metropolitana para la toma de decisiones y la actualización de instrumentos de planificación territorial, proporcionando antecedentes técnicos, cartográficos y normativos que favorezcan un desarrollo urbano sostenible, equilibrado y coherente con las políticas públicas regionales.

3. Alcance del trabajo

El objetivo principal del cargo es contribuir al desarrollo y coordinación y apoyar técnicamente el proceso de formulación, modificación, actualización, seguimiento e implementación del Plan Regulador Metropolitano de Santiago (PRMS), mediante la aplicación de criterios de planificación urbana y territorial, análisis espacial y herramientas de Sistemas de Información Geográfica (SIG), contribuyendo al desarrollo urbano sostenible y al ordenamiento territorial de la región.

Entre las funciones y resultados esperados se encuentran:

A. Planificación territorial y actualización del PRMS

- Participar en la elaboración, actualización y modificación de la planimetría del Plan Regulador Metropolitano de Santiago.

- Desarrollar análisis territoriales para la definición de áreas urbanas, rurales, de extensión urbana, protección ambiental, riesgo y planificación estratégica.

- Apoyar la definición de criterios territoriales para la toma de decisiones institucionales

B. Análisis espacial, diagnóstico y cartografía territorial

- Realizar diagnósticos territoriales, utilizando herramientas SIG y bases de datos espaciales

- Elaborar cartografía temática, normativa y de diagnóstico requerida en las distintas etapas de actualización de la planimetría del PRMS.

- Analizar tendencias de crecimiento urbano, expansión urbana, densificación, movilidad, equipamientos y usos de suelo.

C. Gestión de información geográfica y monitoreo territorial

- Construir, administrar y actualizar bases de datos geográficas para la gestión del PRMS como instrumento de planificación territorial.

- Desarrollar indicadores territoriales y sistemas de monitoreo para la gestión del PRMS.

- Apoyar la gestión y actualización de información territorial estratégica regional.

D. Evaluación, coordinación e integración de antecedentes y apoyo a la gestión del conocimiento

- Participar en procesos de Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica (EAE) del IPT.

- Revisar antecedentes territoriales provenientes de municipios, organismos públicos y consultorías externas.

- Participar en procesos de participación ciudadana y coordinación intersectorial vinculados a la actualización de la planimetría del PRMS.

- Capacitar y asesorar técnicamente a equipos internos según se requiera.

El/la titular podrá desempeñar otras funciones dentro de su perfil profesional que se consideren necesarias para el adecuado funcionamiento del proyecto, de las áreas relacionadas a éste y sus articulaciones.

4. Acuerdo Institucional

La persona contratada se desempeñará en forma presencial en dependencias de la SEREMI Metropolitana de Vivienda y Urbanismo, ubicada en Avda. Libertador Bernardo O`Higgins 874, Santiago, Región Metropolitana, además de asistencias en terreno. Se desempeñará bajo la supervisión directa de la jefatura del Departamento de Desarrollo Urbano e infraestructura de dicha SEREMI. Por parte del PNUD, administrativamente corresponderá al Coordinador/a del proyecto la respectiva supervisión. Se considera una jornada laboral completa, de lunes a viernes, en horario homologable al establecido para los demás profesionales de la SEREMI.

5. Competencias

Competencias Esenciales

Lograr Resultados - NIVEL 1: Planea y monitorea su trabajo, poniendo atención a los detalles, realiza un trabajo de calidad y a tiempo.

Pensar Innovadoramente - NIVEL 1: Abierto(a) a nuevas ideas, conoce los riesgos, resuelve los problemas en forma pragmática, hace mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente - NIVEL 1: Abierto(a) de mente y curioso(a), comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad - NIVEL 1: Se adapta a los cambios, maneja la incertidumbre/ambigüedad constructivamente, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación NIVEL 1: Demuestra manejo y motivación, capaz de afrontar la adversidad calmadamente, seguro(a).

Participar y Asociarse - NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento frente a otros, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión - NIVEL 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, es consciente de los prejuicios, confronta la discriminación.

Competencias Transversales y Técnicas

Gestión institucional - Comunicación

Comunicar de manera clara, concisa, sin ambigüedades, tanto de manera verbal como escrita; adaptar mensajes y elegir métodos de comunicación según audiencia. Habilidad de gestionar comunicaciones interna y externamente, a través de redes sociales, medios, y otros canales apropiados.

Gestión institucional - Gestión de proyectos

Capacidad para planificar, organizar, priorizar y controlar recursos, procedimientos y protocolos para alcanzar objetivos específicos

Gestión de asociaciones - Gestión de relaciones

Capacidad para relacionarse con un amplio abanico de asociados públicos y privados, así como para crear, mantener y reforzar las relaciones, la confianza y la comprensión mutua.

Entorno digital- Análisis geoespacial

Competencia en técnicas que estudian entidades a partir de sus propiedades topológicas, geométricas o geográficas.

Agenda 2030: Prosperidad - Crecimiento inclusivo

Desarrollo urbano y diseño inclusivo

Agenda 2030: Prosperidad - Crecimiento inclusivo

Infraestructuras y activos comunitarios urbanos

Agenda 2030: Planeta - Reducción del riesgo de desastres y recuperación

Resiliencia urbana.

6. Calificaciones mínimas de un NPSA

Educación académica mínima requerida

- Educación secundaria completa es requerida.

- Título profesional universitario (Grado de licenciado(a)) en áreas de la Geografía o equivalente, se dará debida consideración, pero no es un requisito.

Años mínimos de experiencia laboral relevante

- Mínimo de 5 años (con educación secundaria) o 2 años (con licenciatura) de experiencia relevante.

- Se entenderá por experiencia relevante al conjunto de experiencia laboral que incluya: Experiencia en formulación, evaluación o gestión de Instrumentos de Planificación Territorial y en estudios territoriales vinculados a Planes Reguladores Intercomunales, Metropolitanos o Comunales. Experiencia en instituciones públicas, municipalidades, gobiernos regionales o consultoras especializadas en planificación urbana y territorial. Experiencia en elaboración de cartografía temática y análisis geoespacial aplicado a la planificación urbana y en coordinación de estudios territoriales y gestión de información geográfica.

Habilidades competencias requeridas

- Experiencia en el manejo de herramientas de trabajo remoto y colaborativo, tales como Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Google Docs, Google Drive y nubes de almacenamiento.

- Experiencia en el manejo de herramientas tradicionales Microsoft Office: Word, Excel, Power Point.

- Experiencia en capacitaciones relacionadas con el ejercicio del cargo, tales como: Urbanismo, Planificación Urbana, Ordenamiento Territorial, Planificación Territorial, Desarrollo Urbano, Sistemas de Información Geográfica, Geomática, Gestión Territorial, Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica.

Habilidades y competencias deseables

- Contar con título profesional en el área mencionada (geografía o equivalente) .

- Contar con postítulo o postgrado en materias asociadas al cargo.

- Experiencia en el manejo avanzado de ArcGIS Pro, QGIS y Microsoft Office.

- Experiencia en el manejo intermedio de AutoCAD, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, GeoServer.

- Experiencia con la perspectiva de género en sus ámbitos de acción.

Idiomas requeridos (a nivel laboral)

Fluidez en el idioma español es requerida

Certificados profesionales

Se exigirá a los/as postulantes acreditar mediante certificados u otros documentos similares, su experiencia laboral y/o el manejo de las herramientas señaladas.

7. Viajes:

Eventualmente se prevén viajes oficiales para este puesto, dentro de Chile.

8. Los siguientes documentos deben requerirse a los aplicantes:

- CV personal y P11, indicando los puestos anteriores y sus funciones, la duración (mes-año), los requisitos, así como los detalles de contacto (correo y número de teléfono) del (la) candidato(a), y al menos tres referencias laborales de supervisores previos. Las referencias pueden incluir también a los colegas.

- Una carta de presentación (máximo una página) indicando por qué la persona se considera idónea para la posición.

- Los gerentes pueden requerir cualquier otro material relevante de su experiencia como reportes, presentaciones, publicaciones, campañas u otros materiales.

Consideraciones en su postulación:

- Complete el formulario en línea; es requerido.

- Adjunte también CV en formato libre, como complemento.

- Incluya una carta de presentación (máximo una página) indicando por qué se considera idónea(o) para la posición.

- Identifique al menos tres referencias laborales de supervisores(as) anteriores. Las referencias pueden incluir también a los colegas.

- Por tratarse de una posición nacional, las personas extranjeras deben contar con las condiciones habilitantes para trabajar en el país (residencia, permiso) al momento de postular.

Importante

Esta posición en categoría NPSA está sujeta a reclutamiento local.

Vacante Tier 3, es decir, abierto a postulaciones internas y externas.

Igualdad de oportunidades

Como empleador que promueve la igualdad de oportunidades, el PNUD valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y culturas en las que operamos y, en ese sentido, alentamos a personas calificadas de todos los orígenes a postular a puestos dentro de la organización. El PNUD también está comprometido con la creación de un entorno laboral inclusivo, en el que todo el personal esté empoderado para contribuir a nuestra misión, sea valorado, pueda desarrollarse y beneficiarse de oportunidades de carrera abiertas a todos.

Acoso sexual, explotación y abuso de autoridad

El PNUD no tolera el acoso, el acoso sexual, la explotación, la discriminación ni el abuso de autoridad. Por lo tanto, todos los candidatos seleccionados se someten a verificaciones pertinentes y se espera que cumplan con los estándares y principios correspondientes.

Derecho a seleccionar a múltiples candidatos

Asimismo, podemos conservar las postulaciones y considerar a los candidatos que apliquen a este puesto para otras posiciones similares en el PNUD, al mismo nivel de grado y con requisitos de funciones, experiencia y formación similares.

Uso de IA por parte de los candidatos/as

jobs.title: Re-advertisement Project Coordinator GCF (N-PSA 10) (Open to Tier 1, 2 & 3 applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups, and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous references and background checks.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. The UNDP Multi-Country Office (MCO) current support to the Government of Mauritius in the energy sector includes several on-going and pipeline projects, which are in line with the Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement to reduce GHG emissions by 40% and increase the share of renewable energy to 60% in the national energy mix by 2030.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations build integrated, lasting solutions for people and the planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow @UNDP.

The UNDP Mauritius Country Office (CO) consists of two distinct units including the Environment Unit and Socio-Economic Development Unit with a diverse portfolio worth USD 65 M including the Green Climate Fund (GCF), Global Environment Facility (GEF), Adaptation Fund (AF), European Union (EU), Japan Supplementary Budget (JSB), E-Health Portfolio and TRAC projects. The Environment Unit manages a portfolio covering various focal areas such as Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation, Biodiversity, Sustainable Land Management, and Chemicals and Waste.

The unit will hire a project coordinator for the “Accelerating the Transformational Shift to a Low-Carbon Economy in the Republic of Mauritius” project which is implemented under National Implementation Modality (NIM).

The project is funded by GCF with implementation initiated in 2017. The objective is to overcome identified barriers to low carbon development and support the inclusive deployment of 25MW of PV system on the electrical grid. The implementing partner is the Ministry of Finance in collaboration with the Ministry of Energy and Public Utilities, the Central Electricity Board, the Outer Island Development Cooperation, and the Mauritius Renewable Energy Agency.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Coordinator (PC) will be locally recruited based on an open competitive process. His/ her responsibilities shall include:

- Overall management of the project, mobilization of all inputs, supervision of staff, consultants, and sub-contractors.

- Reporting to the Head of the Environment Unit and periodic reporting to the Project Steering Committee (PSC).

- Meeting government obligations under the project (NIM modality).

- Liaison with Government, UNDP, UN Agencies, NGOs, project partners, and donor agencies.

Summary of Key Functions

- Strategic project planning, coordination, and implementation,

- Management of the Project,

- Representation and Coordination,

- Management of communication flow,

- Partnership building and donor liaison.

Specific tasks and responsibilities:

- Ensures strategic project planning, coordination and implementation , focusing on achievement of the following results: Provides guidance and manages the overall implementation including planning, budgeting, implementation and monitoring, Ensures overall efficient coordination of programmes/projects including planning processes and timely delivery of results taking into consideration agreed-upon work plans with the UNDP country office and the participating ministries/organizations, Ensures identification and promotion of joint programming and planning opportunities Identifies and develops new programme and project opportunities, Supports capacity building of national counterparts, Oversees project implementation through close monitoring of results. Ensures effective application of RBM tools, management of scorecard targets and other benchmarks, Coordinates and follows through on decentralized local evaluations. Ensures full compliance with audit requirements and timely follow-up to audit recommendations. Promotes identification and synthesis of best practices and lessons learned for organizational sharing and learning.

- Responsible for effective project management focusing on achievement of the following results: Ensures smooth running of the project, builds an effective project team, promotes teamwork and an environment that is conducive to delivering results, Ensures full responsibility for the appropriate use and management of resources attributed to the project by tracking use of financial resources, ensuring the integrity of financial systems and consistent application of the Internal Control Framework and/or rules and regulations. Continually find ways to systematically identify and integrate efficiency gains and cost reductions in all operations. Approves contracts and ATLAS transactions under written delegated authority from the Resident Representative and/or Country Director. Has Atlas manager rights as delegated. Responsible for the management of the project staff, monitors their performance, completing performance assessments where necessary, Ensure timely and regular reporting, Build capacity of the project staff by identifying capacity needs and establishing training/learning programmes.

- Ensures effective management of the three components for proper implementation as per the funding proposal achieving the following: Contribute to preparation and revision of project work and financial plans, as required by UNDP, and support the operational and financial planning processes, Oversee and ensure timely submission of the Inception Report, Combined Project Implementation Review/Annual Project Report, Technical reports, quarterly financial reports, and other reports as may be required by UNDP, GCF and other oversight agencies, Contribute to the preparation and implementation of progress reports, and monitor all project activities, budgets and financial expenditures, Assist in the preparation of payments requests for operational expenses, salaries, insurances etc. as well as follow up on timely disbursements by UNDP CO, Maintain project correspondence and communication, Assist in logistical organization of meetings, training and workshops.

- Responsible for Representation and Coordination in the area focusing on achievement of the following results: Able to represent UNDP with UNCT and development partners if needed, Provides strong coordination support to national authorities and other organizations through the establishment of a wider consultation process, Ensures proper coordination and inputs to Interagency initiatives, Maintains collaboration and coordination with the other project managers to ensure programmatic integration and sharing of best practices.

- Promotes communication flow in the project focusing on achievement of the following results: Maximizes communication between the various portfolios and ensures that stakeholders (development partners, bilateral and multilateral donors, private sector, civil society, UN agencies and Government agencies) have one consistent UNDP counterpart, Ensures internal communication and coordination at project level and effective and proactive communication between relevant project units, Monitors the perception of the GCF project at the local level and suggest media activities that position the GCF project more strategically and effectively as a neutral broker for local development, Enhances local visibility for the project in development effectiveness, Ensures that local development results are effectively communicated in collaboration with Communication Office in the country office.

- Fosters partnership building and donor liaison focusing on achievement of the following results: Contributes to the development of the project Partnership and Resource Mobilization (PRM) strategy, including planning tools to implement the strategy, Identifies new partnerships and strengthens existing ones at the project level through innovative approaches to partnership development, Encourages ways of increasing project funding such as engaging in resource mobilization efforts in consultation with local counterparts and following up with donors on local opportunities.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Impact of Results

- The Project Coordinator is the UNDP senior representative in the project. The results of his/her work impact on the standing and reputation of UNDP in the country and with the Green Climate Fund. When requested by the Resident Representative or Country Director, the Project Coordinator represents UNDP in international and national forums, liaises with external clients and a broad range of constituencies and UNDP counterparts in the Government, local and international media, civil society as well as counterparts from other international organizations.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Coordinator will work under the general supervision of the Head of the Environment Unit (who may delegate a direct supervisory role) in the UNDP MCO for Mauritius and Seychelles and will collaborate closely with the Project Director for National Implementation Modality (NIM) Projects.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigating complex landscape, champion inter- agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management (Insert below standard sentence if the position has direct reports.)

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

People Management

• Show managerial courage

• Ability to demonstrate empathy and emotional intelligence

• Ability to motivate and direct

• Ability to build an enabling Workplace

• Ability to build capability

• Manage performance and ensure accountability

• Lead with Humility

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies (insert up to 7 competencies)

Thematic Area - Name - Definition

Business Management - Result Based Management - Ability to manage programmes and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results.

Business Management - Project Management - Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Business Management - Partnerships Management - Ability to build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Business Development - Knowledge Generation - Ability to research and turn into useful knowledge, relevant for context or responsive to a stated need

Business Direction Strategy - Strategic thinking - Ability to develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks and opportunities; linking the vision to reality on the ground, and creating tangible solutions

Ability to leverage learning from a variety of sources to anticipate and respond to future trends; to demonstrate foresight to model what future developments and possible ways forward look like for UNDP.

Partnership Management - Strategic Engagement - Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking - Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in engineering, Environmental Science, Business Administration or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Experience:

- Minimum of 5 years (master’s degree) or 7 years (Bachelor’s degree) of relevant working experience in the fields related to the assignment, at national is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

jobs.title: Project Analyst [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Energy and Environment Unit of UNDP Kazakhstan supports national efforts to advance a green, low-carbon and climate-resilient economy and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Its portfolio covers climate change mitigation and adaptation, renewable energy, energy efficiency and power system modernization, biodiversity conservation, sustainable agriculture and food systems, sustainable land and water management, waste management, disaster risk reduction and sustainable natural resource use.

Working with government institutions, the private sector, civil society, academia and international partners, the Unit provides policy advice, technical assistance and capacity development. It promotes green and sustainable finance, supports access to international environmental and climate funding, and helps develop investment opportunities and innovative financing instruments aligned with national development priorities. The Unit also strengthens institutional frameworks and supports the application of innovative and digital solutions, while integrating gender equality and inclusive development across its work.

Within this portfolio, the Government of Japan-funded project “The Project for Development of Sustainable Rare Metal and Rare Earth Minerals Value Chains through Environmental Measures” supports the sustainable development of Kazakhstan’s minerals sector. The project combines policy and analytical support, environmental monitoring and capacity development to promote environmentally responsible mineral value chains.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide Policy Advice

- Provide specialized knowledge and expertise in critical minerals, sustainable mineral value chains and natural resource governance within the context of the project;

- Analyze existing policies, frameworks and regulations governing the minerals sector at various levels to identify opportunities, gaps, and barriers for sustainable sector development;

- Assess the regulatory landscape to ensure alignment of mineral sector policies with national development priorities and relevant international environmental and sustainability standards;

- Support the development of policies, strategies and action plans for environmentally responsible mineral sector development, considering input from stakeholders and best practices;

- Establish mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of relevant sectoral policies, providing recommendations for improvements;

- Analyze financial mechanisms and funding opportunities for sustainable mineral value chains and related environmental measures, identifying potential sources of support;

- Advocate for the integration of environmental sustainability, responsible resource management and value chain development into relevant sectoral policies, plans, and programs;

- Support the strengthening of institutional arrangements and procedures for sustainable mineral resource governance in Kazakhstan.

Collaborate with relevant government, industry representatives, research organizations and other stakeholders to facilitate the implementation of sustainable mineral sector policies and practices;

- Engage with policymakers, government officials, the private sector, NGOs, and community leaders to build consensus and support environmentally responsible mineral sector development;

- Coordinate between various stakeholders involved in mineral sector policy development and implementation to ensure coherence and efficiency;

- Translate complex technical and policy concepts into accessible language and communicate the importance of sustainable mineral value chains and environmental responsibility to different audiences;

- Design and conduct capacity-building activities related to critical minerals, sector governance and environmental sustainability, enabling stakeholders to understand and contribute to effective policy development and implementation;

- Prepare technical reports, policy briefs, and communication materials to communicate policy analysis, progress, and recommendations.

Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the project.

- Organize training, workshops, and capacity building activities in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

- Participate in and ensure sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice on project related issues. Support establishment of knowledge platforms for the project, facilitate innovative mechanisms for dissemination of knowledge from the project, and develop knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area.

- Promote advocacy on development trends and opportunities to collaborate in coordination with the project partners, stakeholders, and UNDP communications staff.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Analyst reports to the Project Manager. The job holder will ensure to provide quality advice to Project manager and comply with appropriate UNDP policies and procedures.

Competencies

Core competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- Business Acumen Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization.

- Negotiation and Influence Reach a common understanding/agreement, persuade others, resolve points of difference through a dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Business Development

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP: As the UN lead agency on international development, UN Development Programme (UNDP) works in 170 countries and territories, including those fragile and experiencing crisis, to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. UNDP helps countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities, and to build resilience to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s work is concentrated in three focus areas: (1) sustainable development, (2) democratic governance and peace building, and (3) climate and disaster resilience.

UNDP’s Rule of Law, Security, and Human Rights Team: The UNDP’s Rule of Law, Security, and Human Rights (RoLSHR) Team is responsible for policy and practice development in the areas of the rule of law, justice, security, human rights, including business and human rights (BHR), through the implementation of the UNDP Global Programme on Strengthening the Rule of Law and Human Rights for Sustaining Peace and Fostering Development for 2022-2025. The Global Programme is guided by and aligned with the UNDP Strategic Plan for 2022-2025 and provides tailored, context-specific technical, financial, and strategic support to contexts across the development spectrum.

UNDP’s B+HR Initiative: The RoLSHR’s programmatic work on BHR is provided through the global initiative on B+HR currently implemented in 53 countries (and growing) in Africa, the Arab States, Asia and the Pacific, Europe and Central Asia, Latin America, and the Caribbean, focusing on supporting:

- Governments (across sectors): in upholding their duty to protect human rights from businesses’ abuses, including by strengthening and enforcing robust regulatory frameworks on BHR;

- Businesses (across industries): in embedding their responsibility to respect human rights throughout their operational policies and practices, including to carry out human rights due diligence across supply chains, through the B+HR Academy , which trains approximately 1,300 businesses per year;

- Civil society and other relevant stakeholders: in monitoring businesses’ human rights performance, advocating for advancing corporate respect for human rights, and providing ‘ routes to remedy ’ to people adversely affected by businesses.

The UNDP’s global initiative on B+HR is coordinated from the Geneva Office (Switzerland) and led by the Global Policy Adviser on BHR, which supports and guides Regional B+HR Focal Points. Regional Focal Points are the entry point for requests of guidance coming from B+HR Focal Points at the Country Office level.

The UNDP’s global initiative on B+HR is supported by the Governments of Japan, Netherlands, Sweden, and the EU, and is part of the UNDP Global Programme on Strengthening the Rule of Law and Human Rights for Sustaining Peace and Fostering Development for 2022-2025.

The Business and Human Rights Specialist will work under direct supervision of the Global Policy Adviser on BHR, and in close coordination with the Senior BHR Specialist. They will also work directly with Regional Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Focal Points and/or B+HR Focal Points and provide technical and capacity-strengthening support to B+HR Focal Points at the Country Office level, as needed.

Scope of Work

1. Provide technical and programmatic advisory support in implementing the existing activities of the UNDP’s global initiative on B+HR, including by:

- Advising and supporting the implementation of the global, regional, and Country Office-level donor-funded projects with particular emphasis on the ‘Finance Against Slavery and Trafficking’ initiative.

- Supporting the preparation of global events and seminars held in Geneva;

- Coordinating logistical and substantive elements of UNDP’s participation in the UN Annual Forum on BHR.

- Developing concept notes and contributing to the drafting of project proposals for the purpose of resource mobilization.

2. Provide technical support in scaling up global initiative on B+HR, including by:

- Coordinating the implementation of the resource mobilization strategy (e.g., providing thematic and regional/country-specific research, liaising and partnering with other UN Agencies for joint resource mobilization initiatives and other UNDP Teams for portfolio programming, drafting project concept notes and documents, developing workplans and activity-based budgets);

- Promoting and supporting the positioning of UNDP as a ‘practice setter’ on BHR (e.g., ensuring its global visibility, contributing to the work of the Human Rights Council, UN Working Group on Business and Human Rights and other UN Special Procedures, participating in global and regional multi-stakeholder platforms);

- Developing new thematic offers and internal strategies for way forward of the existing thematic programming;

3. Contribute to the UNDP’s knowledge generation on BHR, including by:

- Contributing to the development of knowledge products on human rights due diligence, EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive and other mandatory human rights due diligence legislation, modern slavery, Universal Periodic Review, etc.;

- Providing peer review of internal knowledge products and inputting into submissions for reports of the UN Working Group on Business and Human Rights and other UN Special Procedures, UN Agencies, UN Teams, multi-stakeholder platforms, etc.;

4. Support overall coordination of the work of the Global B+HR team, including by:

- Coordinating the implementation of the Team Work Plan and, in conjunction with the Project Associate, monitoring the team budget.

- Supporting Country Offices’ efforts in carrying out UNDP corporate private sector due diligence and supporting them in developing and implementing Development Service Agreements with business-partners at the country level.

- Consolidating contributions of the B+HR team to the Annual Report of the Global Program 5 (GP5) and on all submissions needed for GP5 Project Boards. Leading on ROAR reporting.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Business and Human Rights Specialist will work under direct supervision of the Global Policy Adviser on BHR, and in close coordination with other BHR Specialists in the team. They will also work directly with Regional Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Focal Points and/or B+HR Focal Points and provide technical and capacity-strengthening support to B+HR Focal Points at the Country Office level, as needed.

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3 : Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies :

- Business Direction & Strategy — Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

- Business Direction & Strategy — System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

- Business Development — Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

- Business Management — Partnership Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Business Management — Results Based Management: Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

- 2030 Agenda: Peace — Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights: Joint programming for justice and security (GFP)

- 2030 Agenda: Peace — Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights: Safeguarding human rights and protecting vulnerable groups

Required Skills and Experience Education:

- Advanced University Degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Law, Human Rights, Corporate Responsibility, International Relations, Political Science, Development, or relevant fields is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 5 years (with a master’s degree) or 7 years (with a bachelor’s degree) of relevant professional experience on human rights and/or BHR is required.

Required skills and competencies:

- At least 5 years of relevant professional experience with intergovernmental organizations.

- Previous experience in drafting project concept notes and documents and successful resource mobilization initiatives on human rights and/or BHR.

- Previous experience in global project management, including quality assurance, MNEL, partnerships, visibility, reporting, etc..

Desired additional skills and competencies:

- Experience using the application of the UNGPs to the financial sector.

- Experience with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs) .

- Previous experience working on human rights with UNDP and/or other UN Agencies.

- Previous experience in developing and implementing human rights-related services to the business sector.

jobs.description:

De acuerdo con el compromiso de salvaguardar capacidad y apoyar al personal actual de la Organizaciön, la mayoria de vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se han anunciado utilizando un proceso de aplicaciön por niveles (tiers) en donde:

• Nivel O: personal internacional del PNUD/UNCDFNNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos såran abolidos, o cuyos contratos serån rescindidos o no renovados durante el aio 2026.

• Nivel 2: personal del PNUD/UNCDFNNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Eespecialistas de las Naciones Unidas Skip to main content.

• Nivel 3 0 sin nivel indicado: todos los dernés tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y dernås candidatos externos.

Descripción de la Oficina/Proyecto:

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

Por más de 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional:

 Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental

 Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos

 Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos.

Dentro del Clúster de Igualdad e Inclusión Social, Económica y Ambiental, se brinda asistencia al Gobierno de Panamá en alineamiento con el Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible en Panamá 2026-2030 y el Plan Estratégico del PNUD 2026-2030, los cuales destacan la necesidad de fortalecer el capital humano, reducir las desigualdades y apoyar la innovación y el crecimiento sostenible.

El proyecto busca contribuir al desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible de Panamá al mejorar los niveles de cohesión social mediante la inclusión activa de niños, niñas y adolescentes en procesos colectivos de enseñanza musical. Su objetivo principal es cerrar brechas sociales y promover el sentido de pertenencia, confianza en las instituciones y participación ciudadana, especialmente en territorios marcados por la desigualdad y la exclusión.

Se basa en un modelo innovador de enseñanza colectiva de la música —a través de orquestas y coros infantiles y juveniles— que trasciende lo artístico y se convierte en una política pública transformadora que promueve ciudadanía, sentido de pertenencia, equidad de género y el respeto a la diversidad, al tiempo que ofrece nuevas oportunidades de vida para jóvenes en contextos de alta vulnerabilidad.

Alcance del trabajo:

Bajo la supervisión del Asociado/a de Proyecto, el/la Asociado/a de Coros realizará las actividades necesarias de apoyo a la coordinación académica y musical de la Red Nacional de Orquestas.

Las actividades específicas incluyen:

1. Apoyo a la Coordinación Académica y Musical:

• Apoyar en la implementación y actualización de los planes de estudio y formación coral establecidos por La RED.

• Colaborar en la organización y seguimiento de los repertorios secuenciales y repertorios compartidos de las agrupaciones corales.

• Brindar apoyo en el seguimiento de los procesos de formación de las agrupaciones y ensambles corales, de acuerdo con las directrices establecidas.

• Apoyar en la coordinación de metodologías de trabajo y actividades orientadas al fortalecimiento de los procesos musicales del programa coral.

2. Seguimiento y Monitoreo de Programas Corales:

• Dar seguimiento a los cronogramas de clases, ensayos, encuentros y demás actividades de las agrupaciones corales.

• Apoyar la ejecución de los procesos de monitoreo permanente de los programas corales a nivel nacional.

• Colaborar en la recopilación de información sobre el desarrollo de las actividades, avances, retos y resultados del programa.

• Contribuir a la documentación e identificación de lecciones aprendidas y buenas prácticas derivadas de la implementación de las actividades corales.

3. Apoyo Logístico y Operativo:

• Coordinar y dar seguimiento a los espacios, materiales y recursos requeridos para ensayos, encuentros, presentaciones y conciertos.

• Apoyar los procesos de identificación, inscripción y registro de participantes cuando sea requerido.

• Brindar apoyo logístico en la organización de actividades, eventos y presentaciones corales programadas por La RED.

4. Apoyo a Procesos de Evaluación y Selección:

• Participar en los procesos de audición, evaluación y promoción de integrantes de las agrupaciones corales cuando sea requerido.

• Colaborar en el seguimiento de los planes de formación, montaje de repertorios y desarrollo de actividades y etapas del programa coral.

5. Asistir en la Coordinación Institucional y Reportes, y apoyar la gestión de conocimiento:

• Elaborar y presentar informes periódicos sobre las actividades realizadas, avances, dificultades identificadas y recomendaciones de mejora.

• Participar en reuniones, capacitaciones, seminarios y actividades convocadas por La RED, MICULTURA, PNUD u otras instancias relacionadas con el programa.

• Mantener comunicación y coordinación permanente con el equipo técnico y administrativo para garantizar la adecuada ejecución de las actividades corales.

• Apoyar la generación y el intercambio de conocimientos, así como el desarrollo de capacidades, en relación con el proyecto.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

El/La Asociado/a de Coros trabajará bajo la supervisión directa de el/la Asociado/a de Proyecto.

Esta posición estará basada en la Sede del Ministerio de Cultura.

Movilidad: No se prevé desplazamiento a nivel nacional o en el extranjero. No obstante, en caso de ser necesario los gastos que impliquen movilización, hospedaje y alimentación, de acuerdo con las actividades y requerimientos serán cubiertos por el Proyecto.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates
