jobs.title: Project Manager – Integrated Electronic Case Management System (Open to all applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Job Purpose and Organizational Context

The SO-JUST Project is a seven-year social justice reform initiative funded by the Government of Canada and implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), in partnership with the Government of Jamaica and civil society partners. The project aims to use an equitable human rights and gender responsive approach, targeting systemic change within the processes of the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, its departments and agencies, the Courts, the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions and other state and non-state partners to improve social justice in Jamaica. The project aims to support the Government of Jamaica in increasing access to justice for vulnerable and disadvantaged groups and strengthening the capacity of the justice system to implement gender-responsive social justice policies and programmes. It reflects and integrates the four pillars of social justice, which are equity, access, participation, and rights, and adopts a gender-responsive approach. The SO-JUST Project is designed to enhance efficiencies and support transformation initiatives that will result in more equitable and accessible justice services. The project is currently in the fifth year of its seven-year implementation plan.

The Government of Jamaica, through the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (the Ministry), aims to enhance efficiency, transparency and accessibility levels in the island’s justice system. One critical component of this modernization initiative is the development and implementation of an Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS), which will digitize case handling, streamline processes, and provide accurate, real-time data across the justice sector. Currently, case management in courts rely heavily on manual processes, leading to delays, inefficiencies and a lack of transparency. The IECMS will be utilized by the courts and related justice sector institutions, including but not limited to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, the Jamaica Constabulary Force, Department of Correctional Services and the private bar, creating an interconnected and cohesive system that facilitates case tracking and management at all stages of the criminal and civil justice process.

The UNDP therefore requires a qualified project manager – assigned to the SO-JUST project – to provide support to the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (“the Ministry”) by coordinating the timely and effective implementation of GOJ requirements for the successful completion of the IECMS.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager will be responsible for working closely with the International Consulting Firm (ICF) engaged to design, develop and implement the IECMS and oversee the end-to-end planning, design, and execution of the project to implement the IECMS in Jamaica's justice sector. The Project Manager will work closely with the Project Steering Committee, to ensure that the project is delivered on time, within scope, and within budget while meeting the quality standards and expectations of key stakeholders.

The Project Manager will lead the project from initiation to closure, ensuring that the IECMS is effectively integrated and functional across the targeted sections of the justice sector. Key responsibilities are outlined below:

- Project Planning and Coordination Develop a Comprehensive Project Plan and Schedule, that clearly articulates the approach to be used to efficiently and effectively manage the project’s scope, timelines, cost, stakeholders, quality assurance and risk. Define project scope, goals, and deliverables in collaboration with the Project Steering Committee (PSC). Develop technical documents required for successful project implementation, to include TORs for the engagement of technical experts. Coordinate the recruitment of any technical experts or other support persons, and manage the implementation of the associated terms and activities for the duration of the contract period. Manage the completion of all contracts, Memoranda of Understanding and Agreements related to all Consultants, Specialists and project subcontractors engaged to the project. Manage the processes to acquire all permits, approvals, or licenses from the various government authorities, including entry permits for the Consultant’s equipment, as well as all other permits, approvals, or licenses that are not the responsibility of the Consultant for the performance of the Contract. Manage the timely coordination and provision of all resources, information, and decision making on behalf of the Ministry and other justice sector partners within the time specified in the Implementation Schedule. Be responsible for facilitating access, using previously established protocols, to the requisite project sites and to all other areas reasonably required for the proper execution of the project. Coordinate with external vendors, software developers, and other technical teams involved in the development and deployment of the IECMS to ensure timely completion and maintenance of prescribed service delivery standards. Coordinate compliance with all legal, regulatory, and data security requirements governing the roll-out of the IECMS in Jamaica.

- Stakeholder Management Engage and manage relationships with all project and other key stakeholders, including the Ministry, the Judiciary, the Court Administration Division, the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, Office of the Information Commissioner, law enforcement agencies, other justice service providers and external partners. Facilitate regular and inclusive communication and updates with stakeholders to ensure alignment with project objectives and address emerging concerns. Organize workshops, training, and awareness sessions for justice sector personnel and end-users on the IECMS functionality and benefits.

- System Design and Integration Collaborate with technical teams to ensure that the IECMS is appropriately designed to integrate with existing systems used in the justice sector. Coordinate the timely provision of all resources, facilitating access, and information necessary for the Installation and Acceptance Test of the IECMS, as identified in the agreed and finalized Inception Report (except where provision of such items is explicitly identified as being the responsibility of the ICF), being mindful of the effect of any delay on the timeliness of the Acceptance Test. Acting on behalf of the Ministry and its stakeholders, assume the primary responsibility for the timely and effective implementation of the Acceptance Test(s) for the IECMS, including the continued operation of the IECMS after the Acceptance Test, until otherwise directed by the Project Steering Committee.

- Budgeting and Financial Management Develop and manage the project budget, ensuring that resources are allocated efficiently and that expenditures are within approved limits. Provide Monthly Financial Reports and forecasts to the Ministry in accordance with agreed timelines. Acting on behalf of the Ministry and its stakeholders, inspect or test any components of the System, as specified in the ICF Work Plan and prepare budgets for expenses not limited to inspection agent fees, travel and related expenses.

- Risk Management Identify potential project risks and develop mitigation strategies to address them. Implement systems and procedures for ensuring the safe storage, timely and regular backup of all data and software in accordance with accepted data management principles (except where such responsibility is clearly assigned to the IECMS developers/ ICF). Manage all confidential information received from the ICF or justice sector stakeholders and ensure that the confidential information is not used for any other purpose other than operation, maintenance and further development or reengineering of the IECMS.

- Monitoring and Reporting Develop key performance indicators (KPIs) and monitor project progress against these metrics. Prepare and submit regular Monthly Progress Reports to the Ministry, Project Steering Committee, and other stakeholders. Reports should provide updates on activities, bottlenecks, changes to risks, mitigation strategies, as well as progress in implementing or achieving KPIs (as appropriate). Ensure that any deviations from the project plan are identified early, and approval sought from the Project Steering Committee for the implementation of timely corrective measures. Review and approve documents furnished by the Consultant and ensure that there is no departure from any approved document.

- Knowledge management, Training and Change Management Coordinate training programmes for justice sector staff to ensure smooth transition to the new system. Oversee the execution of the change management process to ensure user adoption and reduce resistance to the new IECMS. Oversee the development of user manuals and training guides by the Consultant to ensure that all personnel are fully competent in using the IECMS. Coordinate with justice sector stakeholders to ensure that each organization or department designates appropriate staff for the training courses and also make appropriate logistical arrangements for trainings.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Manager will report directly to the UNDP Jamaica Programme Specialist, working closely with the SO-JUST Project Management Unit, and the Ministry of Justice Focal Point. Approval of any work product produced by the Project Manager will be contingent on feedback from the above-mentioned stakeholders, and receipt of a certification of approval from the Permanent Secretary of the MOJCA (or designate).

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Engage and Partner LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

- Business Management Project Management: Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

- Business Management Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts, and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Business Management Monitoring and Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

- Partnership management Resource Mobilization: Ability to identify funding sources, match funding needs (programmes/projects/initiatives) with funding opportunities and establish a plan to meet funding requirements.

- Business Direction & Strategy System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master´s degree or equivalent) in Business Administration , Information Technology , Computer Science , or a related field is required, or

- University degree (bachelor´s degree) in Business Administration , Information Technology , Computer Science , or a related field in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 2 years of experience (with a master’s degree) or 4 years (with a bachelor’s degree) of experience in managing large scale IT projects, preferably within the public sector or justice system.

Required experience, knowledge and skills:

• Proven experience managing the development and deployment of case management systems or similar solutions.

• Experience implementing technology-driven changes in large organizations or multi-agency contexts.

• Experience in managing projects in a high-security environment with multiple stakeholders, vendors, and contractors.

Desired skills:

- Past experience working with judicial workflows and justice system operations, the legal framework and processes.

- Previous experience working with Governments, UN System or similar organisations.

Required Language(s) (at working level):

Fluency in English is required.

Professional Certificates:

Professional certification in project management (e.g., PMP, PRINCE2) is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Climate Policy Analyst [Open to Internal & External Applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, an organization advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. UNDP is on the ground in about 170 countries and territories, working with national counterparts on solutions to global and national development challenges.

In the programme countries, UNDP supports stabilization, state-building, governance and development priorities in partnership with the host governments, the United Nations system, the development partners and other partners to help the countries to achieve sustainable development by eradicating poverty in all its forms and dimensions, accelerating structural transformations for sustainable development and building resilience to crises and shock.

UNDP has been a trusted development partner of Thailand for more than 50 years, helping to reduce inequalities and exclusion in areas such governance, environment protection, climate change mitigation and adaptation. In each of its thematic areas of work, UNDP at the request of its national partners provides relevant policy advisory support, technical assistance, advocacy, and knowledge to help Thailand achieve its global commitment on Sustainable Development Goals (SDG).

UNDP is currently looking for a Climate Policy Analyst with a background in climate change policy, sustainable energy, climate adaptation and/or mitigation. The incumbent will provide research, policy analysis, project coordination, monitoring and implementation support for selected initiatives under the Climate Action Portfolio. The position requires strong analytical, communication, coordination and organizational skills, as well as the ability to work across interconnected climate and development issues.

In this context, under the direct supervision and strategic guidance of the Climate and Small Grants Programme Portfolio Manager, the Climate Policy Analyst will work cooperatively within an integrated programme comprising analysts and professionals from programme, operations, policy and project teams. The incumbent will provide technical and coordination support and collaborate with relevant project managers and team members in implementing, monitoring and reporting on assigned climate-related initiatives.

Background and scope of the climate action portfolio

Among several ongoing and pipeline climate-related activities, UNDP is working on topics related to: support to the implementation and reporting of climate policies (e.g. Nationally Determined Contribution, Long Term Low Emission Development Strategy, Biennial Transparency Report), climate finance, climate change adaptation and climate resilience for agriculture and water management, just energy transition/emission reduction, climate education, and others. The elements of human rights, gender, youth, minority groups, and most vulnerable communities are incorporated as core cross-cutting issues in all the initiatives.

In this context, UNDP in Thailand is looking for a Climate Policy Analyst who will perform under the direct supervision and strategic guidance of the Climate and Small Grants Programme Portfolio Manager. They would work cooperatively within an integrated programme, comprising analysts and professionals (operations, policy advisors, project and programme team).

Duties and Responsibilities

The Climate Policy Analyst will be based in Bangkok as part of the UNDP Thailand country office and will report to the Climate and Small Grants Programme Portfolio Manager. The Climate Policy Analyst will work in coordination with the other project managers in UNDP Thailand.

The Climate Policy Analyst will provide technical, analytical, coordination, monitoring and implementation support for assigned projects and initiatives under UNDP Thailand’s Climate Action Portfolio. The incumbent will undertake policy research and analysis, coordinate with implementing partners and stakeholders, monitor project progress and risks, contribute to reporting and knowledge products, and support the development of climate-related initiatives. The Climate Policy Analyst will perform these responsibilities in close collaboration with relevant programme, project and operations colleagues, in accordance with UNDP policies and procedures.

1. Support implementation and coordination of assigned climate-action projects

- Provide day-to-day coordination and implementation support for assigned activities under selected projects within the Climate Action Portfolio. The selection of the suite of projects will be guided by the Country Programme Document and existing pipeline of projects in a given year;

- Coordinate with implementing partners, responsible parties, consultants and relevant UNDP teams to support the timely delivery of agreed outputs;

- Support compliance with applicable UNDP and government procedures, including procurement, human resources, financial management and project implementation requirements, including in the UNDP’s internal EPR system (Quantum);

- Monitor the implementation of assigned activities against approved workplans, timelines and budgets, and bring potential delays or implementation issues to the attention of the supervisor;

- Prepare and follow up on requests for financial resources, including advances, direct payments, reimbursements and FACE forms, under the guidance of the supervisor and in coordination with the relevant operations team;

- Maintain project files, implementation records and supporting documentation in accordance with UNDP requirements;

- Support results-based implementation and coordination of project activities; and

2. Support project monitoring, reporting and risk tracking

- Monitor the implementation of assigned project activities and compile information on progress against agreed results, indicators, workplans and budgets;

- Support the review of programme results and the collection and verification of data and evidence used to demonstrate progress;

- Monitor project risks and issues, maintain the Project Risk Log and Issues Log, and bring emerging risks or proposed mitigation measures to the attention of the supervisor for review and possible escalation;

- Support the documentation and follow-up of project changes, issues and management decisions;

- Draft project progress reports covering implementation progress, results, risks, issues and expenditure for review and clearance by the supervisor;

- Support the timely preparation of quarterly financial and activity reports and follow up with relevant partners to obtain required information and supporting documentation;

- Contribute to the preparation of reports to donors, government counterparts and other stakeholders, ensuring the completeness and accuracy of assigned inputs; and

- Prepare briefing notes, presentations, talking points and background materials for meetings with government, development partners and other stakeholders.

3. Support stakeholder coordination and development of climate-related initiatives

- Support coordination with government agencies, development partners, civil society, the private sector, academia and local stakeholders for the implementation of assigned portfolio activities;

- Maintain regular working-level communication with partners and stakeholders and support the organization of consultations, technical meetings, workshops and other project activities;

- Contribute research, background analysis and technical inputs to concept notes, project proposals and resource-mobilization materials under the guidance of the Climate Action Portfolio Manager;

- Support the technical development of project proposals on just energy transition, climate mitigation, adaptation and related topics, including the proposed submission to the Mitigation Action Facility;

- Coordinate with other UNDP Thailand teams to identify operational and programmatic linkages and promote coherence across related projects and thematic areas;

- Support collaboration with other UN agencies on relevant joint activities, including initiatives addressing the needs of women, children, youth, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups; and

- Monitor and compile information on relevant policy developments, stakeholders and partnership opportunities and provide regular updates to the supervisor and project teams.

4. Support policy research, knowledge management and communication

- Conduct research and policy analysis on climate mitigation, adaptation, just energy transition, climate finance and other assigned topics;

- Prepare technical inputs, policy briefs, background notes, analytical papers and other knowledge products for review by the supervisor and contribute the CO’s overall pipeline development effort;

- Support the provision of technical inputs to UNDP Thailand, implementing partners and other stakeholders within the incumbent’s areas of expertise;

- Identify, document and synthesize good practices, lessons learned and evidence generated through project implementation;

- Contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice and support the dissemination of relevant knowledge products;

- Support the design and delivery of learning and capacity-development activities for government counterparts, implementing partners and other stakeholders; and

- Contribute to the implementation and periodic updating of the Climate Action Portfolio’s communication and knowledge-management activities.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction and Strategy

- Effective Decision Making: Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner inline with one's authority, area of expertise and resources and take into consideration potential wider implications.

Business Development

- Knowledge Facilitation: Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

Business Management

- Project Management: Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Monitoring & Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Partnership Management

- Strategic Engagement: Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives.

- Emerging Partnerships: Ability to engage with emerging partners, develop and manage a strategy and develop approaches to developing and managing these new strategic partnerships.

- Resource Mobilization: Ability to identify funding sources, match funding needs (programmes/projects/initiatives) with funding opportunities, and establish a plan to meet funding requirements.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Climate Change, Environmental Sciences/Engineering, Energy Engineering, Disaster Management, Environmental Economics/Management, International Relations, Political Science and/or relevant field is required, OR:

- A first level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.;

- Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience in programme and project implementation, related to the area described above;

- Experience in project management including coordination, policy analysis and partnership management;

- Experience in working effectively with diverse groups of professionals towards common goals;

- Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and advance knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired Additional Skills:

- Experience making new and useful ideas work, including the adaptation with complex concepts and challenges convention purposefully;

- Experience in policy analysis and development on just energy transition or climate resilience (or related fields);

- Research experience on just energy transition or climate resilience (or related fields);

- Experience and knowledge of the country’s institutional framework and policies of climate change;

- Experience with working with/in the UN Agencies is an asset

- Previous experience working with government, donors or the UN.

Required Language(s):

- Fluency in English and Thai is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.
